post_text: Marketing has always been an essential part of any business house, including healthcare. Healthcare ( Hospitals , Retails , Diagnostics , Labs etc. ) marketing has evolved significantly in the past decade, with new and innovative trends emerging. In today's digital age, healthcare providers , we must adapt to these trends to reach and engage with the patients more effectively. Recent trends: Videos - A/V is very important .Video content have become very popular now a days and are very effective for healthcare providers to connect with their patients. 80% to 90% of internet users watch video content on their personal devices. Moreover, 54% of consumers want to see more video content from the brands or businesses they support. The healthcare industry should take a notice of this trend, and video marketing is a crucial part of healthcare marketing strategies. Furthermore, video marketing is very highly effective in generating qualified leads. Video marketing has several benefits, including increased engagement, improved SEO, and better patient education. Here are some lucrative video marketing statistics for businesses.• 84% of internet users have watched video content on their personal devices.• 57% of consumers want to see more video content from the brand or business they support.• 90% of video marketers are happy with their ROI.• Video marketers receive 60% more qualified leads every year than non-users. Generate New Reviews for Locations & Providers Your online reputation can make or break your practice. According to Our Doctoral Survey's , the following insights are true:• 80% of people read reviews of local businesses before engaging.• 85% of patients read reviews before booking appointments with practices.• People typically read an average of 10 to 15 reviews before they feel ready to trust a local business.• 57% of people will never work with a local business that has less than 4 stars on Google, Facebook.• 91% of 18-34-year-olds trust online reviews as much as word-of-mouth recommendations. Generating reviews for your locations and providers is extremely important to your status as a credible practice. The most effective way of generating new reviews for your healthcare practice can be by simply asking your patients and their families to leave honest reviews on Google, Facebook, or Yelp. The more reviews you receive, the more prospective patients will be able to trust you. We always recommend leveraging review generation software to make adoption and adding to your existing workflows that much easier. Leverage On-Page SEO to Increase Organic Traffic Search engine optimization (SEO) is the very critical component of healthcare marketing. SEO makes your website more visible and rank higher in search engine results pages (SERPs). On-page SEO is a subset of SEO that focuses on optimizing individual web pages. On-page SEO factors that matter the most in healthcare marketing include metadata, images, keywords, and value. Properly embedding keywords throughout your website, optimizing your images, and providing valuable content like an FAQ section will improve a website's overall SEO ranking. Promote the Healthcare Practice Via Guest Posts & INfluencers Content marketing is a proven method of establishing your business as an authority and growing an organic search traffic. This is also true for healthcare organizations. Publishing a guest post or column on an authoritative website or featuring on a popular medical podcast can help spread your expertise online. A feature on a popular medical podcast or Influencer is an effective way of reaching a broad audience, especially since 32% of the population in the globally listen to a podcast every month. Another major benefit of guest posting and podcasting is gaining a high-quality backlink, which can help improve your website's domain authority. Focus on Patient Experience In recent years, the focus of healthcare marketing has shifted from attracting new patients to retaining existing ones. Patients are spoilt for more choices than ever before, and they expect high-quality care and an exceptional patient experience. Medical practices need to provide a patient-centered approach to care, which means putting the patient’s needs and preferences first. By focusing on the patient experience, practices can increase patient satisfaction and loyalty, which can lead to positive word-of-mouth referrals and increased revenue. Practices can improve the patient experience by providing easy-to-use patient portals, online scheduling, and personalized communication with patients through email and social media.

After three and a half years of having the privilege of working in the Private Secretary's Office in The Queen's Household, last week I rejoined the Civil Service and moved to the Home Office.

My time in the Royal Household was amongst the most interesting and challenging of my career and it was a genuine honour to have been able to support The Queen. To all my many former colleagues, thank you for making my brief time with you all the more memorable, and to those partners I worked alongside, thank you for your support.

And now, onto new challenges!

post_text: 👷 En el marco de los trabajos de control y evaluación estructural de la obra Variante de Zafra (Badajoz) , se han llevado a cabo ensayos de deflexiones con el objeto de determinar los módulos de deformación del firme construido. Esta técnica, ampliamente reconocida en ingeniería de carreteras, permite caracterizar el comportamiento mecánico del pavimento y comprobar que las mismas cumplen los estándares técnicos marcados en el Pliego de Prescripciones Técnicos del proyecto. 🔍 ¿En qué consiste el ensayo? El ensayo se ha realizado mediante nuestro deflectómetro de impacto Dynatest FWD 8002, que aplica una carga sobre el firme y mide la respuesta vertical del pavimento en distintos puntos. A partir del deflectograma obtenido, se calculan los módulos de elasticidad de las distintas capas del firme, lo que permite evaluar su capacidad estructural. 📐 Aplicación en la Variante de Zafra En esta actuación, los datos obtenidos han sido fundamentales para: ✅ Identificar tramos homogéneos de comportamiento estructural. ✅ Detectar zonas con deflexiones anómalas que indicarían una mala ejecución de la obra y por tanto comprometer la durabilidad de la misma. 🧠 Valor añadido Gracias a este estudio, Construcciones Sevilla Nevado S.A. refuerza su compromiso con la calidad y la sostenibilidad, aplicando soluciones basadas en datos reales y técnicas avanzadas de diagnóstico. La correcta interpretación de las deflexiones permite no solo mejorar la seguridad vial, sino también optimizar los recursos en obra. #GestiónDeCarreteras #Infraestructura #MovilidadSostenible #GestionVial #IngenieríaCivil #Transporte #SeguridadVial #DesarrolloSostenible #InnovaciónEnIngeniería #AuscultaciónDeInfraestructuras #TecnologíaAvanzada #SeguridadEnObras #GyA #Deflexiones #IndiceRegularidadInternacional #Retroreflexion #Georradar #CoeficienteRozamiento #IndiceBoeing

En el segundo, la presión se transmite al área completa del cerramiento, produciendo efectos más significativos sobre el marco resistente. 📐 Para la representación ingenieril de estas condiciones, los programas de análisis estructural juegan un papel fundamental. 👷 En el marco de los trabajos de control y evaluación estructural de la obra Variante de Zafra (Badajoz) , se han llevado a cabo ensayos de deflexiones con el objeto de determinar los módulos de deformación del firme construido. Esta técnica, ampliamente reconocida en ingeniería de carreteras, permite caracterizar el comportamiento mecánico del pavimento y comprobar que las mismas cumplen los estándares técnicos marcados en el Pliego de Prescripciones Técnicos del proyecto.

🔍 ¿En qué consiste el ensayo?

El ensayo se ha realizado mediante nuestro deflectómetro de impacto Dynatest FWD 8002, que aplica una carga sobre el firme y mide la respuesta vertical del pavimento en distintos puntos. A partir del deflectograma obtenido, se calculan los módulos de elasticidad de las distintas capas del firme, lo que permite evaluar su capacidad estructural.

📐 Aplicación en la Variante de Zafra

En esta actuación, los datos obtenidos han sido fundamentales para:

✅ Identificar tramos homogéneos de comportamiento estructural.
✅ Detectar zonas con deflexiones anómalas que indicarían una mala ejecución de la obra y por tanto comprometer la durabilidad de la misma.

🧠 Valor añadido

Gracias a este estudio, Construcciones Sevilla Nevado S.A. refuerza su compromiso con la calidad y la sostenibilidad, aplicando soluciones basadas en datos reales y técnicas avanzadas de diagnóstico. La correcta interpretación de las deflexiones permite no solo mejorar la seguridad vial, sino también optimizar los recursos en obra.

🚗 Radical Innovation in Chassis Technologies: The Future of Braking, Steering and Suspension

The automotive industry is entering a new era of chassis innovation. From brake-by-wire and electromechanical braking (EMB) to steer-by-wire, rear steering, active dampers, and air suspension systems, next-generation technologies are redefining vehicle dynamics, safety, and driving experience.

Join me on June 19 at 10:00 AM CET for an in-depth discussion on the latest developments shaping the future of braking, steering, and suspension systems.

During the webinar, we will explore:
✅ How by-wire technologies are transforming braking, steering, and suspension systems
✅ Which OEM and regional strategies are accelerating the adoption of next-generation chassis technologies
✅ How the competitive landscape is evolving across established suppliers and emerging innovators
We will also review OEM adoption trends, regional developments, emerging technology strategies, and the evolving supplier ecosystem across advanced chassis systems.
Looking forward to sharing insights and discussing the future of vehicle chassis technologies with you.

⚠️ "When math and literacy goals compete—both lose."

@YvetteLehman on how to align school priorities without overwhelming teachers:

📚 The Naked Truth About School Improvement Silos:
→ Math vs. literacy goals = divided resources + teacher burnout
→ District priorities should connect, not compete (e.g., reasoning in math = critical thinking in literacy)
→ Every school goal should ladder up to a district "why"

🔄 Why This Matters Now:

Ontario’s structured literacy push shows how district-wide focus creates momentum

Isolated school goals lead to initiative overload

Coherence > compliance

🎯 3 Steps to Create Coherent Goals:
1️⃣ The "Through-Line" Test → Can you trace your school goal directly to a district priority?
2️⃣ The "Integration" Opportunity → Look for natural overlaps (e.g., "evidence-based reasoning" in both subjects)
3️⃣ The "Resource Alignment" Check → Are your math/literacy coaches collaborating or competing?

💡 "The best school goals don't add more—they connect what's already there."

If your team isn’t coming up with new ideas, maybe it’s because you’re shooting them down.

Here’s how you unknowingly suffocate your team’s creativity:

1. Defaulting to “We’ve always done it this way” :
   
-When you cling to old methods, you’re not safeguarding tradition—you’re blocking innovation.
   
-Just because it worked before doesn’t mean it’s the right path now. 
   
-Creativity thrives when the old rules are questioned, not worshipped.
   
2. Punishing risk:
   
-If every bold idea is met with a lecture, your team learns to play it safe.
   
-Playing it safe leads to mediocrity. 
   
-Failure isn’t fatal; it’s the cost of admission for breakthrough ideas. 
   
-Show your team that risks are celebrated, not punished.
   
3. Failing to reward creativity:
   
-If new ideas aren’t celebrated, they’ll stop coming altogether. 

-Your team needs to know their creativity has impact and value.
   
-Recognition doesn’t have to be grand—just consistent.
   
Creativity thrives in environments where failure is a stepping stone, not a guillotine. 

The best founders build teams that dare to think bigger—because they’re allowed to.

If your team isn’t coming up with new ideas, maybe it’s because you’re shooting them down.

Here’s how you unknowingly suffocate your team’s creativity:

1. Defaulting to “We’ve always done it this way” :
   
-When you cling to old methods, you’re not safeguarding tradition—you’re blocking innovation.
   
-Just because it worked before doesn’t mean it’s the right path now. 
   
-Creativity thrives when the old rules are questioned, not worshipped.
   
2. Punishing risk:
   
-If every bold idea is met with a lecture, your team learns to play it safe.
   
-Playing it safe leads to mediocrity. 
   
-Failure isn’t fatal; it’s the cost of admission for breakthrough ideas. 
   
-Show your team that risks are celebrated, not punished.
   
3. Failing to reward creativity:
   
-If new ideas aren’t celebrated, they’ll stop coming altogether.

-Your team needs to know their creativity has impact and value.
   
-Recognition doesn’t have to be grand—just consistent.
  
Creativity thrives in environments where failure is a stepping stone, not a guillotine.

The best founders build teams that dare to think bigger—because they’re allowed to.

post_text: Ma; the best deliverable by the Divine. We have been told stories that God could not be everywhere, so he made a ‘Mother’. Statements like “Mothers have eyes behind their heads'' are only proof of the same. It is the sixth sense that comes in handy, empowering a mother to be intuitive and guard her offsprings. This also makes her over protective but she realises that she needs to learn and let-go. It is all about balance. She is selfless, the definition of unconditional love, always thinking of others before ‘herself’. Never to turn a blind eye to the helpless, weaker sections of society.. She stands tall, ready to protect her offspring against anything that might befall them.. Adding the prefix and suffix ‘ma’ to Kali ma, Saraswati maa, Laxmi ma, Parvati maa, Durga maa and above all else, Bharat ma further cements a mother’s connection to the divine. Why else do we add ‘ma’ to all that is nurturing and caring? It would be only right to mention the services Mother Teresa so altruistically rendered through her care for the sick centres across the world. Role of mother, daughter, sister - how does she juggle all. Not just the human race, the role of a mother extends to the animal kingdom too. The way a tigress or a lioness protects her cubs is legendary! Stories around the ‘Aves’ species protecting their eggs are equally popular. A mother’s uniqueness lies in her inherently selfless nature. The way a mother nurtures her babies is truly exemplary. It is for this very reason that most children’s first word is ‘maa’. The expression on mother Mary’s face while she cradles her little one is magical. Corporations and advertisers have used it to their full advantage, truly saluting the ‘other’ through campaigns like Ariel’s “Share the Load”, which covers ‘womanhood’ and the unfair difference between men and women.. So let us all take this day to salute all the mothers and respect this divinity in ‘Human’ form.

post_text: Headline: Canadian Exporters: Are You Prepared for the "U.S. Tariff Trap"? Navigating the U.S. market has become increasingly complex, with Canadian exporters often absorbing unnecessary duties that erode margins. At yesterday's CUSMA Compliance Workshop in Niagara, trade experts—including Jim Trubits (Mohawk Global), Luis Romero, MBA (BDC), Susan Dafoe, CCS (Cole International), and Jon P. Yormick (Yormick Law)—provided a roadmap for businesses to protect their U.S. market access. Key insights for businesses involved in cross-border goods transportation from my participation in this workshop: • Documentation is Your First Line of Defense: Experts emphasize that "the party with the best documentation always wins." To survive an audit, you must maintain a clear audit trail that includes verified supplier certifications, costed bills of materials, and written origin analyses. • Qualification is Not Automatic: A common misconception is that qualification is based solely on regional value percentages. In reality, CUSMA eligibility is strictly tied to HS classification and specific rules such as "tariff shifts" or "regional value content." • Increased Scrutiny & Enforcement: U.S. customs authorities have become more aggressive due to revenue collection pressures. Verifications are no longer rare and are often triggered by something as simple as a refund request or a missing CUSMA claim at entry. • Internal Alignment is Key: Compliance often goes "off the rails" when procurement teams change suppliers without consulting compliance teams. A single sourcing change can unintentionally cause a product to lose its CUSMA eligibility. • Manage Risk Through Contracts: Exporters should treat their terms and conditions as an insurance policy. Include indemnification clauses that hold suppliers accountable if they provide incorrect origin information that results in penalties or duties. • Know When NOT to Claim: If a product already enters the U.S. duty-free, claiming CUSMA may provide no financial benefit while unnecessarily increasing your risk of a customs audit. Immediate Action Steps: 1. Review your supplier certifications and audit trails. 2. Confirm your tariff classifications (HS codes) are up-to-date—remember, the U.S. often requires ten digits for statistical reasons. 3. Audit your internal processes to ensure procurement, sales, and compliance are aligned. CUSMA compliance is a process, not just a form. By doing the work upfront, you can turn a potential verification into a manageable, short-lived event. Headline: Canadian Exporters: Are You Prepared for the "U.S. Tariff Trap"?

Navigating the U.S. market has become increasingly complex, with Canadian exporters often absorbing unnecessary duties that erode margins. At yesterday's CUSMA Compliance Workshop in Niagara, trade experts—including Jim Trubits (Mohawk Global), Luis Romero, MBA (BDC), Susan Dafoe, CCS (Cole International), and Jon P. Yormick (Yormick Law)—provided a roadmap for businesses to protect their U.S. market access.

Key insights for businesses involved in cross-border goods transportation from my participation in this workshop:

• Documentation is Your First Line of Defense: Experts emphasize that "the party with the best documentation always wins." To survive an audit, you must maintain a clear audit trail that includes verified supplier certifications, costed bills of materials, and written origin analyses.
• Qualification is Not Automatic: A common misconception is that qualification is based solely on regional value percentages. In reality, CUSMA eligibility is strictly tied to HS classification and specific rules such as "tariff shifts" or "regional value content."

• Increased Scrutiny & Enforcement: U.S. customs authorities have become more aggressive due to revenue collection pressures. Verifications are no longer rare and are often triggered by something as simple as a refund request or a missing CUSMA claim at entry.

• Internal Alignment is Key: Compliance often goes "off the rails" when procurement teams change suppliers without consulting compliance teams. A single sourcing change can unintentionally cause a product to lose its CUSMA eligibility.

• Manage Risk Through Contracts: Exporters should treat their terms and conditions as an insurance policy. Include indemnification clauses that hold suppliers accountable if they provide incorrect origin information that results in penalties or duties.

• Know When NOT to Claim: If a product already enters the U.S. duty-free, claiming CUSMA may provide no financial benefit while unnecessarily increasing your risk of a customs audit.

Immediate Action Steps:
1. Review your supplier certifications and audit trails.
2. Confirm your tariff classifications (HS codes) are up-to-date—remember, the U.S. often requires ten digits for statistical reasons.
3. Audit your internal processes to ensure procurement, sales, and compliance are aligned.

CUSMA compliance is a process, not just a form. By doing the work upfront, you can turn a potential verification into a manageable, short-lived event.

post_text: Leadership and management roles – aren’t these what most ambitious, career-minded people are ultimately striving for? Attaining such a position proves our capabilities and is a sign of true success. I know that in my own career, I have always focused on having the greatest positive impact on an organisation, and as my career grew, this has led me most often to positions of authority. However, there is a seldom-voiced con to leadership that I discovered once I was in a management role. Loneliness. Being elevated above your peers sometimes results in a deep sense of isolation that can be overwhelming. A few years ago, Harvard Business Review ’s inaugural CEO Snapshot Survey found that more than half of the CEOs surveyed experienced feelings of loneliness, and 61% believed that it affected their job performance. But the feeling isn’t unique to CEOs. The study found that loneliness was impacting leaders and managers at all levels. Those new to an authority role were found to be particularly susceptible to feelings of isolation. So why, when we are at the top of our game and finally reaching the heights we have been striving for years to attain, are we suffering from loneliness to such a crippling degree? I can only speak for myself, but throughout my time in leadership roles I have found that the lack of someone to confide in, to bounce problems around with and just to talk with about the general business of the day has at times left me feeling quite alone. So why did I feel I had no-one to confide in? When I reflected on it, I realised that I struggled with finding the right balance between being a friend, a manager, a leader and a teammate to those I managed. How could I effectively be all these things, all at once? There has to be a distance between you as a leader and your team or staff. Even if you might have drinks with them on a Friday night, or chat to them over lunch, there will always come a point at which you have to stop being a colleague or friend and become their boss. This barrier between you and the people you work beside every day means that, to some extent, you keep everyone at arms-length. I battled with this, just as I battled with feeling comfortable showing vulnerability to my team. I didn’t want to admit mistakes or that I might be struggling with a problem because I believed that, as a leader, I always had to be strong. What I have found most helpful in overcoming this has been getting a career coach. I have someone to talk to and someone I am able to be vulnerable with, who in turn helps me to be vulnerable with my team and colleagues and to find ways to connect with them while maintaining appropriate leader/team relationships. Through coaching I have learned that good leaders aren’t always strong and great leaders allow themselves, when necessary, to share their challenges and weaknesses with their staff. Coaching has helped me bridge that divide a little. I also learnt that you need different coaches and mentors to help you through your career and at different times, because people are not infallible. Of course, as a leader you will always bear the weight of responsibility. With coaching, I have been able to find some ways to manage this burden but, in all honesty, I must admit that I haven’t completely overcome the challenge of solitude. There are times that I still feel alone, even when surrounded by people. Management, at any level, can involve an enormous amount of stress and responsibility. I’ve seen these play out in colleagues through drinking, weight gain, smoking, affairs and often simply because these people felt they had no-one to confide in when it came to the day-to-day challenges of leadership. Wonderful leaders have become so crippled by it that they appear distant and lacking empathy, or even worse. There is no doubt that leadership can be lonely, however, as a leader I feel that I have a responsibility – to my team, to the organisation and to myself – to find ways to deal with this. With the help of coaching, I’ve taken the first steps and I’ll continue to find ways to combat the sense of separation that can make top of the tree an often lonely place to be.

post_text: Hello all! Over the last few weeks Scratch Caddie has been moving along well. After giving our MVP pitch back in December we were given some great feedback on our presentation and product. We made a discovery that Scratch Caddie will now be fully marketed towards golf courses instead of customers. We plan on making a more stationary design with more features rather than focusing on the functionality and convenience of our product. Going into this sprint out goal was to create our new prototype and create a new survey geared towards golf courses rather than people. Starting with the prototype, Andrew and I researched and discovered some of the supplies we will be using. We proceeded to order those off of amazon and they have just come in. We are eager and exited to finally start making our prototype. We also completed our survey that will be marketed towards courses. In the next sprint our goals will be to finalize our prototype and start making connections to golf courses and manufactures. This has been a process for both Andrew and I but with each goal completed we are 1 step closer to our business launching.

post_text: While detailing a roof access ladder, a simple question came up: How should the first rung height be handled to stay OSHA-compliant without creating fabrication or site issues? OSHA allows a maximum of 14″ to the first rung, but maintaining consistency in rung spacing is just as important for constructability. In this case, two approaches were evaluated: 1. Keeping the first few rungs at a reduced spacing, then switching to standard spacing, 2. Maintaining uniform 12″ spacing throughout and absorbing the tolerance at the bottom. This kind of decision may look minor on drawings, but it directly affects code compliance, field installation, and safety. Proposed Solution: The ladder layout was finalized by maintaining the minimum required first rung height and equally spacing the initial rungs, followed by standard spacing for the remaining ladder height. This approach meets OSHA requirements, preserves constructability, and eliminates unnecessary field adjustments, resulting in a safer and more efficient installation.

While detailing a roof access ladder, a simple question came up:

How should the first rung height be handled to stay OSHA-compliant without creating fabrication or site issues? OSHA allows a maximum of 14″ to the first rung, but maintaining consistency in rung spacing is just as important for constructability. In this case, two approaches were evaluated:

1. Keeping the first few rungs at a reduced spacing, then switching to standard spacing, 
2. Maintaining uniform 12″ spacing throughout and absorbing the tolerance at the bottom.

This kind of decision may look minor on drawings, but it directly affects code compliance, field installation, and safety.

Proposed Solution: The ladder layout was finalized by maintaining the minimum required first rung height and equally spacing the initial rungs, followed by standard spacing for the remaining ladder height. This approach meets OSHA requirements, preserves constructability, and eliminates unnecessary field adjustments, resulting in a safer and more efficient installation.

Inspection is no longer just maintenance.

For critical subsea infrastructure, inspection is becoming a way to build awareness, reduce risk and strengthen resilience.

Offshore energy systems, subsea cables, ports and underwater assets operate in environments where access is limited and uncertainty is high.

Seeing what happens below the surface is the first step.
Understanding it is the next one. 🌊

At Seamorph Robotics, we are working on reconfigurable autonomous underwater vehicles designed for the next generation of subsea inspection and infrastructure protection.
What does infrastructure resilience mean below the surface?

post_text: As a society the price we collectively pay for cyber-attacks continues to grow, not only in the obvious financial and operational impacts, but other physical and social hazards as well. The August cyber attack on Clorox has led the company to warn of likely supply shortages as we roll into flu season and the predictable and cyclical increase in COVID cases. The cyber attack on St. Margaret’s Health resulted in the hospital chain shuttering its doors leaving area patients stranded. Attacks on other healthcare organizations such as Prospect Medical have resulted in ambulances re-routed away from the closest hospitals and surgical procedures delayed, placing patients in serious risk. With every new story the societal penalties seem to rise while the solution seems almost hopeless for many…almost. In her talk at the Trellix Ransomware Detection & Response Virtual Summit in August 2023, the “Friendly Hacker” Keren Elazari highlighted some data points around how threat groups have begun cataloging and highlighting their exploit speeds. Additionally, in an October 5th Recorded Future article , the author highlights how cybercrime gangs have begun deploying ransomware (late stage of an attack) in as little as 24-hours; down from 4.5 days a year ago. With the broad availability of tools such as ChatGPT and Bard providing new capabilities for everyone, including the threat actors, you can rest assured the velocity of attacks is going to increase in the near term. In the race to build resiliency into our cyber architectures, a concept the security community must keep focus on is that same concept of “velocity.” Velocity in cybersecurity comes in several forms: velocity of comprehension, velocity of response, and velocity of recovery. Velocity before, during, and after an attack. In the cybersecurity marketplace we see and hear a loud and steady stream of media on solutions, approaches, frameworks and other cyber practice recommendations; most having at least some merit, but few holistically revolutionizing the work at hand and helping solve the adjacent challenges such as resource shortages. Enter Extended Detection and Response (XDR). In a recent blog post, Trellix CISO Harold Rivas explains how true XDR has gone from just “marketechture” to a reality and, more importantly, a necessity for CISOs today. XDR becomes the critical linchpin for creating cyber resiliency in your organization, regardless of your philosophy or approach. Most importantly, XDR brings velocity to your program. Velocity of Comprehension Comprehension refers to the speed at which your organization can observe, interpret, and understand the modern and ever-changing operating environment and threat landscape in front of them. This comprehension becomes the driving force for effective (and automated) response and remediation of threats. Poor comprehension means organizations do not understand the goals and motives of the threat actors at their door leaving key resources inadequately defended, that the organization may see part of an attack but miss the bigger picture of a multi-staged threat, or the organization may miss the subtle changes made by a stealthy threat actor in the larger noise of a dynamic enterprise. Understanding the Dynamic Threat Landscape: As new systems and services come and go from our environment, we must be able to dynamically assess the associated risk and apply real-time intelligence and insights to understand the actors, trends, and types of threats we face. Shift From Reactive to Proactive: An understanding of the tactics and techniques exploited by threat actors, the real-time posture of your individual assets, and the actions you can take to prevent exploitation of specific TTP’s before an incident allows organizations to shift from a reactive posture to a proactive one. The proactive approach helps organizations take cumulative action to reduce the risk of entire classes and groups of threats at once. Ubiquitous Threat Intelligence: To be successful, organizations require comprehensive threat intelligence, continuously updated, carefully curated and validated by teams of experts, and consumable across their entire security stack to ensure complete visibility. Broad Integration Capabilities: Organizations have significant investments of time and money in existing solutions and services to defend their enterprise. Thus, they should look to an XDR platform with broad integration capabilities that allows them to pull in the critical insights from all of their investments, and yet remain flexible enough so the organization can swap out technologies and capabilities as their needs evolve. Velocity of Response When responding to incidents, organizations must have clear, consistent, and holistic steps that are taken with speed and precision to minimize potential damage while ensuring complete eradication. Organizations must acquire the capabilities that will allow them to identify, classify, and respond the threats across their complete operating environment. Threat Interpretation and Prioritization: As events occur within the environment, analysts must be presented with actionable alerts, correlated and consolidated across vectors, providing a clear understanding of the complete attack chain, the users, devices, and data at risk, and the next steps. Automation and Orchestration: Automation and orchestration significantly extend analyst capabilities by automatically performing tasks to enrich, contain, block, or other actions as needed. These capabilities must occur quickly, in a consistent and repeatable fashion, and reduce the mean-time-to-resolution. Act Globally: XDR gives security teams the ability to act globally across their organization, responding to and eliminating threats across their stable of assets and across vectors. AI-Guided Investigations: AI-guided investigative playbooks dynamically evolve for the incident at hand, providing analysts expert guidance derived from security experts and machine learning. This ensures a consistent approach and a complete response to the incident. Velocity of Recovery In the event an incident does occur, swift recovery is paramount to allow the organization to resume normal operations and minimize the any financial, operational, or reputational damages. An organization’s resiliency is measured by their ability to recover quickly. Rollback Remediation: Even with the best defenses, new threats will arise. Defenses such as Rollback Remediation to identify unauthorized changes caused by threats like ransomware, kill the processes, and rollback the file and registry modifications to their original state. This provides a painless and rapid recovery for targeted systems. Minimizing Business Impact: Swift threat identification, containment, and recovery ensures that business operations are restored quickly, minimizing potential financial losses and ensuring trust is not eroded. Learning and Adapting: One of the most important parts of an incident is the lessons learned that come out of that incident. The right XDR solution highlights the areas for improvement following an incident to show how an organization can improve their posture and prevent similar incidents from re-occurring in the future. In conclusion, while technology, tactics, and strategies are essential components of a robust cybersecurity posture, the speed at which we comprehend, respond to, and recover from threats holds paramount importance. As cyber threats continue to evolve, the velocity will undoubtedly remain a defining factor in an organization's ability to safeguard its digital assets and reputation. Exploring the world of DevOps!🚀
In the final part of the ADAM Coding Program, we stepped into DevOps, moving beyond code into servers, networking, and automation.

One of the most valuable projects so far was the Deep-in-System project, where I:
🔹 Installed and configured an Ubuntu LTS server from scratch
🔹 Managed Ubuntu and database users and their permissions
🔹 Set up static networking and firewall rules
🔹 Created secure user access (PPK and password-based SSH)
🔹 Installed and configured MySQL & WordPress
🔹Installed and configured an FTP server 
🔹 Automated daily backups with cron
It was my first true “sysadmin” experience! Understanding not only how things work, but also why they’re configured that way!

Alongside it, I completed Deep-in-Net project, that is a series of networking exercises done using Cisco Packet Tracer; to visualize and troubleshoot network flows, subnets, and protocols.

These projects gave me a stronger appreciation for how infrastructure, networking, and security all tie together.

👉 Tutorial for Deep In System Project: https://lnkd.in/e8bcjvpC

post_text: Several times I share my strong conviction that a National Healthcare system does not work properly without providing an effective Primary Care service. General Practitioners (GP) and Family Doctors play a crucial role in diagnosing, monitoring, and treating patients. These are the healthcare professionals (also to mention the nurses) that stand closer to the patients. Because of this proximity, these physicians often play the role of confidents or advisors. They are the “Family” Doctors. Also, mentioned by me before, the communication between Primary Care and Secondary Care is of utmost importance; referring patients to the hospital means, in the first hand, that these patients need additional care. This must be done based on a fluent, clear and honest communication between physicians. Most probably a proximity between Primary Car and hospital, works much better than just a letter sent from one to another. In terms of shared skills, the Specialists must be open to share their knowledge and expertise with the GP, and these must be available to talk about the complexity of being a Family Doctor, the relationship with the patients, their families, problems, needs, in summary, all the knowledge that comes from the close relationship with “their” patients. Although apparently simple, the truth is that it doesn’t work exactly this way. Because of lack of resources (time?), need to accomplish with specific performance indicators (time spent with patients?), but also due to inertia, who is ready to give the first step, there is still a lot to improve. The population lives longer, with more and specific medical needs. It is not possible that the hospitals will be able to answer all these needs. A well prepared, well equipped and highly skilled Primary Care provides all the necessary assistance, referring to hospitals only the patients who, in fact need, additional medical care. Recently, a partnership in the Centre Region between the Healthcare authorities and local government authorities (Aveiro, Mortágua, Pedrógão Grande, Santa Comba Dão and Ovar) was announced with the objective of allocating funds to increase the quality of healthcare assistance to the population. This is a great example of the recognition that joined efforts to face common problems result in a much better outcome and services. After all, the population benefits from it and this is what is expected from those who work to answer peoples’ needs. Well done.

Although apparently simple, the truth is that it doesn’t work exactly this way. Because of lack of resources (time?), need to accomplish with specific performance indicators (time spent with patients?), but also due to inertia, who is ready to give the first step, there is still a lot to improve.

The population lives longer, with more and specific medical needs. It is not possible that the hospitals will be able to answer all these needs. A well prepared, well equipped and highly skilled Primary Care provides all the necessary assistance, referring to hospitals only the patients who, in fact need, additional medical care.

Recently, a partnership in the Centre Region between the Healthcare authorities and local government authorities (Aveiro, Mortágua, Pedrógão Grande, Santa Comba Dão and Ovar) was announced with the objective of allocating funds to increase the quality of healthcare assistance to the population. This is a great example of the recognition that joined efforts to face common problems result in a much better outcome and services.

After all, the population benefits from it and this is what is expected from those who work to answer peoples’ needs.

Well done.

post_text: Loyalty programs are an integral part of the retail landscape, as familiar and enduring as commerce itself. In this new digital era, where data flows faster and technology evolves daily, retailers must look beyond what customers do and strive to understand why people feel loyal in the first place. Loyalty programs began as tangible gestures with stamp and punch cards that tracked return visits and rewarded commitment with goods or discounts. The computer age introduced points systems, elite tiers, and digital coupons, offering more sophisticated ways to recognize individual shoppers and track behaviors. Today, as commerce stretches across in-store, online, and mobile, the most successful loyalty programs are defined by deep personalization and unified omnichannel experiences. Retailers now use customer data to tailor offers and design rewards that move seamlessly with their customers, whether shopping from a laptop in the evening or scanning a barcode at a register during lunch. The Psychology Behind Loyalty At its core, loyalty satisfies fundamental human needs: Recognition – Customers want to be noticed and appreciated for their choices. Progress and Achievement – Earning points or unlocking new tiers taps into our love of accomplishment. Trust and Belonging – We remain faithful to brands that feel trustworthy and inclusive, a genuine tribe. Surprise and Delight – Unexpected bonuses or thoughtful perks activate our sense of reward and forge lasting positive memories. Decades of behavioral science confirm that these motivations—recognition, achievement, trust, and delight—drive repeat engagement more powerfully than discounts alone. The Science of Emotional Loyalty Modern loyalty programs do more than tally transactions; they build emotional loyalty by signaling, "We see you." When a brand recognizes a birthday, celebrates a milestone, or lets a customer use points for a favorite cause, it creates a powerful emotional anchor. Several psychological triggers are at play: Endowment Effect : Believing "my points" have added value. This cognitive bias means people value the items they own, even if identical to others, more highly, creating emotional attachment and increasing engagement with the program. Variable Reinforcement : Random, fun surprises. In behavioral psychology, variable reinforcement describes a schedule where the timing or frequency of rewards is unpredictable, keeping customers delightfully engaged. Social Proof : Badges or leaderboards that show where you stand in a community. Social proof is the tendency to copy the behavior of others, especially in uncertain situations. In loyalty marketing, showcasing the popularity or positive experiences of others encourages participation and boosts engagement. AI and the Future of Loyalty: Where Human and Machine Meet The next horizon blends advanced technology with classic psychology. Artificial intelligence is giving retailers the tools to anticipate needs, personalize in real time, and respond at exactly the right moment. AI-enabled loyalty solutions now: Proactively re-engage at-risk customers with personalized offers or reminders, often before a human marketer could even spot the risk. Provide conversational support via chatbots, making it easy to check balances, redeem rewards, or get help at any hour. Tailor reward options to a customer's beliefs by matching them with sustainability projects or charitable campaigns that resonate personally. Navigating New Challenges These innovations bring new responsibilities: Avoiding Fatigue : Too many generic offers erode trust. Smart AI now focuses on relevance and resonance rather than volume. Privacy and Control : Customers expect transparency and must be able to view, control, and restrict how their data is used. Human Touch : Even as AI grows more sophisticated, genuine human empathy, especially in problem-solving, remains a premium feature. Conclusion: The Future of Loyalty Is Human at Its Core Tomorrow's loyalty winners will not just automate, but also humanize. AI and advanced analytics will free brands to focus on deeper connections, understanding psychology, amplifying recognition, and making every reward feel uniquely meaningful. The future is not only high tech but also high touch. Brands that master both will turn shoppers into fans and fans into advocates in a world where genuine loyalty still matters most.

cold email booked me a sales call with an AI founder within 3 hours. No case study. No audience and no ads. Just 200 words. Here's the exact strategy: When I started reaching out to AI-first founders, I did what everyone does: Cold pitches and volume. And don't get me started on the automation. And I got ghosted. A lot. So I stopped sending and started asking one question: \"What would make a founder reply within the hour?\" I landed on 2 answers: 1) The message has to prove I studied THEIR product. Not their industry. Their product, their content, their funnel & their marketing. 2) It has to hand them something they can use immediately. Free and no strings attached. That second part became my Trojan Horse. Instead of pitching, every email contains one concrete, ready-to-film content idea or a usable lead magnet or newsletter idea. Built for their product. Why that specific gift? It passes 3 filters: 1) It's a piece of what I'd deliver anyway in a full engagement. Real work, not a teaser. 2) I can build one in under an hour. So I can do it for every prospect, every week, without burning out. 3) It's the thing almost every AI B2B founder is missing. They built a product that sells itself in a demo, but nobody's booking the demo. They get value whether they will work with me or not. The results since switching: 26% of my cold emails get a reply. Cold outreach benchmarks sit around 1 to 5%. 100% of booked calls actually show up. Or if I can, I fiscally go to them. And that founder from the first line? I mailed him the morning his accelerator news dropped, with an angle built on that exact momentum. Meeting confirmed the same day. The lesson isn't \"write better emails.\" Stop asking strangers for their time. Start handing them a reason to want yours. So, what's the ONE piece of your paid work you could give away this week? PS: the timing part matters more than people think. Funding news, accelerator selections, product launches: mail on momentum, not on Mondays. Content SDR’s will completely wipe out the outbound SDR role.

Why hire 100 SDR’s when 1 can create daily content & bring you boat loads of demos?

Think of the math:

You spend $70k/year on an outbound SDR +$30k/year on commissions.

They make 200 dials/day using a power dialer & book maybe 1 meeting per day.

But if you get a content SDR, instead of spending 8 hours/day cold calling to get 1 meeting booked, that SDR can create content all day.

Now you just gotta figure out which type of content converts into demos (Contento can help you figure that out by the way) then you replicate it over & over again.

Voila, now you have a Linkedin content engine🔥

Content SDR’s are the future.

Especially since everyone’s emails & LinkedIn DM’s are filled with AI slop, & soon cold calls will be AI slop.

Content will become the clear winner (especially video content).

Do you think Content SDR’s will replace cold outbound?

attended by all 20 partner Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) and Town Clerks (TCs). Held in #Harare on 28 and 29 April, the workshop aimed to identify and share good practices in local governance. Combining expert insights with management best practices, the event aimed to strengthen the capacity of CEOs and TCs to drive transformation, mobilise funding and partnerships, and advance service delivery. Participants agreed to establish follow-up platforms for continuous learning, allowing local authorities outside the project to access and benefit from the identified best practices. The workshop was part of the Good Governance in Local Authorities (GGLA) project, which supports local authorities (LAs) in identifying, piloting and sharing good practices in areas such as service delivery, local economic development, public financial management, councillor support, digitalisation, gender and citizen engagement. The project aims to strengthen the capacity of LAs to meet key government policy expectations, including National Development Strategy 2 (NDS2), the Call to Action – No Compromise to Service Delivery and, in particular, the Minimum Service Delivery Standards. The GGLA project is fully managed by the 𝗚𝗙𝗔 𝗘𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗳𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮 𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝗶𝗻 𝗡𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗶, which supports the GFA Governance Department's East and Southern Africa portfolio. post_text: Hard to believe it's already been two months since I returned to clinical practice! During my time in industry, I evaluated promising technologies in therapeutic areas ranging from dermatology to ophthalmology to immunotherapy, always asking: "Will this work in the real world?" Now, seeing patients and clients, I appreciate that question needs refinement. What I've observed is that we have newly approved therapies that offer only marginal improvements over established treatments, that don't justify the price premium for many clients. Meanwhile, truly transformative innovations await regulatory approval or are priced beyond the reach of most families. As a result, many decades-old protocols remain the workhorses of daily practice given their reliability, accessibility, and effectiveness. This isn't about assigning blame. Having worked on both sides, I understand the complex ecosystem and see opportunities for bridging these gaps. Development is expensive, regulatory pathways are challenging, and market dynamics are complicated. Recognizing these realities means we can have more honest conversations about solutions. Pet owners are becoming remarkably sophisticated about treatment decisions and ask thoughtful questions regarding outcomes versus costs; they draw distinctions between meaningful innovation and incremental improvements. I think this creates opportunities for everyone involved. Moving forward I see a need for both accessible therapies that serve everyday practice and breakthrough innovations that advance veterinary medicine (even if initially limited in reach). The key is transparency about which is which. Every day in practice reminds me that successful innovation is more than scientific elegance. We need to ask, "What's the practical impact in the exam room?" For those of you who've moved between industry and practice: what insights did you gain after switching perspectives? #VeterinaryMedicine #AnimalHealth #ClinicalInnovation #IndustryInsights

Luckily, chitosan presents a promising solution in veterinary ophthalmology. 💧 How Chitosan Helps The Dry Eye Crisis - Mucoadhesion Power: Chitosan's positive charge strongly binds to the negatively charged mucin on the ocular surface. This bioadhesion significantly prolongs the lubricant's contact time, directly reducing the required frequency of daily application [1, 2]. - Active Wound Healing: Chitosan is more than just a passive lubricant. It actively accelerates the proliferation and migration of corneal epithelial cells, supporting the repair of the abrasions and ulcers that often accompany severe dry eye [3]. - Antimicrobial Shield: The polymer possesses intrinsic, broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. While not a substitute for antibiotics, this property helps reduce the risk of secondary infections in a compromised, dry ocular environment—a valuable secondary benefit [3]. - Viscosity & Comfort: A recent article from SignalPET® highlights how easy it is to make mistakes. Artifacts can be misinterpreted as tumors or infections, while real lesions may be mistaken for noise or technical errors. Some key insights to keep in mind: 🔹 Artifacts often arise from superimposition, anatomical variations, or technical factors, and are typically characterized by, for example, opaque spots that change shape or disappear in other projections. 🔹 A symmetrical finding in the opposite limb often indicates a normal variation, always compare with the contralateral limb. 🔹 Seek further advice if a finding is uncertain; don’t automatically dismiss anything ambiguous as an “artifact.” 🔹 AI tools help highlight suspicious changes and contribute to a more objective interpretation. 👉🏼 In short: by combining systematic analysis, anatomical knowledge, and modern support tools, you can reduce the risk of both overdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. Hard to believe it's already been two months since I returned to clinical practice! During my time in industry, I evaluated promising technologies in therapeutic areas ranging from dermatology to ophthalmology to immunotherapy, always asking: "Will this work in the real world?"

Now, seeing patients and clients, I appreciate that question needs refinement. What I've observed is that we have newly approved therapies that offer only marginal improvements over established treatments, that don't justify the price premium for many clients. Meanwhile, truly transformative innovations await regulatory approval or are priced beyond the reach of most families.

As a result, many decades-old protocols remain the workhorses of daily practice given their reliability, accessibility, and effectiveness.

This isn't about assigning blame. Having worked on both sides, I understand the complex ecosystem and see opportunities for bridging these gaps. Development is expensive, regulatory pathways are challenging, and market dynamics are complicated. Recognizing these realities means we can have more honest conversations about solutions.

Pet owners are becoming remarkably sophisticated about treatment decisions and ask thoughtful questions regarding outcomes versus costs; they draw distinctions between meaningful innovation and incremental improvements. I think this creates opportunities for everyone involved.

Moving forward I see a need for both accessible therapies that serve everyday practice and breakthrough innovations that advance veterinary medicine (even if initially limited in reach). The key is transparency about which is which.

Every day in practice reminds me that successful innovation is more than scientific elegance. We need to ask, "What's the practical impact in the exam room?"

For those of you who've moved between industry and practice: what insights did you gain after switching perspectives?

#VeterinaryMedicine #AnimalHealth #ClinicalInnovation #IndustryInsights

If you recognized yourself in even ONE of these, you're leading unconsciously.

And you're not alone.

Most capable leaders operate on autopilot, not because they lack skill, but because urgency rewards reaction over reflection.

Here's what unconscious leadership creates:

❌ Teams that comply but don't commit
❌ Decisions that stall while waiting for perfect certainty
❌ High performers who leave without warning
❌ Culture that erodes beneath surface-level performance
❌ Leaders who burn out while still delivering results

The cost?
Trust weakens.
Standards become negotiable.
Your best people update their resumes.
You become the bottleneck instead of the multiplier.

But here's the truth:

Unconscious leadership isn't a character flaw. It's a consequence of pace.

The moment you interrupt the cycle, the moment you choose awareness over autopilot, everything shifts.

From "Conscious LeaderShift" by Corliss Charles-Sutton:

This book reveals the inner and outer shifts required for modern leadership, how to lead with clarity when certainty isn't available, how to hold accountability without fear, and how to build influence through consistency instead of authority.

Which of these 5 signs hit hardest for you?

Drop the number in the comments. Let's talk about it.

And if you're ready to shift from performing leadership to practicing it, get the book.

post_text: Who says you can't bootstrap to unicorn status? Johanna Småros with her co-founders led RELEX Solutions , to become a leader in supply chain and retail planning with her last valuation at €5 billion, raising to date more than €800 million including a strategic infusion by Blackstone . From supporting brands such as Coles Group to SEPHORA to Lowe's Companies, Inc. , their innovative solutions are ones you probably use today but don't even know it. But hold up—how did this unassuming company built out of Finland, come to be? This summer, I spent some time with Johanna in her office in Helsinki and unpacked her incredible journey. From bootstrapping for over a decade to transforming the company into a global leader, her story is a testament to innovation, resilience, and strategic vision. This is why, Johanna is next on the list of #BillionDollarMoves we should all learn from. This article is part of the Billion Dollar Moves CEO Series — exploring the convictions behind how leaders build, decide, and scale through moments of risk and inflection. #BillionDollarMoves Deconstructed 1. Don't Underestimate Academic Foundations Business folk are often quick to glaze over R&D projects that lack clarity on the 'go-to-market'. Especially in this environment, the pressure for a monetization strategy early on, is VERY real. And yet, challenging the status quo, RELEX's inception is deeply rooted in the academic rigor of its co-founders. To be precise, it started from when Johanna "accidentally landed a summer job in a research group" which led to research on supply chain collaboration, where collaborative planning, forecasting and replenishment were not quite where it is today. Frustrated by the 'slowness of it all' in research, Johanna and her co-founders, Michael and Mikko transitioned from academia to industry with a vision to address real-world supply chain challenges. “We felt that maybe research isn't the right vehicle to actually build new things and change the world,” Johanna reflects on their strategic move to start RELEX. This transition was not just a leap of faith; it was a calculated step after realizing by working with clients through their initial research group that a gap in the market existed. 2. Do It Your Way: The Finnish Way of Building 🇫🇮 Instead of rushing to Silicon Valley to build, RELEX leaned in to their Finnish roots and their rich tech ecosystem. Johanna and her co-founders leveraged the country’s exceptional R&D talent, particularly in software development. Even more compelling was the way they built their culture; the 'Finnish way': “We don't believe too much in hierarchy here in the Nordics. And that's actually super helpful when you're starting your own company; people around you are willing to offer their opinion and their expertise.” This collaborative and pragmatic approach has been a cornerstone of RELEX’s success, fostering an environment where innovation thrives. Even today as a multi-billion founder actively leading her company, Johanna hot-desks like everyone else! 3. Find Your Unique Approach in a Saturated Space While supply chain management solutions may seem saturated, RELEX emerged by focusing on nuanced, overlooked areas. The foundation of Johanna's strategy was again tied to her rich academic insight into the industry's intricacies, enabling the development of solutions that resonated on a deeper level with clients. Further, while Finland's small market could be seen as a disadvantage (where a single vertical may not have been deep enough), RELEX used it to their advantage: “…consumer electronics, agriculture, retail, car tires - we eventually had to serve them all. Sure, there was a big variance in clients that we landed. It was a bit of a challenge, but it was actually a huge blessing for our R&D effort.” Their commitment to delivering impactful solutions and measurable performance has been a key driver of their success. RELEX further distinguished itself by combining elements needed by their clients in these different verticals, stitching together demand planning, commercial planning, and operational execution into a seamless platform, effectively addressing the disjointed nature of supply chain management. This innovative integration ultimately made them a category-maker for a cohesive approach to optimizing supply chains. And to make it a no-brainer for new clients to expand their cohesive use of RELEX?Johanna introduced a business model that minimized client risk by demonstrating tangible ROI and offering piloting with money-back guarantees. We actually had a money-back guarantee where clients could step off anytime and we'll just refund them what they paid us. So their risk was only the work that they needed to put in to try using our system, and it worked. We never needed to refund anyone. 4. Leverage Existing Champions to Drive Global Ambition Many founders I've spoken to have in the past faltered on global expansion — too soon, too slow, not quite right. RELEX’s expansion was strategic to say the least—using global clients who were working with RELEX through their Finnish regional office. Johanna was clear from day one that they needed a beachhead strategy— to gain a stronghold with multi-national brands locally before expanding into a larger market. Initially focusing on the Finnish market further allowed RELEX to refine their product and understand diverse client needs intimately. That was exactly how they landed brands like Coles Group PetSmart Lidl GB and many others! Their decision to bootstrap for the first decade further demonstrates RELEX's commitment to sustainable growth and product excellence. It wasn't until the company set its sights on the U.S. market that they opted for venture capital, to fuel their expansion in the global arena with the firepower, and right backers to compete and win. It proved to be a very worthwhile bet that set the foundations for the future. And there you have it, to make Billion Dollar Moves like Johanna; here are three actionable questions you can ask yourself: How can I leverage my local ecosystem to build global success? What do I need to do to package the success stories I am already delivering my clients? And finally, what strategies can I implement to build trust and minimize client risk? Johanna will remain one of the most notable leaders I’ll be watching, especially as she now expands her important philanthropic work with her co-founders: "Our commitment to the RELEX Foundation stems from our belief that successful businesses have a responsibility to give back. By dedicating €100 million in company stock and a €10 million cash injection to combat climate change, we aim to leverage our resources to drive significant environmental impact. This initiative reflects our deep-seated values and our dedication to creating a sustainable future for generations to come." RELEX's transformation from an academic project to a global leader in supply chain optimization is a compelling example for B2B founders. By focusing on strategic growth, client-focused product development, innovative business models, and a strong commitment to sustainability, RELEX has achieved impressive success and set a high standard for how tech companies can effect positive global change. How has Johanna inspired you? -- This episode brought to you by Helsinki Partners is part of the #BillionDollarMoves CEO series, which unpacks the mental models and key leadership strategies of today’s movers & shakers as they navigated crisis, failure, and built success. Grow Your Local Businesses - Day: 3

🌟 "Your Next Customer Could Be Right Around the Corner!" 🌟

Did you know most people search for businesses near them before making a purchase? In fact:
📍 46% of all Google searches are looking for local information.
📱 Searches like "coffee shop near me" or "best plumber in [city]" are happening every second.

But here’s the catch: If your business isn’t optimized for local searches, your competitors could be scooping up those customers.

💡 Quick Tip for Today:
Make sure your website (or social media page) clearly shows:
✅ Your business name
✅ Address (if applicable)
✅ Contact information
✅ Service areas

These small updates can make a BIG difference in helping nearby customers find you!

✨ Question for You:
If someone searched for your business type in your area, would they find you? Let me know in the comments or message me—I’d love to hear how you’re showing up locally!

92475586561","post_text":"Last year, I met a consultant who was brilliant at what she did. She had loyal clients, strong referrals, and solid results. But her business had hit a strange wall. She couldn’t understand why new leads kept going cold after the first meeting. Then one day, she googled her own name. Her face dropped. The first thing that showed up was an outdated website from 2017. Broken links, blurry photos, and a contact form that didn’t even work. It looked like the business had been closed for years. And that’s when it clicked. People weren’t ghosting her. They just didn’t trust what they saw. Be honest for a second. Have you ever judged a business by its website or online presence? We all have. Because in today’s world, your website is your first handshake. It’s the version of you that people meet before you ever speak. That experience taught me something simple but powerful: You can be amazing at what you do, but if your online presence doesn’t show it, people will move on. And it’s not about fancy designs or flashy effects. It’s about clarity, trust, and ease. If your website doesn’t instantly show who you are, what you offer, and how to reach you, you’re losing opportunities every single day. Here’s what you can do right now: 1. Google yourself. Grow Your Local Businesses - Day: 3

🌟 "Your Next Customer Could Be Right Around the Corner!" 🌟

Did you know most people search for businesses near them before making a purchase? In fact:
📍 46% of all Google searches are looking for local information.

But here’s the catch: If your business isn’t optimized for local searches, your competitors could be scooping up those customers.

💡 Quick Tip for Today:
Make sure your website (or social media page) clearly shows:
✅ Your business name
✅ Address (if applicable)
✅ Contact information
✅ Service areas

These small updates can make a BIG difference in helping nearby customers find you!

✨ Question for You:
If someone searched for your business type in your area, would they find you? Let me know in the comments or message me—I’d love to hear how you’re showing up locally!

#LocalBusinessTips #GrowYourBusiness #LocalSEO

post_text: Do you love your Freight Forwarder? Below I share my thoughts on what makes this business a very difficult but invaluable component of International commerce. Would be interested to hear your comments and experiences on what is like to work with your freight forwarder (or to be a Freight Forwarder), and if you agree or not with my comments below. If you ship product Internationally, you have heard the term freight forwarding. Freight forwarding is a massive business, and has been around for as long as trade has occurred between nations. The role of the freight forwarder is to serve as the intermediary between the two or more parties involved in an International buying transaction. They perform a large variety of services on behalf of all related parties, normally under the direction of the product buyer. Their services can include help with the myriad documentation required for International trade; Arranging transport of the product; Providing abundant amounts of information about the transaction; Quality assurance; and a whole range of discreet value added functions as prescribed by their clients. Despite their yeoman's role in facilitation of trade, Forwarders often get a bad rap. From experience, there are a variety of reasons for why that is likely the case: complexity of the transactions, opaque processes, mistrust between the buyer and seller (that the forwarder is often in the middle of), the uncertainty involved with International trade in general, the number and wide variety of services they offer. And to be fair, they sometimes bring it on themselves, through poor service or by also being opaque. On the other hand, having worked with and for a variety of Freight Forwarders, from the biggest to the smallest, I wanted to share a couple of observations in support of this industry. In fact, I would say freight forwarding is deserving of much praise, as they are truly a swiss army knife in the transportation industry. In order to be successful, a forwarder has to operate in all 24 time zones, multiple languages, coordinate a large number of parties with often competing interests, and rely on a large number of other actors (such as ports, carriers, gov't agencies) in order to perform their jobs flawlessly. Do you love your Freight Forwarder? Below I share my thoughts on what makes this business a very difficult but invaluable component of International commerce. Would be interested to hear your comments and experiences on what is like to work with your freight forwarder (or to be a Freight Forwarder), and if you agree or not with my comments below.


If you ship product Internationally, you have heard the term freight forwarding. Freight forwarding is a massive business, and has been around for as long as trade has occurred between nations. The role of the freight forwarder is to serve as the intermediary between the two or more parties involved in an International buying transaction. They perform a large variety of services on behalf of all related parties, normally under the direction of the product buyer. Their services can include help with the myriad documentation required for International trade; Arranging transport of the product; Providing abundant amounts of information about the transaction; Quality assurance; and a whole range of discreet value added functions as prescribed by their clients.


Despite their yeoman's role in facilitation of trade, Forwarders often get a bad rap.


From experience, there are a variety of reasons for why that is likely the case: complexity of the transactions, opaque processes, mistrust between the buyer and seller (that the forwarder is often in the middle of), the uncertainty involved with International trade in general, the number and wide variety of services they offer. And to be fair, they sometimes bring it on themselves, through poor service or by also being opaque.


On the other hand, having worked with and for a variety of Freight Forwarders, from the biggest to the smallest, I wanted to share a couple of observations in support of this industry. In fact, I would say freight forwarding is deserving of much praise, as they are truly a swiss army knife in the transportation industry.



  1. In order to be successful, a forwarder has to operate in all 24 time zones, multiple languages, coordinate a large number of parties with often competing interests, and rely on a large number of other actors (such as ports, carriers, gov't agencies) in order to perform their jobs flawlessly. Most of the time, despite all of this orchestration, they pull it off.

  2. Unlike other transportation functions, the forwarder must deal with every single mode of transport and type of distribution activity including ocean, air, rail, trucking, parcel, consolidation, deconsolidation, storage, drayage, LTL, LCL. Each segment of transportation industry believes theirs is the most challenging, and forwarders must perform all of them.

  3. In many cases, the forwarder is working with inexperienced customers. With a few exceptions, the customer is often painfully unaware of the complexities of International trade themselves. As we all know, when your boss doesn't understand what you do, your job can be quite challenging.


So what do you think? Villian, Hero, or Something In Between?

post_text: “My work should speak for itself.” I hear this all the time. And I get it - I used to think this too. But here’s what that mindset misses: By the time you’re in the interview room, everyone is equally qualified. The person who interviewed before you also has 10+ years of B2B experience at top brands. So does the person after you. So at that point, it’s not about who’s most qualified. It’s about who makes it easiest for the hiring team to say yes. Hiring teams run on signal. They’re not sitting there reading between the lines of your experience - they’re waiting for you to translate it for them. What problem do they have? How does your background solve it? Why are you the obvious answer? That’s your job as a candidate. Not to let your work speak - but to speak for your work. The people who get offers aren’t always the most qualified in the room. They’re the ones who made it easiest for the hiring team to say yes.

What it really feels like is this: “You have the experience to do the job, but hiring someone with your background requires commitment. We’re choosing candidates who cost less, won’t push back, and will fill a seat without expecting long‑term investment.” That’s the part that stings — not the “no,” but the reality that too many companies are prioritizing convenience over capability. I’m not frustrated because I lack the qualifications. I’m frustrated because so many employers never take the time to actually see the value behind the resume. But here’s the thing: I’m not lowering my standards, and I’m not shrinking myself to fit into a checkbox. If a company can’t recognize my worth now, they were never the right fit to begin with. “My work should speak for itself.” I hear this all the time. And I get it - I used to think this too. But here’s what that mindset misses:

By the time you’re in the interview room, everyone is equally qualified. The person who interviewed before you also has 10+ years of B2B experience at top brands. So does the person after you.

So at that point, it’s not about who’s most qualified.

It’s about who makes it easiest for the hiring team to say yes.

Hiring teams run on signal. They’re not sitting there reading between the lines of your experience - they’re waiting for you to translate it for them.

What problem do they have?
How does your background solve it?
Why are you the obvious answer?

That’s your job as a candidate. Not to let your work speak - but to speak for your work.

The people who get offers aren’t always the most qualified in the room. They’re the ones who made it easiest for the hiring team to say yes.

post_text: 🛑 WHY MOST ENTERPRISE AI PROJECTS FAIL (And how to fix it) 🛑 Terms like RAG, Semantic Layer, and Knowledge Graphs are the "buzzwords of the year." But why do they actually matter for your business? To understand why these technical pieces are non-negotiable, let’s look at what happens when you build an AI without them—using an E-Commerce analogy. 🛒 1️⃣ Chunking: The Difference Between a Manual and a Search Bar ❌ The Con: If you store data as one massive document, the AI has to "read" the whole thing to find one fact. This leads to high costs, slow responses, and "lost in the middle" errors where the AI misses the most important detail. ✅ The Fix: We break data into "chunks" (Specs, FAQs, Reviews). 👉 Result: The AI finds the needle in the haystack instantly, saving time and compute costs. 2️⃣ Embeddings: Beyond Keyword Matching ❌ The Con: Traditional search is "dumb." If a customer searches for "inexpensive footwear" but your data only says "cheap shoes," a keyword-based AI will say "Out of Stock." ✅ The Fix: Embeddings understand the mathematical "closeness" of meaning. 👉 Result: Your AI understands that "low-cost," "affordable," and "budget-friendly" all mean the same thing, providing a human-like search experience. 3️⃣ RAG: Eliminating the "Creative" Assistant ❌ The Con: Without Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), if you ask about your 2024 refund policy, the AI might make up (hallucinate) an answer based on another company's policy it saw online. ✅ The Fix: RAG forces the AI to check YOUR verified catalog before it speaks. 👉 Result: No more hallucinations. Only fact-based, trustworthy answers. 4️⃣ Semantic Layer: Ending the "Metric War" ❌ The Con: Imagine if Marketing defines "Revenue" as gross sales, but Finance defines it as net profit. Your AI will give different answers depending on which table it looks at, destroying executive trust. ✅ The Fix: A Semantic Layer provides one "Logic Map" for the whole company. 👉 Result: Whether it’s a chatbot or a dashboard, "Revenue" always means the same number. 5️⃣ Knowledge Graph: Understanding Contextual Relationships ❌ The Con: Relational databases are bad at context. If a customer asks "Will this charger work with the phone I bought last week?", a basic AI struggles to link the User, the past Order, and the Product Compatibility. ✅ The Fix: A Knowledge Graph maps these relationships as a web. 👉 Result: The AI can reason through complex questions that involve multiple layers of business logic. At Bodh Analytics, we specialize in building the architecture that prevents these common failures: ✅ Structured Chunking for speed. ✅ Semantic Layers for accuracy. ✅ RAG for trust. Is your AI strategy addressing these "cons," or are you just building a fancy chatbot? AI refers to advanced artificial intelligence systems that possess agency—the ability to independently set goals, reason, plan, and execute multi-step actions with minimal human oversight. Unlike traditional AI, which is reactive and requires step-by-step instructions, agentic AI is proactive, meaning it can initiate work on its own to achieve a high-level outcome. Core Characteristics of Agentic AI Agentic systems are defined by their ability to transition from \"thinking\" to \"doing\". Key features include: Autonomy: They can operate independently within defined guardrails, making decisions and completing workflows without human intervention. Goal Orientation: Users provide a high-level objective (e.g., \"optimize this supply chain\") rather than specific instructions. The AI then determines the necessary sub-tasks to achieve it. Adaptability & Learning: These systems use feedback loops to evaluate their own performance. If a plan fails, they can self-correct and refine their strategy in real time. Multi-Step Planning: They break complex, long-term goals into smaller, manageable sequences of tasks. Tool Use: They can interface with external software, APIs, and databases—for example, searching the web, updating a CRM, or executing code. How Agentic AI Works (The \"Perceive-Reason-Act\" Loop) Agentic systems typically operate in a continuous, five-stage cycle: Perceive: Gathers real-time data from environments via sensors, APIs, or user input. Reason: An underlying Large Language Model (LLM) acts as the \"brain,\" interpreting the goal and evaluating context. Plan: The system develops an action plan, choosing the most efficient sequence of steps. Act: The AI executes tasks by calling external tools or interacting with third-party software. Learn: Through a \"data flywheel,\" the system reflects on results, updates its internal logic, and improves for future iterations.
