#10 Retrieval Augmented Generation AI doesn't become smart just because it uses an LLM. It becomes useful when we give it memory. That's where RAG comes in. Let me explain RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) in the simplest way possible. An LLM is like a very intelligent student who has read a lot of books… But, It doesn't know your company data, It doesn't know your documents, It doesn't know your database. If you ask, \"What is our refund policy from our internal handbook?\" The model has no idea. That’s where RAG helps. What is RAG? RAG = Search First Answer After Instead of letting AI guess (hallucination), we search the correct information -> give it to the AI -> AI writes the answer. So the AI no longer hallucinates, it answers from the real data. How RAG Works Step 1: Convert data into chunks and then into numbers (Generate Embeddings): All documents are converted into chunks and then vectors (number representations) so that machines can understand meaning (semantic search). Step 2: Store in a Vector Database These vectors are stored in systems like: FAISS, Pinecone, PgVector, etc. Step 3: User gives a query Example: \"Show me leads from last week who haven’t been contacted\" We generate the embeddings of this query. Step 4: Vector Search There are three types of vector search: 1. Dense Search Understands meaning \"Car\" = \"Vehicle\" Great for semantic similarity. 2. Sparse Search Keyword-based Exact word matches matter. 3. Hybrid Search Best of both worlds Meaning + keywords Most powerful for real systems. We may set the weightage of dense or sparse scores in hybrid sesrch by adjusting the value of alpha-> Hybrid score= alpha×dense score + (1- alpha)×sparse score Step 5: Optionally we may use a re-ranker to improve the search results. Step 6: Give results to the LLM We take the most relevant pieces of data and send them to the LLM with a prompt: \"Answer using ONLY the information below…\" Now the AI is grounded in facts. Step 7: AI Generates Final Answer The model has: • Correct context • Relevant data • Instructions The answer becomes: • More accurate • Less hallucinated • More useful for business Without RAG, AI is like general knowledge With RAG, AI becomes company brain It can answer about: • Your database • Your documents • Your customers • Your logs • Your systems That’s how AI moves from chatbot to intelligent assistant and that's how you make your business automated and go digital. Almost every serious AI system today uses some form of RAG. AI is not magic. It’s search + context + generation working together. Once you understand RAG, you understand how modern AI products are actually 🛑 WHY MOST ENTERPRISE AI PROJECTS FAIL (And how to fix it) 🛑

Terms like RAG, Semantic Layer, and Knowledge Graphs are the "buzzwords of the year." But why do they actually matter for your business?


To understand why these technical pieces are non-negotiable, let’s look at what happens when you build an AI without them—using an E-Commerce analogy. 🛒


1️⃣ Chunking: The Difference Between a Manual and a Search Bar

❌ The Con: If you store data as one massive document, the AI has to "read" the whole thing to find one fact. This leads to high costs, slow responses, and "lost in the middle" errors where the AI misses the most important detail.

✅ The Fix: We break data into "chunks" (Specs, FAQs, Reviews).

👉 Result: The AI finds the needle in the haystack instantly, saving time and compute costs.

2️⃣ Embeddings: Beyond Keyword Matching

❌ The Con: Traditional search is "dumb." If a customer searches for "inexpensive footwear" but your data only says "cheap shoes," a keyword-based AI will say "Out of Stock."

✅ The Fix: Embeddings understand the mathematical "closeness" of meaning.

👉 Result: Your AI understands that "low-cost," "affordable," and "budget-friendly" all mean the same thing, providing a human-like search experience.

3️⃣ RAG: Eliminating the "Creative" Assistant

❌ The Con: Without Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), if you ask about your 2024 refund policy, the AI might make up (hallucinate) an answer based on another company's policy it saw online.

✅ The Fix: RAG forces the AI to check YOUR verified catalog before it speaks.

👉 Result: No more hallucinations. Only fact-based, trustworthy answers.

4️⃣ Semantic Layer: Ending the "Metric War"

❌ The Con: Imagine if Marketing defines "Revenue" as gross sales, but Finance defines it as net profit. Your AI will give different answers depending on which table it looks at, destroying executive trust.

✅ The Fix: A Semantic Layer provides one "Logic Map" for the whole company.

👉 Result: Whether it’s a chatbot or a dashboard, "Revenue" always means the same number.

5️⃣ Knowledge Graph: Understanding Contextual Relationships

❌ The Con: Relational databases are bad at context. If a customer asks "Will this charger work with the phone I bought last week?", a basic AI struggles to link the User, the past Order, and the Product Compatibility.

✅ The Fix: A Knowledge Graph maps these relationships as a web.

👉 Result: The AI can reason through complex questions that involve multiple layers of business logic.



At Bodh Analytics, we specialize in building the architecture that prevents these common failures:

✅ Structured Chunking for speed.
✅ Semantic Layers for accuracy.
✅ RAG for trust.

Is your AI strategy addressing these "cons," or are you just building a fancy chatbot? Let’s talk about building a foundation that scales. 👇

Deze maand starten wij op ons hoofdkantoor in Sleeuwijk met een grootschalige verbouwing. Een deel van ons pand wordt gesloopt en maakt plaats voor een aanzienlijke uitbreiding van ons magazijn, een nieuwe technische dienst, een moderne showroom en een nieuwe kantine. Daarnaast krijgt het volledige interieur van ons pand een eigentijdse uitstraling. 

Naar verwachting wordt de verbouwing in juni 2027 afgerond. Tot die tijd doen wij er alles aan om onze bedrijfsprocessen met zo min mogelijk overlast te laten verlopen. Vanwege de werkzaamheden zullen er gedurende deze periode geen trainingen op onze locatie plaatsvinden. Uiteraard kunnen wij trainingen bij voldoende deelname op uw locatie of elders verzorgen. 

Het gebouw is ontworpen door TROVIS Architectuur en wordt gerealiseerd door Almbouw & Onderhoud B.V. Giessen. Het interieurontwerp is verzorgd door Studio Jesce.

Why do we see logarithms so much in probabilistic models?

Here's one of my favourite ways to explain how important logarithms are.  Probability is a multiplicative process.  When we try to determine the likelihood of a set of things happening, we often multiply their individual probabilities.  

But what happens when we multiply a set of random, normally distributed variables which have positive values less than 1?  We get a right-skewed distribution (first image).  

Maybe you remember from high school that the log of two multiplied variables is the SUM of their individual logs? So taking logs give us a way turn our multiplication into summation, which allows us to transform back to a nice unskewed normal distribution again (second image).  Much easier to model the logs and then transform back at the end.

If you want to learn more, I wrote a blog post about this here: https://lnkd.in/enPMcE2M

Scaling game-changing climate solutions requires more than just catalytic capital; it also requires credible climate intelligence.

Massachusetts Institute of Technology's new “Catalytic Capital Finance Project” highlights an important truth: many of the climate solutions with the greatest potential won’t scale on conventional investment terms alone.

They need catalytic capital. Capital that is deployed to absorb early risk, unlock innovation, and crowd in larger pools of private investment.

But here’s the challenge. Catalytic finance only works at scale if investors can credibly answer:

- What climate outcomes are we actually enabling?
- Which solutions deliver the greatest real-world impact?
- How do we compare opportunities consistently?
- Can we defend our decisions to our stakeholders?

This is exactly why climate intelligence infrastructure matters. And this is exactly why Koi.eco exists.

At Rho Impact, this work didn’t start with software. It started with shaping the field.

Rho Impact has led and contributed to emerging standards, frameworks, and initiatives focused on climate investing, including:

 - The CRANE Tool with the Prime Coalition 
 - Project Frame 
 - BearingPoint Point & Boston Consulting Group (BCG)’s Avoided Emissions Platform Initiative
 - CDP’s Emerging Climate Technology Framework

Koi.eco is built on that foundation.

Not as another black-box ESG score. But as decision-grade climate intelligence that helps investors, lenders, and institutions understand the carbon value and climate impact of their capital allocations. 

Because catalytic capital doesn’t just need ambition, it needs infrastructure trusted enough to move institutional capital. And that begins with Koi.eco.

Reach out to learn more or log on to Koi.eco to get started today!

Rho Impact. The new normal is already here. Let’s get to work.

⚠️ Something I see hiring leaders wrestling with more than they admit:

You’re being asked to hire at a high bar
while the organization is still figuring out what it actually needs.

The pressure isn’t talent quality.
It’s alignment.

Alignment on:

1. who truly owns the decision
2. which tradeoffs are acceptable
3. what “success” looks like 6–12 months after the hire

When that work doesn’t happen early, hiring leaders absorb the cost.

Searches extend.
Processes restart.
Credibility gets strained — internally and externally.

Not because anyone is careless.
But because clarity was assumed instead of established.

The strongest hiring leaders I work with don’t rush to open a search.
They slow things down just enough at the start to protect the outcome on the back end.

That discipline doesn’t delay results.
It prevents expensive missteps.

Discipline at the front end is what protects outcomes on the back end.

— Brett

PROJECT COMPLETED!

We are excited to announce the completion of the Save-A-Dog-Scheme Yarrambat Animal Welfare Facility!

McCorkell worked closely with SADS and Architecture Matters Pty Ltd for over twelve months to secure this project via an ECI procurement model which aided in resolving some of the specialist animal enclosure details.

The project involved partial demolition of the existing building and the construction of a brand-new canine facility to cater for 61 internal and external exercise pens, including a dog wash, utility and food preparation room, covered walkway, and stair access.

One of the project features is the unique suspended concrete floor slab, which was expertly crafted to achieve the complex and fine tolerances specified for individual kennel separation, set down, and fall to waste requirements.

Now the new facility has been built, SADS will be able to operate Yarrambat in conjunction with their current headquarters in Glen Iris and significantly expand SADS’ capacity to save more animals.

Well done and thank you to all involved!

\"Entry-Level\" Paradox. Entry Level: 3 to 5 years of experience required. It is a phrase seen on almost every job board today. It is a contradiction that is quietly stalling the careers of a whole generation of talent. If an \"Entry Level\" role requires three years of experience, the goal isn't to find a junior. The goal is to find a senior professional who is willing to be underpaid. This isn't just a formatting error in a job description. It is a gatekeeping mechanism. It tells the hungry, the capable, and the newly qualified that the door is locked until they somehow find a way to get experience that no one is willing to provide. Why did \"Entry Level\" stop meaning \"Entry Level\"? The shift likely comes from a place of fear, the fear of the \"time-cost\" of training. There is a corporate obsession with immediate ROI. The preference is for a \"plug-and-play\" employee who knows the software, the jargon, and the internal politics from day one. But this short-term gain has a heavy long-term cost. By refusing to invest in \"unpolished\" candidates, industries are essentially eating their own seed corn. The pipeline of future leaders is drying up because the bottom rungs of the ladder have been removed. The result? Senior staff are burned out doing tasks that a junior could easily handle, while talented newcomers are stuck in a loop of \"no experience, no job.\" Hiring for \"potential\" has been replaced by hiring for \"proven history.\" But history has to start somewhere. True leadership isn't just about managing current success; it’s about having the courage to build the talent of tomorrow. It is time to stop the experience paradox and actually open the door. 🌱 Why Hiring Entry-Level Talent Can Be a Game-Changer 🌱
Many companies focus on experience, but hiring entry-level employees comes with unique advantages:
✅ Fresh Energy & Motivation – They’re eager to learn, contribute, and prove themselves.
✅ Adaptable & Open-Minded – They can be trained to fit the company culture and adopt new technologies quickly.
✅ Innovative Perspectives – Without preconceived habits, they bring creative ideas and challenge outdated processes.
✅ Cost-Effective & Long-Term Investment – Lower starting salaries, with high potential for loyalty and growth within the organization.
💡 Experienced employees help you succeed today. Entry-level employees help you grow for tomorrow.
If you’re a company looking to build the future workforce, don’t underestimate the power of starting with talent that’s ready to learn and evolve.

When Geoffrey Hinton said in 2016 that “people should stop training radiologists,” it sounded like an inevitable prophecy.

Nine years later, the opposite happened:

🔸 Radiology residency positions reached a record high.
🔸 Salaries increased by 48%.
🔸 And the volume of imaging studies keeps growing.

The truth is that AI hasn’t replaced radiology — it has expanded it.
Triage models speed up workflows, algorithms prioritize critical cases, and assistive tools reduce errors.

But the final diagnosis still requires a human eye — informed, empathetic, and contextual.
The future isn’t AI vs Human, but AI + Human.

And that balance depends on trustworthy data, interoperability, and an ethical vision of progress.

post_text: Pom Strauss ‘25 spent the past three years developing a protein delivery system to make antibiotics work better. Using a method called cell-free protein synthesis, she was able to produce proteins involved in antibiotic transport and insert them into liposomes that make it easier for antibiotics to get inside the bacteria and do their job. Her work could help combat antibiotic resistance, leading to better treatments for infections that no longer respond to standard medicine. Working in the Daniel lab as an undergraduate researcher allowed Pom to further develop her collaboration, problem-solving, and technical skills in a welcoming and interdisciplinary environment. “When I first began, the techniques I now use daily were entirely new and quite confusing. Over time, I've become much more comfortable in the lab environment and have learned to problem-solve on the spot when things don't go as planned,” Pom said. Using a method called cell-free protein synthesis, she was able to produce proteins involved in antibiotic transport and insert them into liposomes that make it easier for antibiotics to get inside the bacteria and do their job. Her work could help combat antibiotic resistance, leading to better treatments for infections that no longer respond to standard medicine.

Working in the Daniel lab as an undergraduate researcher allowed Pom to further develop her collaboration, problem-solving, and technical skills in a welcoming and interdisciplinary environment. “When I first began, the techniques I now use daily were entirely new and quite confusing. Over time, I've become much more comfortable in the lab environment and have learned to problem-solve on the spot when things don't go as planned,” Pom said.

Seven years ago, we incorporated KlariVis.

I could tell you about launching an MVP right before a pandemic. About the sleepless nights and the moments we weren’t sure we’d make it.

But when I think about what these seven years actually mean, it’s not the milestones.

It’s the people.

The founding team—four bankers who left successful careers to solve a problem we’d lived, even though we had no idea how to build software. Still here. Still building. The ones who joined the mission along the way and made it theirs. The bank partners who took a chance on us and pushed us to be better.

Our clients aren’t just clients. They are partners. They show up. They cheer us on. They make us better. They’re invested in our success the way we’re invested in theirs.

This is the work I was meant to do. I’ve never been more sure of it.

Huge shoutout to the our early believers and adopters- Thank you!! 💜

post_text:
Almost lost everything because of that



For a long time, I said “yes” to everything. Every opportunity, every request, every new idea. It felt productive, but it was pulling me away from what truly mattered. Letting go wasn’t easy, it felt uncomfortable at first. But it was the only way to get real work done.

Focus isn’t just about what you choose to do. It’s about what you’re willing to let go of. Doing less but doing it well creates clarity and momentum, and that is the real driven of growth. 
The noise doesn’t disappear, but when you let go of it, you give yourself room to move forward.

post_text: Actabl , the leading hospitality software company, has appointed Joseph Benjamin as its new 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗲𝗳 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗲𝗿 (𝗖𝗧𝗢). In this role, Joseph will drive Actabl’s global technology strategy, focusing on platform integration, innovation, and data-driven solutions that empower hotels worldwide. With over 30 years of technology leadership, Joseph has scaled startups and global enterprises. Most recently, as CTO at iCIMS , he led a 430-person team across engineering, security, cloud operations, and IT, optimizing $40M in cloud infrastructure. He also served as Chief Product & Technology Officer at Behavox , where he tripled revenue in three years, and as founding CTO of Oracle | Datalogix , which was acquired by Oracle for $1.2B. At Oracle Data Cloud, Joseph scaled engineering to 730 people, supporting $500M+ in revenue. His diverse career includes roles at IBM , Netidentity , Olera Software, and advising multiple tech ventures. This appointment marks a pivotal moment as Actabl continues to innovate at the core of hospitality transformation, delivering integrated solutions that simplify operations and unlock value for hotel brands worldwide. Investors are increasingly focused on healthtech platforms with recurring revenues, modular product design, and strong clinical relevance. Now besides the obvious the thing just doesn’t work (meaning discovery and customer insights weren’t gained….do not pass go, do not collect $200) most healthtech pilots don’t fail on product issues alone — they fail because of procurement tempo. The startup runs on venture time. The buyer (healthcare systems) runs on budget cycles, legal review, InfoSec, and committee time. That mismatch quietly kills more good technology than bad science ever will. The solution isn’t “faster demos.” I think it’s more along the lines of adaptive procurement — aligning proof and payment in real time. 👉 Short, milestone-based sprints 👉 Parallel security and compliance reviews 👉 Outcome-based triggers that release the next tranche of funds automatically 👉 Pre-priced expansion ladders (pilot → ward → enterprise) We’re exploring this in depth at #HLTH2025 next week as part of our work at the University City Science Center — especially as federal instability pushes more responsibility for commercialization and adoption onto state and private innovation engines. 🔹 If you’re attending HLTH ( #hlthusa ), stop by the Science Center booth or DM me to connect. 🔹 We’re building a community of partners to co-develop an adaptive procurement framework that can actually move pilots to scalable adoption. Actabl, the leading hospitality software company, has appointed Joseph Benjamin as its new 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗲𝗳 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗲𝗿 (𝗖𝗧𝗢). In this role, Joseph will drive Actabl’s global technology strategy, focusing on platform integration, innovation, and data-driven solutions that empower hotels worldwide.
With over 30 years of technology leadership, Joseph has scaled startups and global enterprises. Most recently, as CTO at iCIMS, he led a 430-person team across engineering, security, cloud operations, and IT, optimizing $40M in cloud infrastructure. He also served as Chief Product & Technology Officer at Behavox, where he tripled revenue in three years, and as founding CTO of Oracle | Datalogix, which was acquired by Oracle for $1.2B.
At Oracle Data Cloud, Joseph scaled engineering to 730 people, supporting $500M+ in revenue. His diverse career includes roles at IBM, Netidentity, Olera Software, and advising multiple tech ventures.
This appointment marks a pivotal moment as Actabl continues to innovate at the core of hospitality transformation, delivering integrated solutions that simplify operations and unlock value for hotel brands worldwide.

post_text: When I used to be an equity analyst (sounds like the beginning of a fairy tale), the most difficult part of my life was coverage. There were just too many stocks, there was this little brain of me and a limited understanding of how things work. The good thing about quantitative research is that it is like a software product. You can create a module and then plug and play in different markets. It is so easy. It is, isn’t it? I think it is. Last year was a breakthrough for me in trying out different ways of implementing quantitative strategies. It is not that I was not doing it earlier. The issue was to do with implementation and rules. It is like this. Say for example, you are running a mid cap strategy. What if a stock that you selected does well and becomes a large cap stock? As per general rules of indexing or passive investing or rule-based trading, you would let go of the stock. But why would you do that? Is the reason only it moving from one size segment to another? But that is stupid. So the new approach says that you hold it till it fulfils all other criteria and ideally, it should be preferred over other stocks. It is like not attempting a question in the examination even if you know the solution, only because it was not in the ‘prescribed syllabus’. There are no such rules in the market. Or better still, you make those rules in the market. And if it works, it works. Going back to the topic of GARP investing, 2018 was a challenging year more so because growth as a factor did not fare well. The main reason was that most investors globally were looking for safety stocks and in spite of the low valuation as compared to their growth rates, GARP stocks did not provide that kind of comfort to the investor. Therefore, the focus was on less volatile stocks. The focus was more on preserving your returns from the previous year rather than losing it on your chosen strategy. Further on that, I tried to run similar strategies in other markets. Till now, I have attempted US, Japan and China. I have been looking to do more but for each of these new markets, I have to go back and clean the underlying data and all this in the middle of the normal work that I continue doing. Some part laziness, some part a paucity of time. From the numbers, it works fairly well for India, China or USA but not so much for Japan. It makes sense because Japan has not been a growth market for ages. Even momentum doesn’t work there well. It is understandable. Frankly, I would be scared exploring many strategies in Japan. It works so well for emerging markets because growth as a factor works much better, or it used to be much better in pre-GFC periods than it is now. PS: I have not updated my dataset for China. I will add a bit more on that later. And I will step back from GARPing for a bit and explore other strategies.

post_text: Losing a job—especially one rooted in service—can feel like the ground has disappeared beneath you. If you're one of the many federal employees facing this unexpected shift, I see you. The work you’ve done still matters. Your experience still holds value. And while nothing replaces human resilience and community, AI can help steady your next steps. But let’s be clear: AI is a tool, not the driver. Think of it as your sidekick, not your replacement. You are still the one making decisions, telling your story, and shaping your next chapter. AI can help smooth the way—but it’s your authenticity, experience, and skills that will open doors. How AI Can Support You—While You Stay in Control 1 | Strengthen Your Resume & Cover Letter AI can help refine and tailor your resume to match job descriptions so it gets past screening filters. But it should enhance your voice, not replace it. Always review AI suggestions to ensure they reflect your experience authentically. AI Tools to Try: ChatGPT – Paste a job description and ask, "How can I adjust my resume to match this role?" Jobscan – Upload your resume and compare it against job postings for keyword alignment. 2 | Find the Right Job Faster Instead of endless scrolling, AI-powered job platforms can suggest roles based on your experience. But you set the direction. AI helps with efficiency, but only you know which roles truly align with your goals. AI Tools to Try: LinkedIn’s AI Job Matching – Click “Easy Apply” jobs that match your profile. Rezi – Creates AI-assisted resumes and job search tools to match you with opportunities. 3 | Prepare for Interviews with AI Coaching Speaking about yourself can be tough. AI can help you practice, but confidence comes from within. Don’t over-rehearse; let AI refine your talking points while keeping your responses natural. AI Tools to Try: Yoodli – Analyzes your speech, pace, and tone to refine your responses. ChatGPT – Ask, “What are common interview questions for [your role]?” and practice answers. 4 | Reconnect & Network Authentically Your next opportunity may come from a conversation. AI can help craft outreach messages, but genuine connection matters most. Let AI help you get started, but make each message personal. AI Tools to Try: ChatGPT – Ask, “Help me write a LinkedIn message to reconnect with a former colleague.” Post on LinkedIn – Share your experience, what you’re looking for, and how your network can help. AI can help shape your message. 5 | Upskill & Explore New Paths If this is a time to grow or pivot, AI-powered learning platforms can help. But choose skills that truly interest you, not just what’s trending. AI Tools to Try: Coursera & LinkedIn Learning – AI suggests courses based on your interests. Google’s AI-Powered Career Certificates – Learn in-demand skills with employer recognition. 6 | Stay Organized & Focused Job searching is a job in itself. AI can help keep you on track, but you decide what matters most. AI Tools to Try: Notion AI – Organizes your job search, application deadlines, and to-do lists. Otter.ai – Transcribes networking conversations and interviews so you can focus on the discussion. Authenticity Over Automation AI can speed up the process, but it can’t replace your story, your passion, or your unique value. Use it to enhance your message, but make sure every application, post, and conversation still sounds like you. Best Practices for Using AI Without Losing Your Voice: ✅ Use AI for structure, but rewrite in your own words. ✅ Be human—share your personality, values, and insights. ✅ Review and edit AI-generated content to ensure accuracy and authenticity. ✅ Trust your instincts—if something feels off, adjust it. 💬 If AI feels overwhelming, start small. Even using it to refine a resume bullet point or draft a LinkedIn post can make a difference. You don’t have to master it—just let it assist. Let’s Support Each Other If you know of job openings, resources, or advice that might help, drop them in the comments. A small act of connection could lead to someone’s next opportunity. This is a hard moment. But it’s not the end—it’s a shift. You are still the hero of your story. AI is just your sidekick. If I can help connect you to opportunities or resources, reach out. And if you’re hiring, look toward this incredible pool of dedicated professionals. #CareerTransitions #AIForJobSearch #Resilience #NextSteps

VASP: The New Frontline of AML, CFT and CPF in the Crypto Economy Crypto is no longer operating on the sidelines. Today, Virtual Asset Service Providers or VASPs sit at the center of financial crime prevention. A VASP is any business that handles, transfers, exchanges, or safeguards virtual assets on behalf of customers. That simple idea changes everything. It places crypto firmly inside the global regulatory perimeter. 🧭 What Do VASPs Actually Do A business is considered a VASP if it performs any of the following activities. 💱 Exchange virtual assets with fiat currencies 🔄 Exchange one virtual asset with another 📤 Transfer virtual assets between wallets or accounts 🔐 Safekeep or administer customer assets through custodial wallets 🚀 Support the issuance or sale of virtual assets such as token offerings If a platform can control customer funds or influence transactions, regulators treat it as a VASP. 🚨 Why Regulators Are Paying Attention VASPs operate at the entry and exit points of the financial system. This makes them vulnerable to misuse for ⚠️ Money laundering ⚠️ Terrorist financing ⚠️ Sanctions evasion ⚠️ Proliferation financing This is exactly why FATF brought VASPs under AML, CFT and CPF obligations. 🛡️ What Compliance Means for VASPs ✅ AML Customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence Ongoing transaction monitoring Suspicious transaction reporting Strong record keeping and audit trails ✅ CFT Terrorist list screening Monitoring fast and cross border transfers Immediate freezing of designated assets ✅ CPF Targeted financial sanctions compliance Wallet and counterparty screening Prevention of crypto based sanctions evasion 📌 The Travel Rule applies Sender and beneficiary information must travel with virtual asset transfers. ⚖️ What This Really Means Crypto is no longer a regulatory grey zone. VASPs are expected to meet the same level of governance and accountability as traditional financial institutions. Weak compliance does not just bring penalties. It puts licenses, reputation, and financial stability at risk. 💡 One Thought to Remember If AML controls fail at VASPs, the entire financial system becomes exposed. Strong compliance does not kill innovation. Stablecoins are digital tokens meant to maintain a steady value often tied to something like the U.S. dollar. Tech Challenges Add Complexity Stablecoins often move across multiple blockchains — so simply tracking transactions can be harder than with traditional finance. In 2025, regulators and law-enforcement agencies worldwide placed unprecedented focus on cryptocurrency firms, issuing record setting AML/CFT and sanctions enforcement actions across exchanges, payment providers, and crypto adjacent platforms.

Billions in penalties, license actions, and criminal investigations signaled a clear shift:

Crypto is no longer viewed as an emerging edge case, it is now treated as core financial infrastructure subject to the same expectations as traditional banking.

➡️But this enforcement wave isn’t just about compliance failures.

It reflects a broader reality: digital assets are now central to fraud, ransomware, sanctions evasion, and organized crime, and governments are responding by tightening oversight while demanding stronger investigative and recovery capabilities.

At 𝗖𝗮𝘁 𝗟𝗮𝗯𝘀, we see this trend firsthand. AML/CFT enforcement is increasingly intersecting with blockchain forensics, asset tracing, and recovery operations, requiring collaboration between regulators, financial institutions, and law-enforcement agencies.

➡️ The message from 2025 is clear:

Understanding crypto risk is no longer optional, it’s operationally essential.

post_text: There’s a quote used by Abraham Lincoln before becoming President of the United States, which reads ”This too shall pass”. The #Coronavirus will pass, it is true, but the question we must ask ourselves is: how will the day after be like? This pandemic is not a parenthesis, it is not a pause. It is a CTRL + ALT + DEL of the world as we used to experience it every day: work, family life, globalization, relationships, what matters and what doesn't, the economy ... In 2018, just two years ago, we could fearfully imagine that the fights over power between the world's strongest nations and their highly irrational leaders could, with a certain degree of logic, lead us to a war that no thinking human being on this earth would want to experience. But reading an article called New World, Same Humans I realized that what actually ended up happening could not have been imagined by a science fiction scriptwriter. Things like, for example, ultra-right leaders like Boris Johnson or Donald Trump embracing the most socialist move that a capitalist mind could have ever imagined: giving money away. The great difference between this #crisis and any other that we have experienced is that this one affected all of us equally, and also that the end will be very different from the beginning. The world stopped, a "microscopic bug" invited us to take a shower of humility, transforming what we believed to be progress (globalization, life expectancy, etc.) into a huge challenge, for better and for worse. Some of the immediate changes we saw were: Airplanes around the world had to travel without passengers and park without departure dates at airport hangars Health personnel became the best Army of any country, armed with masks and respirators Not being able to accompany and dismiss our loved ones during their last moments Parents and children found themselves reunited at home, for the first time having to interact 24/7 without being on vacation Marriages were suddenly confined to fidelity, having to understand each other or else facing the dissolution they were somehow trying to avoid Social distancing led us to try to avoid getting close to another person, much less shake hands or kiss to greet them Millions of people around the world desperately rushed to supermarkets to buy the most illogical of all items: toilet paper, demonstrating the emotional vulnerability of human beings For many years I managed major business crises: plane crashes, financial crises, product recalls, oil spills, and countless other crises. The difference? It was a matter of time. Even the worst crises, such as a plane crash that causes great pain and shock, not only in families but also on the airline, after a while it returns to normal. However, now the question we should ask ourselves is what will the new normal be? Will it be necessary for us to reinvent 90% of business models? Time for the Great #Reset (personal, professional and business) 8 years ago we created a program called #ResetyourLife because we believe that everyone reaches a moment in their life that has to rethink what they want, what they do, whom they do it with, what they do it for ... Today we are not only faced with a different reality personally but also professionally: layoffs, salary reductions and of course, all working from home with immense uncertainty, confinement, and fear. From the business point of view, in many cases, business continuity is in question. This is not only applicable to traditional companies, but also to new and exponential companies like Airbnb or Uber. The day after #Coronavirus we don't know when it will be. What we do know is that it will come full of opportunities and challenges because there are countless new problems to solve. From the world's health systems to the millions of people and companies that will have been left out of the game or the millions of children who will have missed a school year due to not having computers or access to the Internet. The history of evolution shows us that the species that have the ability to adapt quickly are the ones that survive. Today #leadership is seriously questioned because it will not be the traditional #CEOs that manage the resources of a company that lead the future of organizations, but those with the ability to innovate, re-invent and lead their employees and clients in the reinvention process. post_text: Introduction While supporting foreign investors in their activities in Poland, we can observe five major drivers that compel many of these investors to enter the Polish market or expand their operations in this country. While in earlier years Poland was primarily considered as a well-located, low-cost production base for Western Europe, more recently many investors are attracted firstly by Poland’s large population, its steadily growing economy and its rising middle class. Poland seems to be establishing itself as one of the EU’s “Big 6” markets, especially in the eyes of investors from outside Europe. Naturally, the original attractions still stand. Poland remains centrally located at the heart of the New Europe, linking Western EU markets with resource-rich countries like Russia or Ukraine. Land is still amply available at relatively low cost. The labour force is no longer sought after only in terms of cost levels, but also as it's considered highly skilled, hard working and reliable. The Polish authorities are mostly appreciated for their steady and supportive policy towards foreign investors, although executives mention that red tape should be cut further. Last but not least, many investors are keen to take advantage of the truly massive flow of EU funds towards the Polish economy and especially its infrastructure. Poland has been allocated more than € 105 billion in EU funds for the 2014-2020 period, by far the largest amount of all member states. Nevertheless, investors need to be aware of a number of challenges that are common to most transition economies in the region, including Poland. Although property rights and transparency are deemed relatively strong compared to other countries in CEE, institutional risks still exist, albeit mostly at a local level. While EU membership is gradually bringing stability, legislation is still changing relatively rapidly and is sometimes inconsistently applied. Legal procedures can be inefficient and the administrative requirements for setting up a company or doing business remain cumbersome, although improvements are being noted. Furthermore, the accessibility, timeliness and robustness of financial and commercial information are not always up to international standards, and the condition of plant and equipment should be carefully considered. Infrastructure quality can also vary and local supply chain limitations can be a challenge for some foreign investors. Given Poland’s attractive opportunities and strong underlying fundamentals, it is no surprise that many companies are considering expanding into the Polish market. Although the country’s appeal is justified by many factors, any entry does require comprehensive research, due diligence and planning. While the investment prospects may be attractive, decisions made now can have enduring consequences. Whether you are considering an acquisition, a Greenfield investment or a restructuring, you need to understand the strategic and financial impact of your decisions as well as the implementation risks. Understanding where the opportunities and risks lie, the size of each opportunity and what competitors are doing will arm you with the confidence to make a sound investment decision. Large domestic market with good growth prospects As the largest economy to join the European Union (EU) over the last decade, Poland’s combination of sustained growth with economic and political stability is drawing a great deal of interest from around the world. Fuelled by the growing number of middle-income consumers and a wave of infrastructure investments, the economic environment has blossomed. While Poland features among Europe’s growing economies, with some 38 million inhabitants it is also becoming one of the EU’s six biggest markets. Moreover, Poland accounts for four of the largest urban areas in Central & Eastern Europe, including Warsaw (3.3 million inhabitants), Katowice (2.8 million), Cracow (1.5 million) and Gdansk Tri-city (1.3 million). Poland’s economy, measured in GDP, has grown to become larger than those of Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary combined, and accounts for more than one-third of the total GDP of CEE. Based on information from the World Bank, GDP per capita for 2012 was roughly € 17,300 and has reached 66% of the EU average. Poland has been a leading economic performer in the region since 2005, with annual GDP growth rates ranging between 3.6% and 6.8% in most years. In 2009 it was the only economy in the EU to show positive GDP growth, and it grew by 3.9% in 2010 and 4.3% in 2011. Growth cooled in 2012 and 2013 to 1.9% and 1.6% amidst a renewed Euro-zone dip. However, more recent projections point to a rebound in growth which, according to the European Commission, could reach 3.2% and 3.4% in 2014 and 2015 respectively. According to the latest IMF forecast, Poland’s economy is expected to continue to outperform the majority of its regional peers in terms of GDP development with a projected annual growth rate of 3.5% in the 2014-2019 period. The Wall Street Journal (31/5/2012)explained Poland’s position among neighbouring CEE countries as follows: “ …Poland is a bright spot compared with Hungary and the Czech Republic… as robust domestic consumption and rising exports helped the country escape the fate of others in Central and Eastern Europe dragged down by the troubles in the neighbouring Euro zone. ” Poland has a large and steadily growing number of middle-income consumers with increasing disposable income. Upper- and middle income groups (earning a gross monthly income above PLN 3,100), currently at 2.7 million, are expected to surpass the 3 million milestone by 2015. Total disposable income in Poland grew at over 7% per annum before the financial crisis, and continued to show notable growth even over the 2009-2012 period, while according to EIU projections, the rate of growth is picking up in the next few years to over 5% per year. Disposable income of upper- and middle income groups is growing at above average rates, with the EIU forecasting over 6% per annum. However, although disposable incomes are growing, they still have a long way to catch up to Western European levels, particularly in rural areas where more than a third of the Polish population lives. Poland is not burdened by excessive debt and government debt levels are constitutionally capped. The inflation rate was 3.7% in 2012 and slowed to 0.9% in 2013, while the reference interest rate stood at 2.5%, allowing the government to pursue mildly expansionist policies. The Polish banking system has proved relatively resistant to the recent global financial crisis and did not require any financial support from the state. So strong have been the fundamentals and so steady the growth of the Polish economy that Barclays Capital featured it on its global list of 10 Advanced Emerging Markets – economies graduating from emerging market status, with risks similar to developed nations paired with the higher returns that are typical of emerging markets. Location at the heart of Europe Poland is well located, both as a nearby manufacturing base for many companies from Germany and the Benelux, but also as a natural east-west corridor in northern Europe, linking North Sea ports with the resource-rich former Soviet states. Poland’s infrastructure is still underdeveloped when compared to other EU countries. This can be viewed both as a challenge and an opportunity. The situation has been improving gradually from the start of the new millennium, especially after Poland joined the European Union. Of the €67 billion of EU funds allocated to Poland for 2007-2013, as much as €20 billion was allocated for immediate priorities relating to transportation infrastructure. Moreover, a large portion of funds related to Regional Operational Programmes has been spent on infrastructure investment at the regional and local levels. Between 2011 and November 2012, approximately 1,116 km of major roads and city bypasses had been built, with over PLN 21 billion being spent in 2012 on highway projects. According to official statistics from the Polish Ministry of Transport, about 1,657 km of railways were put into use between 2011 and 2012. Poland’s IT infrastructure is also rapidly being upgraded and can compete with its peers in Europe. For example, the Polish Internet eXchange, the world’s 12th-largest Internet Exchange Point in terms of maximum throughput, is located in Warsaw. Poland’s solid economy and funding from the EU allow Poland to invest heavily in improving the transport and energy infrastructure throughout the country in the coming years. High skill – low cost labour Labour costs in Poland remain substantially lower than in Western Europe, but also lie below those in, for example, Czech Republic or Hungary. According to statistics published by the European Commission, the total hourly labour costs in Euro increased by 1.4% in 2012 compared to 2011. This outperformed not only the EU as a whole (1.7%) but in particular neighbouring Czech Republic (1.9%), Slovakia (2.5%), Hungary (2.7%) and Romania (4.8%). Redundancy costs also compare favourably with most European markets. However, foreign and local investors alike frequently state that labour laws are unnecessarily complicated and at the same time often strictly implemented. Issues mentioned include the definition of working hours being unclear, sick leave regulations and excessive paperwork. Labour is relatively highly qualified, above the EU average. Poland ranks in the top three in CEE in terms of tertiary education enrolment rates, with 18% of people between the ages of 15 and 64 having completed some form of higher education. Poland also has one of the lowest dropout rates in Europe, with approximately 4.5% of the population aged 18-24 not enrolled in some form of primary or vocational programme – compared to the EU average of 12.8%. Foreign investors tend to praise the Polish labour force for its craftsmanship and dedication. A Japanese executive I recently spoke with put it aptly: “The technical skills of Polish employees are very developed, to the point that they are comparable to those of Germans”. On the other hand, investors point out that foreign language skills are sometimes limited, especially outside the major cities. The Polish worker ranks among the most productive in all of Europe. According to data published by Eurostat, Poland is a leader in CEE in terms of real labour productivity, measured as real output per unit of labour input. Poland is also the only country in all of Europe that has maintained a continuous increasing trend in productivity since 2009. Steady and supportive authorities The international companies I have worked with often praise Poland’s authorities as steady and investor-friendly. The government is seen as solid, equitable and genuinely pro-business. It is interesting to observe that Polish law and tax regulations, which are commonly criticised by Polish entrepreneurs and perceived as complicated and unclear, are not an insuperable obstacle for many investors from abroad; on the contrary they are seen as stable and fair. In addition, the foreign investment agency PAIiIZ is considered helpful in building bridges with the relevant authorities. Data from international institutes such as the World Economic Forum confirms that Poland consistently features among the better performers in the CEE region on institutional strength and transparency. Moreover, the country recently rose in the World Bank’s Ease of Doing Business ranking to 33rd place, ahead not only of Slovakia, Czech Republic and Hungary, but also of Belgium. Nevertheless, foreign investors frequently complain about red tape and bureaucracy, for example in customs clearance procedures, or redundant paperwork for tenders, and that all formal communication must be in the local language. EU funds The EU promotes the balanced development of its member countries, and of the 28 member countries, the EU has contributed the most subsidies to Poland. Between 2007 and 2013, the EU allocated 38% of all CEE structural and cohesion funds to Poland. From 2014 to 2020, the EU is to increase the amount contributed to Poland to more than €105 billion, of which over €82 billion in structural and cohesion funds. The EU funds are likely to be designated not only to infrastructural works, but also to support entrepreneurship, innovativeness, R&D, training and other areas. Besides EU funds, the Polish authorities offer a pool of diverse incentives for investors, depending on the type of business, the scale of operations as well as the location of the investment. Prime among such mechanisms designed to support FDI are the Special Economic Zones (SEZ). SEZs are separate parts of the country’s territory where business activity can be conducted under preferential conditions. The main benefit of investing in an SEZ is the possibility of obtaining a corporate or personal income tax exemption. Investors can also obtain real estate tax exemptions granted by local authorities. The tax exemptions for the companies operating within an SEZ are a form of EU-approved state aid. Public incentives in SEZs can also go toward the cost of two years’ employment for newly hired employees. The above support is classified as regional aid and can be cumulated with other forms of state aid such as EU- or state-funded grants. Currently there are 14 SEZs in Poland, covering an area of over 15,000 ha. In 2013 the Government decided to extend the SEZ arrangement from 2020 to 2026. Investment projects may combine different incentive sources, which require additional negotiations which have to be coordinated with the relevant authorities. At the same time, there are maximum aid limits which differ by region. In Poland, the grants and incentives are allocated on a competitive basis, hence it is crucial to prepare your application well. Conclusion: Why invest in Poland now? Whereas most of Europe has been in the doldrums over the last five years, Poland has gained much traction. We can observe that, while inward investment from Europe was slowing, US and Asian investors have made strong inroads into the country. Privatisation is still going strong and the country is awaiting the next wave of infrastructure investment. EU membership is driving the modernisation of institutions, the legal environment as well as business culture, but good professional advice grounded in local experience is required in getting Poland right. All told, Poland is a large and attractive market with a growing middle class, which has withstood the economic crisis well and is receiving over €105 billion in EU funds. Labour is highly skilled, increasingly productive and remains relatively cheap. There are not many countries presenting such a great opportunity at less than a day’s drive from the EU’s core markets.

The leaders who create the strongest cultures aren’t perfect. They’re the ones who balance confidence with humility: proud of their strengths, honest about their growth areas, and willing to be fully present with their teams. Attention is a choice. Today was the first in person PVHO meeting I've been to in a few years. It did not go quite the way I expected. 15 years ago I brought up the need to address software safety but was told to not open that can of worms. I've poked at it here and there over the years, but not too hard because there was a lot of push back. Today I went in with my Japanese fighting beetle pin over my heart, looking to pick a fight. I walked out as the Chair of PVHO 1, Section 3 for Quality Assurance with a resounding "AYE!" I was stunned but also humbled by the trust the ASME PVHO comittee members have in me to do the job.

The group has been in mothballs for years with no chair or members. There's a lot of work to be done to bring it up to date, to include addressing all the aspects of software safety and security that currently affect the hyperbaric and diving industries. I fully expect the work to be messy and contentious. It wouldn't be Codes and Standards if it weren't.

I am thrilled to announce the next phase of the #BeyondtheBag Initiative alongside Target, CVS Health, Kroger, Dollar Tree Stores, Family Dollar, Meijer, and Walmart!

The blueprint for our strategy to eliminate single-use bag waste can be found in our recently released report, Sparking a National Culture Shift to Reduce Plastic Bag Waste, which shares the learnings and impact from our 2023 Bring Your Own Bag Pilot. The pilot engaged 160 retailers and 375+ stores of all sizes across Denver, Colorado, and Tucson, Arizona, implementing messaging across the customer service journey to encourage shoppers to bring their own bag or not use a bag at all. The campaign eliminated up to 9.5 million bags across the two test markets, reducing plastic waste and creating operational savings for our retail partners.

Both initiatives demonstrate the opportunity and impact of collaboration and a systems approach to drive waste reduction, and we’re excited to prove our strategy in the next phase of the #BeyondtheBag Initiative.

Please reach out if you’re interested in learning more, as it truly takes a team to scale systems change, and thanks to our collaborative group of retailers and partners now and over the past four years (“our team”) who have helped make this impact and the next phase come to life!

Read the report here: https://lnkd.in/ejpjCeKd

post_text: In the rapidly evolving landscape of digital marketing, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force, especially in the realm of content creation. From crafting compelling articles to generating engaging social media posts and persuasive ad copy, AI tools are reshaping the way brands communicate with their audiences. This revolution in brand messaging is not just about automation; it's about creating more personalized, relevant, and dynamic content at scale. Here, we explore the facets of AI-powered content creation and how it's changing the game for marketers and content creators alike. The Dawn of AI in Content Creation AI in content creation utilizes sophisticated algorithms to generate text-based content. These AI models, trained on vast datasets of human-generated text, can produce a wide variety of content that ranges from informative articles to creative ad copy. Tools like GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) have been at the forefront, offering capabilities that were once thought to be exclusively within the human domain. Unveiling the Benefits Enhanced Efficiency and Productivity One of the most significant advantages of AI-powered content creation is its efficiency. AI tools can generate drafts, suggest edits, and even produce ready-to-publish content much faster than human writers. This speed does not just save time; it allows content creators to focus on strategic tasks such as content planning and audience engagement, thereby increasing overall productivity. Scalability of Content Production For brands looking to maintain a robust online presence, the demand for fresh content can be overwhelming. AI steps in as a scalable solution, capable of producing large volumes of content tailored to various platforms and audience segments. This scalability ensures that brands can keep up with the content demands of their marketing strategies without compromising on quality. Personalization at Scale AI's ability to analyze data and understand audience preferences is unparalleled. By leveraging AI, brands can create content that resonates with different segments of their target audience, enhancing the personalization of their messaging. This tailored approach not only improves engagement rates but also builds a stronger connection between the brand and its consumers. Creativity and Innovation While AI might not replace human creativity, it certainly can enhance it. AI tools offer new ways to approach content creation, from generating unique ideas to suggesting improvements in tone and style. By providing a fresh perspective, AI can inspire human creators to innovate and experiment with their content strategies. The Future of Brand Messaging As AI technology continues to advance, its integration into content creation will become more seamless and sophisticated. We can expect AI to offer even more personalized and interactive content solutions, such as dynamic content that adapts to real-time audience interactions. Moreover, ethical considerations and the need for a human touch will shape how AI is used, ensuring that content remains authentic and true to the brand's voice. Conclusion AI-powered content creation is revolutionizing brand messaging by offering unparalleled efficiency, scalability, personalization, and opportunities for innovation. As brands navigate the challenges of the digital age, AI stands out as a crucial ally, enabling them to communicate more effectively with their audiences and stay ahead in the competitive landscape. However, the successful integration of AI in content strategies will depend on finding the right balance between technological capabilities and the irreplaceable value of human insight and creativity.

🚀 Want to Stand Out in Web Development? Master Node.js! 🚀

Here’s the deal: If you're serious about a high-impact career in web development, Node.js is your ticket. 🌐 Whether you’re just getting started or leveling up, mastering Node.js opens the door to real-time, scalable, and lightning-fast applications.

So, What Exactly is Node.js?

Node.js lets you use JavaScript — yes, the same JavaScript you use in the browser — to create full-blown server applications. Think of it as JavaScript for the backend! 🚀

But Here’s the Twist:- Unlike regular JavaScript, which is all about the frontend, Node.js runs on the server. This means you can handle data processing, database access, and heavy backend tasks all using one language.

How Node.js Works (Without the Tech Jargon) :

Node.js is different because it’s single-threaded and non-blocking. Instead of waiting for things to load (like a database), Node.js moves on to the next task, making it incredibly efficient for real-time applications like chats, dashboards, or streaming.

Ready to Dive In? Here’s Where to Start --

1. Master JavaScript Essentials: Async functions, promises, and closures are a must.

2. Build a Basic Server: Use Node.js to set up a simple API. This will get you comfortable with the backend basics.

3. Explore Real-Time Apps: Create a basic chat app or real-time dashboard. You'll see why Node.js is loved for high-speed performance.

Node.js isn't just another tool. It’s your key to becoming a full-stack developer who can handle both sides of the web. Ready to make it happen?

(what makes it so fast in dev mode...) Before we dive deeper into Vite, why do you need a build tool for web development? A browser can render a web app using HTML, CSS, and Javascript. While this approach can work for smaller applications, you still need a build tool if you are building a large-scale application. A bundler can make your web application performant in three ways: -> Reduce the number of network requests -> Reduce total bytes sent over the network -> Improve JavaScript execution performance Vite provides all of the above advantages and improves developer experience with these features: -> Instant server start -> Lightning-fast HMR (Hot Module Replacement) -> Pre-configured optimized build Now the real question - how is Vite faster than other build tools? Vite uses two different bundlers for dev and production mode. It uses: -> esbuild for dev mode -> Rollup for prod mode esbuild makes sure all JS served to the browser is unbundled and in ESM format. This helps Vite to only replace the module that changed without transpiling the whole bundle. This makes Vite extremely fast for hot reloads in development mode. Like other bundlers, there is a build step involved in bundling the code. While esbuild is faster and gives better performance, it's not used for bundling in production. Vite uses esbuild for minification and transpilation but bundling is left for Rollup. It uses Rollup for bundling because of its flexible plugin API and ecosystem. In addition to the features mentioned above, Vite also comes with: -> CSS Support -> Code splitting -> Tree shaking -> Static assets handling -> Dynamic imports -> WebAssembly Support -> Web Worker Scripts -> Build optimizations All in all, Vite has transformed the developer tooling for front-end development. 🚀 Want to Stand Out in Web Development? Master Node.js! 🚀

Here’s the deal: If you're serious about a high-impact career in web development, Node.js is your ticket. 🌐 Whether you’re just getting started or leveling up, mastering Node.js opens the door to real-time, scalable, and lightning-fast applications.

So, What Exactly is Node.js?

Node.js lets you use JavaScript — yes, the same JavaScript you use in the browser — to create full-blown server applications. Think of it as JavaScript for the backend! 🚀

But Here’s the Twist:- Unlike regular JavaScript, which is all about the frontend, Node.js runs on the server. This means you can handle data processing, database access, and heavy backend tasks all using one language.

How Node.js Works (Without the Tech Jargon) :

Node.js is different because it’s single-threaded and non-blocking. Instead of waiting for things to load (like a database), Node.js moves on to the next task, making it incredibly efficient for real-time applications like chats, dashboards, or streaming.

Ready to Dive In? Here’s Where to Start --

1. Master JavaScript Essentials: Async functions, promises, and closures are a must.

2. Build a Basic Server: Use Node.js to set up a simple API. This will get you comfortable with the backend basics.

3. Explore Real-Time Apps: Create a basic chat app or real-time dashboard. You'll see why Node.js is loved for high-speed performance.

Node.js isn't just another tool. It’s your key to becoming a full-stack developer who can handle both sides of the web. Ready to make it happen?

🌟 Let’s connect and talk Node.js tips!

post_text: Europe’s EV chargers are about to get a major upgrade: within just 13 months, hundreds of thousands of chargers across Europe will need to be equipped or retrofitted with a compliant payment solution. Three forces are driving this change: - Ease of use: drivers want to charge without registering. - Fraud: RFID charge cards are increasingly vulnerable to misuse. - AFIR: by 2027, all public chargers ≥50 kW must support card payments. The case for payment terminals is clear. Is this a headache for operations? Not really. Terminals bring extra hardware, software, and financial players - all manageable with the right approach. Operators are increasingly focused on total cost of ownership, not just the sticker price or one piece of the financial flow. The ultimate goal is peace of mind. A one-stop-shop - a so-called “Payment Terminal as a Service” - sounds appealing, but what does it actually mean? Steven Tromp (Head of Proposition), Mai Nguyen (Product Manager), and Jos Westerkamp (Product Marketing), explain how we tackled these challenges and turned them into a complete solution. 👉 Watch the full webinar via the link in the first comment.

Europe’s EV chargers are about to get a major upgrade: within just 13 months, hundreds of thousands of chargers across Europe will need to be equipped or retrofitted with a compliant payment solution.
 
Three forces are driving this change:
- Ease of use: drivers want to charge without registering.
- Fraud: RFID charge cards are increasingly vulnerable to misuse.
- AFIR: by 2027, all public chargers ≥50 kW must support card payments.
The case for payment terminals is clear.
 
Is this a headache for operations? Not really. Terminals bring extra hardware, software, and financial players - all manageable with the right approach.
 
Operators are increasingly focused on total cost of ownership, not just the sticker price or one piece of the financial flow. The ultimate goal is peace of mind.
 
A one-stop-shop - a so-called “Payment Terminal as a Service” - sounds appealing, but what does it actually mean?
 
Steven Tromp (Head of Proposition), Mai Nguyen (Product Manager), and Jos Westerkamp (Product Marketing), explain how we tackled these challenges and turned them into a complete solution.
 
👉 Watch the full webinar via the link in the first comment.

😉 What is 1050 H14 material?

1050 H14 is a grade of aluminum alloy that's 99.5% pure aluminum and is used for general engineering applications:

Composition
1050 H14 is an unalloyed, non-heat-treatable aluminum alloy. It contains trace amounts of other elements, including iron, silicon, zinc, magnesium, titanium, manganese, and copper

Properties
1050 H14 is known for its corrosion resistance, ductility, and reflective finish. It has a modulus of elasticity of 71 GPa, an electrical resistivity of 0.282 x 10-6 Ω.m, a thermal conductivity of 222 W/m.K, and a thermal expansion of 24 x 10-6/K. 


Applications
1050 H14 is used in a variety of applications, including:
General sheet metal work 
Heat transfer devices 
🛳 Vessels 
Boiler making 
Appliances 
🏢 Architecture 
🚘 Automotive

Temper
1050 H14 is work hardened by rolling to a half-hard temper.

Understanding these elements helps us choose the right steel for any application. 🔹Carbon (C): The primary hardening element. It increases steel’s hardness and strength by forming carbides, but too much carbon reduces ductility and weldability, making steel brittle. 🔹Manganese (Mn): Improves toughness and strength, enhances hardenability, and neutralizes the negative effects of sulfur. It also acts as a deoxidizer during steel production. 🔹Chromium (Cr): Boosts corrosion and wear resistance by forming a protective oxide layer. It also increases hardenability and improves steel’s strength at high temperatures. Steels with over 11% chromium are stainless steels. 🔹Nickel (Ni): Adds toughness and impact resistance, especially at low temperatures. It also enhances corrosion resistance and helps refine the grain structure, improving ductility and fatigue life. 🔹Molybdenum (Mo): Raises high-temperature strength and resistance to creep and pitting corrosion. It improves hardenability and wear resistance, commonly used in stainless and high-strength low-alloy steels. 🔹Vanadium (V): Refines grain size and forms hard carbides that increase strength, toughness, and wear resistance. 🔹Tungsten (W): Provides “red hardness,” allowing steel to maintain cutting hardness even at high temperatures, ideal for high-speed cutting tools. 🔹Silicon (Si): Adds strength and elasticity, improves oxidation resistance, and serves as a deoxidizer in steelmaking. 🔹Cobalt (Co): Enhances hot hardness and magnetic properties, making it valuable in tool steels and special alloys. 🔹Copper (Cu): Improves atmospheric corrosion resistance in weathering steels, helping structures last longer outdoors without paint. 🔹Aluminium (Al): Controls grain growth for better Ever wondered how we get those perfect steel slabs without chaos? This magical powder used in continuous casting of steel is called Mold Flux! 🔥 Mold flux isn't just dust; it's a meticulously engineered synthetic slag powder sprinkled onto the molten steel surface in the continuous casting mold. When it meets that fiery steel, it melts, forming distinct layers (powder, sintered/mushy, liquid slag) – each playing a vital role. ✨ What's its SUPERPOWER? 🦸♂️ It's multi-functional! 1. 🌡️ Thermal Insulation: The top powder layer prevents excessive heat loss from the molten steel meniscus, stopping premature solidification which can cause surface defects. Keepin' it toasty! 2. 💧 Lubrication: The molten slag layer infiltrates the gap between the solidifying steel shell and the water-cooled copper mold wall. This reduces friction, prevents sticking, and allows smooth withdrawal of the strand. Like oil for the caster! 😉 3. ♨️ Heat Transfer Control: This is CRITICAL! The liquid slag film controls the horizontal heat transfer rate from the shell to the mold. Too fast? Cracks! Too slow? Thin shell & breakouts! It needs to be just right – the Goldilocks effect! 🤓 4. 🧹 Inclusion Absorption: As non-metallic inclusions (e.g., Alumina) float up from the steel, the liquid slag layer absorbs them, acting like a cleaner for the final product. Cleaner steel = Happy customers! 💪 5. 🛡️ Reoxidation Prevention: The continuous layer(s) protect the molten steel surface from interacting with air, preventing reoxidation. The Secret Sauce? Chemistry & Physics! 🧪🔬 • Composition: Typically based on CaO-SiO2 systems, often with Al2O3, fluxes like CaF2 (fluorite), Na2O, Li2O, B2O3, and carbon (to control melting rate). • Key Properties: We tailor its viscosity, melting/solidification temperature range (break temperature), basicity precisely for the steel grade, casting speed, and mold conditions. Getting the mold flux wrong can lead to surface defects (longitudinal cracks!), sticker breakouts 😱, and reduced steel quality. It's a high-tech balancing act! 😉 What is 1050 H14 material?

1050 H14 is a grade of aluminum alloy that's 99.5% pure aluminum and is used for general engineering applications:

Composition
1050 H14 is an unalloyed, non-heat-treatable aluminum alloy. It contains trace amounts of other elements, including iron, silicon, zinc, magnesium, titanium, manganese, and copper

Properties
1050 H14 is known for its corrosion resistance, ductility, and reflective finish. It has a modulus of elasticity of 71 GPa, an electrical resistivity of 0.282 x 10-6 Ω.m, a thermal conductivity of 222 W/m.K, and a thermal expansion of 24 x 10-6/K.


Applications
1050 H14 is used in a variety of applications, including:
General sheet metal work 
Heat transfer devices 
🛳 Vessels 
Boiler making 
Appliances 
🏢 Architecture 
🚘 Automotive

Temper
1050 H14 is work hardened by rolling to a half-hard temper.

and a conversation I had recently came to mind. At first glance, the industry looks chaotic: artists creating music at the core, A&R teams scouting talent, labels investing, managers, publishers. There are so many moving parts, it gives me headache ( I am still trying to understand streamign revenue to be honest...). And yet, I feel that this fragmentation isn’t just a mess. I see it as both a weakness and a strength. Here’s why I think that way: The complexity creates opportunities for discovery and support. Behind the scenes, there’s an ecosystem that helps new talent get found, invested in, and developed, even if imperfectly. Compare that to many creative startups. Ideas are abundant. Products are often solid. Yet so many fail, not because the idea is bad, but because they aren’t discovered fast enough or don’t have access to the people who could help them grow. It made me realise that even the music business isn’t perfect, its structure shows us the value of networks, support systems, and discovery pipelines. Lessons that any creative entrepreneur could apply. **Spotify's Price Adjustment: Implications for Subscription Businesses**

Spotify's recent increase in individual subscription rates to $12.99 signals a broader trend within the subscription-based business model. As the market evolves, companies must balance price sensitivity with the need for profitability.

At ElevenX Capital, we view such adjustments as essential for long-term growth, but they also require deep understanding of consumer behavior. Will user loyalty withstand this price hike, or could this be a tipping point for customers to explore alternatives?

What strategies do you believe subscription businesses should adopt in this climate?

Now we’re also seeing a wave of marketers who’ve only recently discovered AI and treat it like the holy grail. The result? Sanitised briefs that all look, feel, and sound the same — no matter which boardroom you sit in. Systems then churn out reams of “communication” that anyone with an IQ above 80 can spot as just stuff — disconnected, hollow, and forgettable. Because it doesn’t connect, the instinct is to produce more of it. So the flood continues. Until marketing departments mature — with real experience and real understanding — the ad and PR industry will keep circling the same drain. But I’m an optimist. in 1999, Ogilvy tried something new. And it was refreshing to see. I remember opening up AdWeek back then and seeing a story on ‘The Syndicate’. It was a network of independent/boutique creative agencies aligned with Ogilvy North America, allowing them to tap into some fresh thinking. The agencies were Core (St. Louis), Pyro (Dallas), WongDoody (Seattle), Work (Richmond, VA), VitroRobertson (San Diego), Hunt Adkins (Minneapolis), and Grant, Scott & Hurley (San Francisco). According to one article about why The Sydnicate was created stated it was to give Ogilvy more varied creative options for its multinational clients, while still allowing these creative shops to remain independent. Rick Boyko (CCO Ogilvy North America) was credited as one of the masterminds behind it. As far as I can see from past articles, The Syndicate existed from 1999-2002. I have no idea why it ended. With everything that is changing so fast in this industry, this concept should be explored by some major agencies that are now trying to dodge the iceberg looming on the horizon. There is a slew of new, small, nimble, creative agencies emerging, it seems almost weekly. Many were established by talented creative minds who were let go by bigger network shops. It would make sense for a smart network to think of a model such as The Syndicate if they want to stay competitive and be able to deliver new ideas that have not been slowed down by the lumbering internal processes that hinder the big agencies. Many brands have built agency villages, made up of big and small agencies. It works for them. So it would seem to make sense for a big agency to consider the same approach, build a village of small, indie shops that they can lean on when needed. But don’t try to buy them or control them, that’s how this mess started in the first place. But, as I mentioned, it would require a smart, big agency with creative leadership to see the value of this and also understand how to make it work. I remember when I read the article about The Syndicate and thought what a smart tactical move it was. I was a big fan of the work coming out of Core and Pyro. If you don’t know their work, look them up; very gritty, grungy and very non-big agency. Now would be a good time for more leaders of agencies to do for themselves what they often tell their clients they do for them - think differently. \"We cannot solve our problems with the same thinking we used when we created them.\" - Albert Einstein … When I'm not having flashbacks to articles I read 26 years ago, you'll find me running my own creative ventures, being a Fractional ECD, working on my own creative projects, or coaching Creative Directors and Creative Founders. post_text: For over 2 years now RJR Technologies ( RJR Technologies, Inc. ), is in an ongoing collaboration between the Chip Integration Technology Center ( CITC ), to develop a Low-Cost, Air-Cavity Package for Photonics Integrated Circuits (PICs) utilizing existing air-cavity (ACP) RF power package solutions with LCP injection molding technology. Based on the existing Semicon RF power experience, this technology offers the photonics world a scalable high-volume packaging solution and lead frame based assembly. This really creates the opportunity to go for cost-effective high-volume mass production. The technology allows for many different package layouts, as shown in one of my previous posts: Multiple package layouts RJR is in ongoing discussions with several photonics OSATs and end-customers. Recently RJR announced a formal collaboration with PHIX. PHIX, a European packaging foundry, specializes in all major PIC (Photonic Integrated Circuit) technology platforms. It provides assembly services and contract manufacturing for PICs and MEMS. With a recently established state-of-the-art production facility in Enschede, the Netherlands, PHIX has positioned itself as a key player in the European OSAT ecosystem for photonics. Wil Salhuana, CEO of RJR Technologies, stated, "As we introduce advanced photonics packages built on the proven performance of our established RF packages—offering best-in-class performance, rapid time to market, and cost efficiency—PHIX emerged as the ideal OSAT partner to provide comprehensive backend solutions for our customers." Press release RJR Press release PHIX At the Optica online industry meeting on Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) packaging for volume manufacturing (25 February 2025 10:00 - 11:30 hrs CET), I will present a short elevator pitch in RJRs Technology. This event gathers industry leaders to discuss transformations in PIC packaging to meet mass manufacturing demands, similar to CMOS microelectronics. This event will explore strategies for high throughput and yield, essential in today's tech landscape.The meeting will tackle challenges in PIC assembly, such as precision alignment, thermal management, and co-packaging with electronic components. They will also discuss the shift towards wafer-level processes required for increased production volumes, encouraging collaboration and innovative solutions for mainstream volume PIC manufacturing.
