Stairway to Purpose: Why I Ask “Why?” Fifteen Times Every great design starts with a question. Not what, not how — but why. Most people stop after their first why. But I’ve learned that your real purpose doesn’t appear until you ask why the fifteenth time. When I coach advisors, athletes, or entrepreneurs, I often ask them: “Why do you want to succeed?” They’ll say, “To make more money.” Then I ask again. And again. Until the truth surfaces — “Because I want my family to never struggle again,” or “Because I want to prove to myself that I can rise after falling.” That’s the power of the 15 WHY Ladder — one of the core frameworks in Winning by Design. It strips away ego, logic, and excuses until all that’s left is your higher purpose. Because purpose isn’t discovered in the noise of achievement. It’s revealed in the silence of self-awareness. In my own journey — from financial planner to national athlete, author, and father — every milestone was built on one staircase: Why do I do this? When you climb far enough, the why stops being about you. It becomes about the people you serve, the legacy you build, and the impact you leave behind. So the next time you’re stuck, don’t look for a new goal. Look for a deeper why. "This is what hard feels like" Alex Hormozi

There's a great clip of modern marketing guru, Alex Hormozi, explaining what it takes to be successful in business.

The late nights. The early mornings. The endless barriers. The thousands of "no's". The missteps. The falling outs with team mates. The disappointed spouses. The unknown.

Over the last 8 years since being in the USA, I've launched, in addition to a small property rental business, FLORUGBY, FloFC, FloBaseball, FLORACING (Moto), FanPower and now Paradigm Roofing's home energy business. Most have been successful, but some have been learnings. There's been a lot of "hard" days alongside a few less-hard ones. The "easy" days are few and far between.

Understanding that building something from nothing is supposed to feel hard, helps me justify the hours, the sacrifices, the all-of-the-above and gives me permission to get it wrong a lot of the time. It gives me the energy to keep going even if it feels futile or like you're wading through quicksand across Morecambe Bay (mine and Tyson Fury's hometown).

What makes it easier? Having a team that is in the trenches with you and is caring, but demanding. A team that pushes you to be better, but doesn't expect you to be perfect. A team that let's you fly on the good days, but covers your ass on the bad ones.

Thankfully I've always been blessed with great teams, but especially at Paradigm Roofing where we have a team of rogues and vagabonds who I know have my back, even though launching a home energy business is probably the toughest challenge yet and certainly epitomizes Hormozi's idea of "hard".

post_text: POV: You're filling out a form and they want your EIN. You: pauses You: opens email You: searches "EIN" You: gets 47 unrelated results You: checks downloads folder You: questions life choices 𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗣. 𝗝𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽. Do this: Write your EIN on the very top portion of a sticky note. Cut out the number. Stick it to your monitor. This is what I mean when I say "you can't force people to operate the way you want them to, but you can design an environment that makes the right thing the easy thing." Will you remember your EIN? No. Can you make it easy to find anyway? Yes. That's literally systems thinking. And before you @ me that this is "too simple to count"... Small operational wins compound. Every time you're NOT hunting for your EIN is time you're spending on revenue-generating activities instead. So yeah. Sticky note. Monitor. Done. (This also works for: routing numbers, business license numbers, and that one Canva hex code you use for everything.)

post_text_html:
POV: You're filling out a form and they want your EIN.
You: pauses 
You: opens email 
You: searches "EIN" 
You: gets 47 unrelated results 
You: checks downloads folder 
You: questions life choices

𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗣. 𝗝𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽.
Do this: Write your EIN on the very top portion of a sticky note. Cut out the number. Stick it to your monitor.

This is what I mean when I say "you can't force people to operate the way you want them to, but you can design an environment that makes the right thing the easy thing."

Will you remember your EIN? No. Can you make it easy to find anyway? Yes.
That's literally systems thinking.

And before you @ me that this is "too simple to count"... 
Small operational wins compound. Every time you're NOT hunting for your EIN is time you're spending on revenue-generating activities instead.

So yeah. Sticky note. Monitor. Done.

(This also works for: routing numbers, business license numbers, and that one Canva hex code you use for everything.)

are carbon credits? A carbon credit is a tradable certificate or permit representing the reduction of one tonne of carbon dioxide (or its equivalent in other greenhouse gases). In simple terms: 1 carbon credit is proof that 1 tonne of carbon dioxide (CO₂) has been removed or stopped from entering the atmosphere. You can think of them like ‘receipts’ for climate action: i) A factory emits CO₂ while working to reduce emissions. ii) Elsewhere, a project such as tree planting or solar energy reduces or removes CO₂. iii) Once that project is verified, it can issue a “receipt” for the reduction; that ‘receipt’ is a carbon credit. Organizations buy these credits to balance out part of their emissions and support climate projects. However, carbon credits are meant to complement, not replace, direct efforts to cut emissions, and they play a supporting role in broader net-zero strategies. To meet global climate targets, we must rapidly reduce emissions and scale carbon removal efforts. By 2050, an estimated 5–10 billion tonnes of CO₂ must be removed annually. The voluntary carbon market is a vital tool to channel finance into these solutions.

Our 2024 Voluntary Carbon Market Report outlines 10 key insights for buyers, including:

post_text: Hey CMA aspirants, after qualifying with AIR 1, recently I've received a lot of queries about my preparation and all. So I would like to share the following, which in my opinion contributed to my rank - 1. Create a well structured study plan - I divided my study period of 5 months. 3 months for studies and 2 months for revision + writing exams of old years and MTPs. I wrote 8 exams(for each paper) thus, of PY s and MTP s . You may create one according to your goals, time availability etc.. 2. Tracking the progression to make sure we are not slow or staying back. 3. Frequent revision is mandatory. 4. Most importantly, a strong mindset which is kind of.. "don't give up" like attitude. And an aim. That aim should be given prime importance. We may need to sacrifice a lot for achieving that. Nothing is impossible ! from AIR 34 in intermediate to AIR 1 in the final, the main reason behind the leap is my determination and persistence. I've attended online classes from Trivandrum chapter CMA-Trivandrum Chapter Hope you all may achieve your aim soon ☺️. All the very best ❤️

post_text: “Earn your leadership every day.” – Michael Jordan Dear LinkedIn Community, I want to reintroduce myself to my network and future/potential connections on LinkedIn. With an unwavering dedication to excellence and a proven track record of success across various environments, my unique blend of qualities will enable me to drive your team toward new levels. Who am I? At my core, I enjoy working with diverse people from different backgrounds, skills, and stories and helping them become a team. My teams are typically marked by getting things done and working well with others, constantly pushing themselves to improve from the day before, not just keeping that knowledge to themselves but sharing it with others. Questions we ask regularly: How am I making myself better today? How am I making others around me better today? How am I helping the company succeed in its mission? Traits that define me as a leader: 🔹 Humility: As a firm believer that knowledge is infinite, I embrace humility as a cornerstone of my leadership style. Acknowledging that I don't know everything allows me to remain open-minded and continuously learn from others, fostering an environment of collaboration and innovation . 🔹 Respect: One of my core values is treating individuals with the utmost respect. By fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace culture , I strive to empower every team member to reach their full potential, ensuring their diverse perspectives and ideas are valued and celebrated. 🔹 People-Centric: Genuine care for my team members lies at the heart of my leadership approach. I prioritize building strong relationships based on trust , empathy, and understanding, as I firmly believe that investing in people's growth and well-being is the key to unlocking their true potential. 🔹 Ownership: Taking ownership of failures and mistakes is not just a responsibility; it is a commitment I make to myself and my team. By accepting accountability, I foster a culture of continuous improvement and encourage a growth mindset where challenges are seen as opportunities for learning and development. 🔹 Credit Sharing: A strong leader recognizes that individual successes are interconnected with the team's achievements. I am committed to ensuring that credit is shared both upward and downward, creating a culture of appreciation, recognition, and collective celebration. 🔹 Results-Oriented: Getting the job done is my passion. With a results-oriented mindset, I continuously strive to exceed expectations, deliver exceptional outcomes, and drive organizational success. I approach challenges proactively, finding innovative solutions that propel the team forward and maximize their collective potential. 🔹 Continuous Learning: In a rapidly evolving world, a commitment to continuous learning is vital. I embrace new knowledge, stay abreast of industry trends, and encourage a culture of curiosity and exploration, empowering my team to adapt, grow, and excel in an ever-changing environment. 🔹 Collaboration: Collaboration lies at the heart of high-performance teams. By fostering an environment where diverse talents converge, I create a culture of collaboration that harnesses the collective genius of individuals, allowing us to tackle challenges together and achieve remarkable outcomes. 🔹 Integrity: High integrity forms the bedrock of my professional character. Guided by ethical principles, I consistently demonstrate honesty, transparency, and fairness in all my interactions. I firmly believe that integrity is the cornerstone of trust, essential for building lasting relationships within the team and beyond. 🔹 Driving Excellence: My unwavering focus on making things better drives me to push the boundaries of what is possible. By building high-performance teams that are both competitive and collaborative, I create an environment where individuals thrive, ideas flourish, and excellence becomes the norm. If you are seeking a TA Leader who encompasses these qualities and is poised to make a transformative impact on your organization, I would be honored to discuss how I can contribute to your team's success. post_text: Introduction Acne is a common skin condition that affects millions of people worldwide. For those with acne-prone skin, managing breakouts and achieving clear, healthy skin can be a constant challenge. However, with the right daily care routine and the right products, you can significantly improve the condition of your skin. In this article, we will explore daily care tips. Understanding Acne-Prone Skin Acne occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells, leading to the formation of pimples, blackheads, and whiteheads. Acne-prone skin is often characterized by excess sebum production, inflammation, and a higher likelihood of breakouts. Last week, I had the opportunity to attend PAC Accelerate Conference in Phoenix, AZ hosted by the Pro Athlete Community (PAC), alongside my colleague Damon Gooch.

As former professional athletes, it was great to be in a room listening and learning with over 250 athletes, alongside executives, investors, and operators, all focused on building, investing, and creating opportunities beyond a primary career.

What stood out most was the intentionality behind both the conversations and relationships. A few takeaways that stuck with me:

Shon Hart spoke about finding your assignment and how your experiences shape who you are and how you’re meant to serve.

Jay Ross led sessions on defining your core values and managing your inner critic, which is oftentimes the biggest barrier to your success.

Bert Zevzavadjian led a session on building your personal brand and networking with authenticity. Building real relationships, not just contacts was a consistent theme throughout the week.  

There were also several panel discussions on building wealth and creating a legacy in the next phase, with clear shift toward entrepreneurship and thinking bigger beyond the game.

It reinforced something I think about often — many athletes are business builders at their core and at Brown Advisory, we spend a lot of time working with clients navigating similar questions — how to thoughtfully build, preserve, and transition wealth in a way that aligns with what matters most.

Grateful to Chip Paucek and Michael T. Moe for welcoming Brown Advisory into the PAC community.

Also, congrats to Damon for coming home with some hardware as the pickleball champion. I didn’t bring back the golf trophy, but still had a great day on the links!

headline: Hig***ook***te *********ds *********************igh***************
post_text: High hook rate in Meta Ads doesn’t always mean high performance. We recently tested multiple video hooks across campaigns, some were generic curiosity hooks designed to stop the scroll and some directly spoke to what the audience was actually looking for. What we observed was interesting. The generic hooks delivered: • Higher hook rate • More initial engagement But they didn’t translate into the result we actually cared about, quality leads and conversions. On the other hand, the hooks that: 👉 clearly mentioned the topic 👉 directly addressed the audience’s pain point in the first 3 seconds had slightly lower hook rate but delivered significantly better business results. Why? Because stopping the scroll is only half the job. The other half is attracting the right viewer, not just more viewers. A lot of marketers optimise heavily for hook rate and assume: better attention = better performance. But in many cases, what actually matters more is relevance and intent alignment. When someone feels the ad is speaking exactly to their situation, they don’t need to be entertained, they’re already interested. Hook rate is a useful metric. But it’s not a success metric on its own. Relevance beats curiosity when the goal is conversion. In your experience, have you seen better results with curiosity hooks or problem-first hooks?

High hook rate in Meta Ads doesn’t always mean high performance.

We recently tested multiple video hooks across campaigns, some were generic curiosity hooks designed to stop the scroll and some directly spoke to what the audience was actually looking for.

What we observed was interesting.

The generic hooks delivered:
• Higher hook rate
• More initial engagement

But they didn’t translate into the result we actually cared about, quality leads and conversions.

On the other hand, the hooks that:
👉 clearly mentioned the topic
👉 directly addressed the audience’s pain point in the first 3 seconds

had slightly lower hook rate but delivered significantly better business results.

Why?
Because stopping the scroll is only half the job.
The other half is attracting the right viewer, not just more viewers.

A lot of marketers optimise heavily for hook rate and assume:
better attention = better performance.

But in many cases, what actually matters more is relevance and intent alignment.

When someone feels the ad is speaking exactly to their situation, they don’t need to be entertained, they’re already interested.

Hook rate is a useful metric.
But it’s not a success metric on its own.

Relevance beats curiosity when the goal is conversion.

In your experience, have you seen better results with curiosity hooks or problem-first hooks?

The Quantum Boltzmann Machine (QBM) is a quantum adaptation of the classical Boltzmann Machine, a type of stochastic neural network used in machine learning. QBM leverages principles of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, to potentially improve computational efficiency and learning capabilities.

Key Features of Quantum Boltzmann Machines:

Energy-Based Model: Like classical Boltzmann Machines, QBMs are energy-based models, where the probability distribution of the system's states is determined by an energy function.

Quantum State Representation: QBMs utilize quantum states to encode the probability distribution, allowing for the representation of complex distributions more efficiently than classical counterparts.

Superposition: The quantum superposition property enables the QBM to explore multiple configurations simultaneously, which can accelerate the learning process.

Entanglement: This quantum property allows for stronger correlations between variables compared to classical models, improving representational power.

Applications: QBMs are used in machine learning tasks such as classification, pattern recognition, and generative modeling. They are also being explored for optimization problems and quantum data processing.

Advantages Over Classical Boltzmann Machines:

Efficient Sampling: Quantum mechanics allows QBMs to sample from complex distributions faster.

Enhanced Expressiveness: Entanglement and superposition enable QBMs to represent distributions that classical Boltzmann Machines cannot.

Potential Speedup: QBMs may solve certain problems faster than classical methods due to quantum parallelism.

Challenges:

Implementation: Building and running QBMs require advanced quantum hardware, which is still in developmental stages.

Noise Sensitivity: Quantum systems are prone to errors due to decoherence and noise, which can affect learning performance.

Scalability: While promising, scaling QBMs to large systems is a significant challenge.

The Quantum Boltzmann Machine (QBM) is a quantum adaptation of the classical Boltzmann Machine, a type of stochastic neural network used in machine learning. QBM leverages principles of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, to potentially improve computational efficiency and learning capabilities.

Key Features of Quantum Boltzmann Machines:

Energy-Based Model: Like classical Boltzmann Machines, QBMs are energy-based models, where the probability distribution of the system's states is determined by an energy function.

Quantum State Representation: QBMs utilize quantum states to encode the probability distribution, allowing for the representation of complex distributions more efficiently than classical counterparts.

Superposition: The quantum superposition property enables the QBM to explore multiple configurations simultaneously, which can accelerate the learning process.

Entanglement: This quantum property allows for stronger correlations between variables compared to classical models, improving representational power.

Applications: QBMs are used in machine learning tasks such as classification, pattern recognition, and generative modeling. They are also being explored for optimization problems and quantum data processing.

Advantages Over Classical Boltzmann Machines:

Efficient Sampling: Quantum mechanics allows QBMs to sample from complex distributions faster.

Enhanced Expressiveness: Entanglement and superposition enable QBMs to represent distributions that classical Boltzmann Machines cannot.

Potential Speedup: QBMs may solve certain problems faster than classical methods due to quantum parallelism.

Challenges:

Implementation: Building and running QBMs require advanced quantum hardware, which is still in developmental stages.

Noise Sensitivity: Quantum systems are prone to errors due to decoherence and noise, which can affect learning performance.

Scalability: While promising, scaling QBMs to large systems is a significant challenge.

post_text: It took me 4 internships to finally realize something I wish I knew earlier. Big names, big companies, or big clients don’t guarantee anything. They don’t automatically pay your bills. They don’t decide your career. I’ve seen people proudly say they worked at the “Big 4”. But when you ask them what exactly they did there, the answer is often: “Not much… just a few small tasks.” 👉 This doesn’t mean big firms or big clients don’t teach anything. They do. But here’s the truth no one says out loud: It’s not the logo you worked under that shapes your career. →It’s the skills you built, the problems you solved, and the experience you gained that actually matter. And sometimes, a smaller role with more responsibility teaches you 10x more than a “dream brand” ever could. Society glorifies the shiny tag. But when you’re in the room—facing deadlines, managing clients, handling mistakes—it’s your capability, not the company name, that decides your future. So, if you’re starting out, here’s what I’ve learnt: • Don’t chase brands, chase learning curves. • Don’t chase logos, chase responsibility and growth. • Don’t just collect CV lines, build real experience. • In the beginning, it’s not about who you work for. • It’s about what you learn while working. What really does matter is? • The skills you build. • The knowledge you pick up. • The mistakes you learn from (and the confidence you gain after). Sure, a big name on your CV looks shiny. But when you’re thrown into new challenges, it’s the skills you’ve built that actually carry you forward—not the logo you worked under. If I could give my younger self one reminder, it would be: → Choose growth over glamour. → Focus on skills, not just CVs. → Say yes to learning curves, not just logos. Here’s my question for you: If tomorrow nobody cared about brand names, would your skills alone make you stand out? #Linkedincommunity #Linkedin #Storytelling

Felicity Swindell of The FDL Agency and 5 tips any small business owner can use to launching an internship program: 1) Recruit Prepared Candidates - Partner with universities and focus on students who already have a foundational, textbook understanding of your field, so you can focus on hands-on learning. I don’t have to take a lot of extra time away to teach the basics because our program is accredited through universities, and we only accept students from Mass Communications and PR departments. 2) Be Selective & Strategic - Take your time hiring to find the right fit. Taking longer to onboard allows you to make sure candidates truly meet the needs of the role and helps weed out those who aren’t as interested. You’ll almost always lose a few along the way, so hire 1-2 more than you need to account for those that fall off. 3) Create a Structured, Incentivized Program - Use defined roles, shadow-to-lead workflows, and weekly check-ins to establish clear goals, keep progress and learning on track. If it's an unpaid role, offer clear meaningful incentives like commissions and access to software tools (i.e. Adobe Creative Suite, Canva Teams) that support both their work and personal growth. 4) Prioritize Real-World Experience - Interns are collaborators not assistants. They are encouraged to bring ideas to the table and help shape campaigns building their confidence and experience from week one. 5) Invest in Their Long-Term Success - Supporting interns’ growth is not competition to your agency, it reflects our commitment to developing the next generation of leaders. At the end of the day, I want to ensure they leave with tangible contacts and portfolio work that serves them moving forward. post_text_html:
It took me 4 internships to finally realize something I wish I knew earlier.

Big names, big companies, or big clients don’t guarantee anything.
They don’t automatically pay your bills.
They don’t decide your career.

I’ve seen people proudly say they worked at the “Big 4”.
But when you ask them what exactly they did there, the answer is often:
“Not much… just a few small tasks.”
👉 This doesn’t mean big firms or big clients don’t teach anything. They do.

But here’s the truth no one says out loud:
It’s not the logo you worked under that shapes your career.
→It’s the skills you built, the problems you solved, and the experience you gained that actually matter.

And sometimes, a smaller role with more responsibility teaches you 10x more than a “dream brand” ever could.

Society glorifies the shiny tag.
But when you’re in the room—facing deadlines, managing clients, handling mistakes—it’s your capability, not the company name, that decides your future.

So, if you’re starting out, here’s what I’ve learnt:
• Don’t chase brands, chase learning curves.
• Don’t chase logos, chase responsibility and growth.
• Don’t just collect CV lines, build real experience.
• In the beginning, it’s not about who you work for.
• It’s about what you learn while working.

What really does matter is?
• The skills you build.
•  The knowledge you pick up.
•  The mistakes you learn from (and the confidence you gain after).

Sure, a big name on your CV looks shiny.
But when you’re thrown into new challenges, it’s the skills you’ve built that actually carry you forward—not the logo you worked under.

If I could give my younger self one reminder, it would be:
→ Choose growth over glamour.
→ Focus on skills, not just CVs.
→ Say yes to learning curves, not just logos.

 Here’s my question for you:
If tomorrow nobody cared about brand names, would your skills alone make you stand out?

📢UPDATE 2/4: See you here again next month - same time, same place! 

President Trump agreed to delay tariffs on Canada and Mexico for 30 days, but moved forward with a 10% tariff on China. 

🌍 Global Trade Alert: New Tariff Changes & What It Means for Brands 🚨

Following recent announcements by President Trump, new tariffs on imports from Mexico, Canada, and China will soon take effect. At Global-e, we are actively analyzing the impact of these changes to support our merchants in navigating the evolving trade landscape.
🔑 Key Takeaways:
📌 25% duty on all products imported from Canada & Mexico to the U.S.
📌 10% additional duty on all imports from China to the U.S. this includes products entering the US with a COO of China. 
📌 No de minimis exemption (<$800 USD) for Canada, Mexico, and China; still applies to other countries.
📌 Effective Date: February 4, 2025
❓ Potential retaliatory tariffs? Canada considering imposing duties on U.S. commodities.

Update: February 3 @ 11 AM EST - Mexico and the US have agreed to put tariffs on hold for one month. 

We recognize that these new regulations may bring challenges, and we are committed to ensuring a seamless transition for our merchants. Our global tax and duties team is working closely with external experts to assess the full impact and implement platform adjustments to keep your business running smoothly. 
💡 Stay tuned—we will provide ongoing updates as more details emerge. If you have questions, we’re here to help.

📢UPDATE 2/4: See you here again next month - same time, same place!

President Trump agreed to delay tariffs on Canada and Mexico for 30 days, but moved forward with a 10% tariff on China.

🌍 Global Trade Alert: New Tariff Changes & What It Means for Brands 🚨

Following recent announcements by President Trump, new tariffs on imports from Mexico, Canada, and China will soon take effect. At Global-e, we are actively analyzing the impact of these changes to support our merchants in navigating the evolving trade landscape.
🔑 Key Takeaways:
📌 25% duty on all products imported from Canada & Mexico to the U.S.
📌 10% additional duty on all imports from China to the U.S. this includes products entering the US with a COO of China.
📌 No de minimis exemption (<$800 USD) for Canada, Mexico, and China; still applies to other countries.
📌 Effective Date: February 4, 2025
❓ Potential retaliatory tariffs? Canada considering imposing duties on U.S. commodities.

Update: February 3 @ 11 AM EST - Mexico and the US have agreed to put tariffs on hold for one month.

We recognize that these new regulations may bring challenges, and we are committed to ensuring a seamless transition for our merchants. Our global tax and duties team is working closely with external experts to assess the full impact and implement platform adjustments to keep your business running smoothly.
💡 Stay tuned—we will provide ongoing updates as more details emerge. If you have questions, we’re here to help.

#GlobalE #CrossBorderEcom #Tariffs #Ecommerce #GlobalBusiness

title: Are***u a***bot***
headline: Are***u a***bot*********, r*********************CAP************************
post_text: When you visit a website to purchase a product, the first thing that often appears is a page asking, "Are you a robot?" requiring you to select images with traffic signs or check a box to confirm you're not a robot. How many times have you encountered this online? Hundreds, maybe thousands? Do you really believe that this small question can distinguish between humans and robots? Many of us feel it's pointless, but in reality, it accurately differentiates between the two. So, what’s the history behind this question, how does it work, and why do we need to tell humans and robots apart? Why Do We Need to Distinguish Between Humans and Robots? Distinguishing between humans and robots is essential for maintaining the security and effectiveness of websites, as well as user convenience. If we don't care whether someone accessing the site is a human or a robot, we will face several issues, including: Fake Clicks on Ads : Anyone can create bots to click on ads artificially, leading to false profits for site owners. Increased Operational Costs : The presence of bots fills servers with fake requests instead of real users wanting to use the site, doubling operational costs as more servers are needed to handle both fake and real traffic. Product Purchases : In some cases, bots automatically buy products as soon as they become available, a practice known as "scalping." These products are then resold at much higher prices, depriving regular consumers of the chance to obtain them. An example of this occurred with the release of PS5/XBOX consoles in 2020, where stocks sold out immediately due to bots, and they were later sold at exorbitant prices on the secondary market, making it hard for regular consumers to buy them at original prices. There are many other issues as well, such as manipulating survey results and creating fake accounts, which can cause harm. Therefore, it is crucial to distinguish between robots and real users. CAPTCHA A CAPTCHA is a security system used to distinguish humans from bots online by presenting challenges that are easy for humans but difficult for automated systems. CAPTCHA stands for "Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart." The first CAPTCHA asked users to retype distorted text, which was hard for bots to read. However, this method was slow and sometimes hard for humans to understand. Audio versions were also developed, but they faced challenges with background noise and distorted speech. Studies have shown that it can take up to 10 seconds to complete a CAPTCHA with distorted text, and even longer for audio versions. This led to frustration among users, who might leave the site if they failed on the first try. CAPTCHA also introduced other methods, such as selecting images that match a certain description. However, attempts to use image-based tests (like identifying objects in photos) did not work well, as users might give incorrect responses, for instance, calling flowers "plants." Despite the variety of CAPTCHA methods, advancements in artificial intelligence and tools like "Decaptcha" have made it easier for bots to bypass these tests. As a result, CAPTCHA systems have become outdated and insufficient for distinguishing between humans and bots. However, CAPTCHA still has its uses in certain situations, and we are likely to see newer, more effective systems in the future. reCAPTCHA Why not make it easier for users? Instead of typing text, users could simply respond to whether they are a robot or not. This may sound crazy, but it's actually more effective! This concept led Google to develop reCAPTCHA, or "I'm not a robot," where all you have to do is click a box. The system analyzes human behavior that robots cannot replicate, using extensive data to track mouse movement patterns and assess if they are random or not. Even the smartest bots struggle to mimic human-like movements. The system also measures how long it takes for a user to click the box, distinguishing between human and programmed actions. It's important to note that other factors are considered, such as overall interaction with the site and previous browsing history. Now, let's say we created a bot that can imitate human movement, or the user accessed the site via a mobile device. How would the system differentiate them? If the system is uncertain whether the user is a robot or a human, what will reCAPTCHA do in these scenarios? The system has three options: Allow User : If the system is confident the user is human. Block User : If the system is certain the user is a robot. Traditional CAPTCHA : If the user is on a mobile device or the system suspects they are a robot. Invisible reCAPTCHA Invisible reCAPTCHA is an enhanced version of the reCAPTCHA technology that aims to improve the user experience by conducting background analysis without requiring direct interaction. It does not ask users to perform any actions; instead, it operates in the background when users access the site by monitoring behavioral patterns such as user interaction with site elements, browsing speed, clicks, and various signals like browsing history and the user's device type, all without users being aware of it. This comprehensive analysis determines whether the user is a robot. This method is effective in avoiding user disruption with tests, and if a robot is detected, it is given a challenge to complete for verification. One interesting method that has emerged to bypass CAPTCHA systems is the use of "CAPTCHA farms," where low-wage workers are hired to complete the tests on behalf of bots, reports reveal that GPT-4 was able to hire a human via TaskRabbit to solve a CAPTCHA, tricking the person into believing it wasn't a bot reports reveal that GPT-4 was able to hire a human via TaskRabbit to solve a CAPTCHA, tricking the person into believing it wasn't a bot.

I came across a very interesting article in WIREs Energy & Environment discussing the current state and future of bio-based chemicals. One point that stood out: the authors note in p.12 that “oxygen has to be removed from biomass” to make bio-based molecules resemble their fossil-based counterparts. 💡 While this makes sense for many applications, I couldn’t help but notice that it doesn’t really apply to plasticisers. Most fossil-based plasticisers are carboxyl esters, where oxygen is essential to their performance. 🌱 And we already have a rich, natural supply of carboxyl esters in the form of triglycerides from vegetable oils, which we chemically modify to obtain our bio-based plasticisers (without removing the carboxyl group, of course!). So, it seems somewhat contradictory to remove oxygen from bio-based feedstocks via cracking, only to add it back later through oxidation. 🔄 Maybe it’s time to rethink this approach—at least for the medium to long term within the PVC value chain—where time and resources invested in developing, optimising, and testing new molecules derived from natural carboxyl-based feedstocks could represent a promising route to enhance the sustainability profile of PVC. I guess this could ultimately lead to more efficient solutions that are better aligned with the growing trend toward offering products with a lower environmental impact. #BiobasedChemicals So, it seems somewhat contradictory to remove oxygen from bio-based feedstocks via cracking, only to add it back later through oxidation. 🔄 Maybe it’s time to rethink this approach—at least for the medium to long term within the PVC value chain—where time and resources invested in developing, optimising, and testing new molecules derived from natural carboxyl-based feedstocks could represent a promising route to enhance the sustainability profile of PVC. This year, I plan to learn one Content Design Tip a Day that I may or may have not known in the course of my career. Here’s the one for today:

📌 Prioritize the User Scenarios over Features you want to sell

When designing content, think about the user's journey and the scenarios in which they will interact with your content, rather than just listing features or information. 

By framing content within real-world use cases, you make it more relevant, intuitive, and engaging for your audience. 

Ask yourself: "What does the user need to accomplish, and how can I help them do it as efficiently as possible?"

This is important for every User Journey, because you’re already thinking ahead of your users to give them a very seamless experience using copy🤗.

What do you think about this tip? Does it make sense to you?

This year, I plan to learn one Content Design Tip a Day that I may or may have not known in the course of my career. Here’s the one for today:

📌 Prioritize the User Scenarios over Features you want to sell

When designing content, think about the user's journey and the scenarios in which they will interact with your content, rather than just listing features or information.

By framing content within real-world use cases, you make it more relevant, intuitive, and engaging for your audience.

Ask yourself: "What does the user need to accomplish, and how can I help them do it as efficiently as possible?"

This is important for every User Journey, because you’re already thinking ahead of your users to give them a very seamless experience using copy🤗.

What do you think about this tip? Does it make sense to you?

#contentdesign
#uxwriting

So back in 2025, a simple calendar invitation could hijack your entire Android OS.

𝗡𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗲 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿, 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁?

𝗪𝗲𝗹𝗹, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆.

It was awesome presenting at Kaltura AI Security Day, where I connected the dots on how threats evolved from 2025 to 2026. We went from Android OS hijacks to completely breaking OpenClaw, escalating to persistent endpoint compromise, and exposing the systemic issues behind Moltbook.

And just when you thought giving AI a browser would be cool, these shiny new agentic browsers can be tricked into leaking your local filesystem, exposing sensitive data, and handing over your password manager.

The attack surface changed, but the chaos stayed the same. 

𝗠𝘂𝗰𝗵, 𝗺𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝘁 𝗕𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗛𝗮𝘁 𝗨𝗦𝗔 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲. 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗱.

I recently listened to the Security Intelligence podcast with Douglas Bonderud, and one guest’s comment really resonated with me: \"Apply IAM principles to your home internet router.\" We often talk about \"Zero Trust\" and \"Defense-in-Depth\" as high-level corporate strategies, but the reality is that our homes have become the new frontier of the network. If we aren't practicing these concepts in our personal lives, we’re missing a huge opportunity to reinforce the habits that keep our organizations secure. I decided to audit my own \"home security stack,\" and I’ve been applying the same IAM principles I use professionally to my digital life: 🔹 Centralized Credential Management: I use a password manager to ensure every account has high-entropy, unique credentials. It’s the simplest way to kill the threat of credential stuffing. 🔹 Hardware-Backed MFA: I’ve moved away from SMS-based codes (which are vulnerable to interception) toward hardware security keys and app-based authenticators. 🔹 Network Segmentation: Inspired by the podcast, I’ve moved my \"smart\" IoT devices (cameras, bulbs, etc.) onto a separate guest network. This ensures that a compromised, unpatched smart bulb can’t provide a lateral path to my primary workstations. 🔹 Applying \"Least Privilege\" at Home: I maintain a standard user account for daily tasks on my personal computers. I only elevate to an administrative account when I absolutely have to perform system-level maintenance. 🔹 Audit & Deprovisioning: I regularly review the \"Connected Apps\" lists on my major accounts (Google, GitHub, LinkedIn). If I haven't used an app in months, I revoke its access. It’s a personal version of the IAM lifecycle deprovisioning process. The takeaway? Security isn't just about enterprise-grade tools; it’s about the discipline of managing identities and access. If we can't secure our own home routers, we have no business designing security architectures for a corporation. How are you applying Zero Trust principles to your home network? This week, Meta made a major announcement: they caught and disrupted a fresh wave of sophisticated mobile spear-phishing attempts targeting users via WhatsApp. The sophisticated campaign bypassed standard mobile application controls, relying on highly targeted malicious links to compromise devices. This brings us to the ultimate paradox facing CISOs and security leaders today: Out-of-the-Box Defenses vs. Human Exploitation. Cybercriminals aren't trying to pick the lock anymore. They’re just convincing your users to hand over the keys. Because our phones hold our entire lives—corporate emails, banking apps, and 2FA credentials—mobile has become the ultimate high-value target. Hackers are shifting from pure code exploitation to sophisticated social engineering: 🔹 Smishing & Vishing: Pretexting that bypasses network boundaries entirely. 🔹 Permissions Abuse: Tricking users into granting system-level access to seemingly benign apps. 🔹 Zero-Day Messenger Exploits: Using data rendering gaps in heavily trusted communication channels. Your mobile endpoint is only as strong as the person holding it. Relying strictly on native operating system defenses without continuous user education and context-aware access policies is no longer enough. How is your organization adapting its Mobile Threat Defense (MTD) strategy? Are you treating mobile security with the same weight as your desktop architecture? iPhone Security Flaw Affects Millions of Older Devices Cybersecurity researchers have identified a serious security vulnerability affecting several older iPhone models powered by Apple’s A12 and A13 processors. Unlike most security issues, this flaw cannot be corrected through a software update because it resides within the device’s SecureROM, the immutable code that runs before iOS loads. The vulnerability, known as “usbliter8,” targets the boot ROM, a foundational component responsible for initializing the device during startup. Researchers demonstrated that an attacker with physical access to an affected iPhone could potentially execute unauthorized code or install malicious software at a very low level within the device. The affected models include the iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR, iPhone 11 series, and certain versions of the iPhone SE that use A12 or A13 chips. Because the flaw is embedded directly into hardware-level code, it cannot be fixed through conventional security patches or iOS updates. There is an important limitation, however. The vulnerability cannot be exploited remotely. An attacker must have direct physical access to the device and specialized technical knowledge to take advantage of the flaw. As a result, the risk to most everyday users remains relatively low compared with remotely exploitable vulnerabilities. Apple has faced similar hardware-level issues in the past, but such flaws are uncommon because they require design changes in future hardware generations rather than software fixes. Key Takeaways Researchers discovered a hardware-based security flaw affecting iPhones powered by A12 and A13 processors. Because the vulnerability exists in SecureROM, Apple cannot eliminate it through software updates. Exploitation requires physical access to the device, reducing the overall threat to most users. Implications The discovery highlights the limits of software-based security in modern devices. Even as operating systems become more secure, hardware vulnerabilities can persist for the entire lifespan of a product. For users handling sensitive corporate, government, financial, or personal data, the finding reinforces the importance of physical device security, strong passcodes, biometric protection, and upgrading to newer hardware when practical. As cybersecurity threats continue to evolve, hardware-level trust and security architecture will become increasingly important in future device design. So back in 2025, a simple calendar invitation could hijack your entire Android OS.

𝗡𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗲 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿, 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁?

𝗪𝗲𝗹𝗹, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆.

It was awesome presenting at Kaltura AI Security Day, where I connected the dots on how threats evolved from 2025 to 2026. We went from Android OS hijacks to completely breaking OpenClaw, escalating to persistent endpoint compromise, and exposing the systemic issues behind Moltbook.

And just when you thought giving AI a browser would be cool, these shiny new agentic browsers can be tricked into leaking your local filesystem, exposing sensitive data, and handing over your password manager.

The attack surface changed, but the chaos stayed the same.

post_text: Internal communication is an entire process within an organization. It includes how information is shared up and down communication channels, as well as laterally, in order to achieve the organization’s goals. Communication is shared in various forms (verbal, written, and digitally), within teams and company-wide. Let’s explore key elements, tips, and trends related to effective internal communications and strategy… Virtual and Remote Communication : With remote and hybrid work arrangements more common than ever, internal communications have increasingly moved to virtual channels such as video conferencing, collaboration platforms, and social media. Employee-Generated Content : Many companies are encouraging employees to create their own content to share with colleagues, whether it’s through internal blogs, videos, or social media posts. This can help increase engagement and create a more authentic and transparent company culture. Personalization and Targeting : Internal communications are becoming more personalized and targeted to specific groups or individuals, using data and analytics to identify what information is most relevant to each employee. Mobile Communication : With more employees working remotely or on the go, mobile communication is becoming increasingly important. Companies are using mobile apps and other mobile-friendly tools to ensure that employees can stay connected and informed from anywhere. Integrated Communications : Internal communications are increasingly being integrated with external communications, including marketing and public relations. This can help create a more cohesive message and improve overall brand reputation. Video and Visual Content : Video and visual content are becoming more popular in internal communications, as they can be more engaging and easier to consume than text-based content. Companies are using tools like live-streaming, webinars, and animated videos to share information with employees. Gamification : Gamification is being used to make internal communications more engaging and fun. Companies are creating games, quizzes, and other interactive content to help employees learn and retain information more effectively. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion : Internal communications are increasingly focused on diversity, equity, and inclusion, with companies using internal channels to communicate about their DEI initiatives and provide resources and support for employees from diverse backgrounds. Alignment and Consistency : Internal communications can help ensure that everyone in the organization is aligned and working towards the same goals. It can also help maintain consistency in messaging and branding across different departments and locations. Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing : Internal communications can facilitate collaboration and knowledge sharing among employees, enabling them to work together more effectively and share best practices and ideas. Change Management : Internal communications are particularly important during times of change, such as mergers, acquisitions, or restructuring. Effective communication can help employees understand the reasons for the change, their role in it, and what to expect going forward. These are just a few of the latest trends in internal communications. As technology continues to evolve and work arrangements continue to change, we can expect to see even more innovation in this area in the coming years. In summary, corporate internal communications are important because they help engage and motivate employees, align and coordinate efforts, facilitate collaboration and knowledge sharing, manage change, and enhance the company’s reputation and branding. Effective internal communications can ultimately help drive business success and create a positive work environment for employees.

Catherine in Spain 🇪🇸 No: 23: 
Following my last post of Chinese being cold, thanks Antonio Teijeiro 安东 for reminding me of the theory of the coconut and peach cultures from Erin Meyer's book The Culture Map.  Yes, Chinese are "coconuts" 🥥🥥. 
"Some are very cold and hard at the beginning, but when they open up, you have a real friend (this would be the coconuts). 
Other cultures are completely opposite: very open for chitchat but will not continue down the path of friendship. These are peach cultures, soft on the outside, hard on the inside (Americans are an example of this). " 

Claudia Elias's million dollar question: 
What's the best way to get a Chinese person (in general) to open up and feel comfortable with you? That could be in a personal or business relationship.

🤔️My two cents: 
I have noticed that lost of Chinese are amazed if you know something about their hometown, especially if they are from  less known provinces and cities. Most foreigners only know Beijing, Shanghai and maybe Guangzhou, if you could invest a little time in their hometown, it could open doors.

Catherine in Spain 🇪🇸 No: 23:
Following my last post of Chinese being cold, thanks Antonio Teijeiro 安东 for reminding me of the theory of the coconut and peach cultures from Erin Meyer's book The Culture Map. Yes, Chinese are "coconuts" 🥥🥥.
"Some are very cold and hard at the beginning, but when they open up, you have a real friend (this would be the coconuts).
Other cultures are completely opposite: very open for chitchat but will not continue down the path of friendship. These are peach cultures, soft on the outside, hard on the inside (Americans are an example of this). "

Claudia Elias's million dollar question:
What's the best way to get a Chinese person (in general) to open up and feel comfortable with you? That could be in a personal or business relationship.

🤔️My two cents:
I have noticed that lost of Chinese are amazed if you know something about their hometown, especially if they are from less known provinces and cities. Most foreigners only know Beijing, Shanghai and maybe Guangzhou, if you could invest a little time in their hometown, it could open doors.

Health systems across the UK are at a turning point. Prevention and care closer to home are widely recognised as part of the solution - but finding the space to act amid financial and operational pressure remains a real challenge.

At the HFMA - IMPOWER roundtable last month, IMPOWER's Samuel R. and Oliver Barnes joined finance leaders from across all four UK nations to explore what transformation really means in today’s context, and what it will take to move beyond pilots and intentions into sustained system change.

One message stood out clearly from the discussion:
“The risk of doing nothing is bigger than the risk of doing something.”

Read the blog and download the full HFMA IMPOWER Roundtable 2026 write‑up here: https://lnkd.in/dqRv2SvQ.

post_text: OSHA has opened an inquiry into crane operations at SpaceX’s Starbase site, reflecting the challenges of maintaining consistent safety controls in large, fast-changing industrial environments. Starbase blends construction, manufacturing, and testing in a way that differs from conventional facilities, which complicates regulatory oversight. OSHA’s review focuses on equipment suitability, operator certification, and site-level planning—core elements of any crane-related assessment. The inquiry does not imply severe outcomes; investigations of this type are routine whenever equipment issues are reported. What the review underscores, however, is the increasing need for adaptable safety processes as industrial projects scale rapidly. In parallel, companies like BitsLab are advancing AI-agent defense technologies aimed at securing emerging autonomous systems. Together, these developments highlight how both physical and digital infrastructures are navigating new oversight expectations. https://lnkd.in/dpENTnQx

Floating Offshore Platforms — Engineering, Risk, and Precision at Sea ⚓ The transportation of floating offshore platforms is a highly demanding marine operation. These structures are massive, heavy, and highly sensitive to environmental forces, often requiring long-distance relocation from fabrication yards to offshore fields. Successful execution depends on detailed planning to control safety risks, costs, and schedules. Several transport methods are commonly applied, depending on platform design and project constraints: 🔹 Heavy-Lift Vessel Transport Large platforms are frequently transported using semi-submersible heavy-lift vessels. These ships ballast down to receive the structure and then deballast to lift it clear of the water. This method offers excellent stability and control for long voyages but comes with significant cost and limited vessel availability. 🔹 Wet Towing When platforms are designed to float, wet towing is an economical option. Tugboats tow the unit at normal or increased draft to reduce wave-induced motions. While cost-effective, this method is highly dependent on weather windows, towing speed, and hull hydrodynamics. 🔹 Deck Transport Smaller floating units or modules may be transported on barges or vessels. Securing the structure on deck simplifies stability management during transit, but vessel deck capacity and load limits restrict its application. 🔹 Modular Transport Platforms may be divided into modules for separate shipment. This approach eases transport constraints but shifts complexity to offshore integration and installation, increasing execution risk. Across all transport methods, stability control, structural integrity, and environmental conditions remain the governing factors. Every move demands precise engineering, continuous monitoring, and disciplined marine operations. OSHA has opened an inquiry into crane operations at SpaceX’s Starbase site, reflecting the challenges of maintaining consistent safety controls in large, fast-changing industrial environments. Starbase blends construction, manufacturing, and testing in a way that differs from conventional facilities, which complicates regulatory oversight. OSHA’s review focuses on equipment suitability, operator certification, and site-level planning—core elements of any crane-related assessment. The inquiry does not imply severe outcomes; investigations of this type are routine whenever equipment issues are reported.

What the review underscores, however, is the increasing need for adaptable safety processes as industrial projects scale rapidly. In parallel, companies like BitsLab are advancing AI-agent defense technologies aimed at securing emerging autonomous systems. Together, these developments highlight how both physical and digital infrastructures are navigating new oversight expectations.

post_text_html:
Ayer participé en el evento “The Journey to Prime Day 2026”, organizado por Amazon Ads en Madrid: un espacio donde marcas, agencias y equipos de Amazon se reunieron para preparar uno de los momentos más decisivos del año.

El cierre fue especialmente inspirador: una mesa redonda donde tres marcas compartimos nuestras mejores prácticas y casos de éxito.
Un orgullo que 3INA fuera una de las seleccionadas y una gran responsabilidad poder representar el trabajo, la creatividad y la ambición de todo el equipo. Aprovecho para reconocer la inestimable labor de Gorka Castrillo y su equipo.

Gracias a Amazon Ads por los insights y la visión compartida, y a Martino Di Pietro por reunir a un ecosistema clave de más de 300 profesionales con un objetivo común. Un especial agradecimiento a Sandra Angora por organizar la increíble mesa redonda. A Javier Castro de Liñán y Aris de Juan de Uribe por pensar en nosotros para compartir nuestro caso de éxito. Y a todos los que presentaron por parte de Amazon Ads , Miren Lasuen , Alicia Maes Onsurbe , Jesús B. , Lourdes Pérez Sánchez-Urdazpal
Y agradecimiento al equipo de NielsenIQ por compartir su visión sobre las tendencias y dinámicas de mercado online.

También, un placer compartir conversación con profesionales y marcas como Jordi Fernandez - Mahou San Miguel y Mª Teresa González García - Biogran . Diferentes aproximaciones, un mismo destino: demostrar que no hay una única forma de llegar más lejos… pero sí una constante, la creatividad y la ejecución marcan la diferencia. Y hablando de ejecución, quiero agradecer a a B2Marketplace por acompañarnos en este viaje.

El evento giraba en torno a una idea potente: el lanzamiento de un cohete 🚀
Preparación, impulso, despegue… y después, la verdadera misión: mantener la trayectoria y maximizar el impacto.

#PrimeDay es ese momento de ignición.
Pero el verdadero reto y la verdadera oportunidad está en todo lo que sucede antes y después.

Este cohete ya está en órbita.
Y el viaje, sin duda, no ha hecho más que empezar. “Let the journey begin“

post_text: A bit late on this, but I'm excited to share that on October 2nd, I successfully defended my MSc thesis titled "𝑰𝒏𝒇𝒍𝒖𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒍𝒆 𝒄𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒔 𝒐𝒇 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒕𝒆𝒊𝒏 𝒂𝒈𝒈𝒓𝒆𝒈𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒔 𝒐𝒏 𝒑𝒉𝒚𝒔𝒊𝒄𝒂𝒍 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒕𝒊𝒆𝒔 𝒐𝒇 𝒐𝒍𝒆𝒐𝒈𝒆𝒍𝒔". This project was completely new to me and allowed me to deep dive into the complexities of understanding particle interactions. In summary, the conditions under which you create your protein aggregates highly influence their properties, e.g. shape, density, surface roughness, etc... In turn, these properties affect the interactions the aggregates have in oil and, therefore, the behavior of the oleogel. Using rheology and CLSM, we could have a slightly deeper understanding of how these particle properties controlled the behavior of the oleogels. This thesis enabled me to grow in more than one way, both scientifically and personally. I was able to learn new lab techniques, but also how to manage your own project, balancing your lifestyle, perseverance, how to communicate your results to others, and planning. I would like to thank my supervisors, Roos Scheermeijer and Elke Scholten 🟥 , for their support, insights, and guidance. Also, to everyone from the oleogel group for collaborating with me. Lastly, I'm grateful to the Physics and Physical Chemistry of Foods - Wageningen University and Research , and Wageningen University & Research for the opportunities and chances they have given me to walk a few more steps towards my dreams. I'm excited for what the future holds and the many opportunities, experiences, and challenges that will come my way.

post_text: I recently found myself in Norwich, and parked the car in my second favourite car park in the city, at Benedict’s Gate* I’ve got a long history with this car park, having been involved in the St Benedict’s project from an early stage. I also had more than a passing involvement in the design of both the car parking and the work to install new walking and cycling infrastructure on St Swithin’s and St Benedict’s Street. As for all my projects, I like to swing by when I get chance and take a look to see how things are faring. I wasn’t expecting to see a big group of teens and early 20-somethings skateboarding and quietly sitting in a car parking bay listening to music. There was a certain amount of uncertainty and shyness from them when I walked over to say ‘hi’ – but once I explained that I was involved in the design of the car park and was curious about what made it so attractive to them, they were happy to have a chat as this is “definitely the best” place to skateboard in Norwich because (quote): 1. “The lighting is really good 2. You can see across the whole of the car park and don’t feel worried that they are going to get hassled 3. The security crew in the accommodation come down for a chat every now and then 4. The car park pavement has no large bits in it [aggregate], so you don’t get wounded 5. It’s covered so dry in the bad weather. 6. The only thing it is missing is some half pipes” It's striking that the reasons that they like the car park is for the same reasons that I like the car park. It feels safe. It's overlooked, well lit, with no dark corners, and there is security nearby. The skaters just want to get on with their thing, without bothering other people and without being moved on. But it’s telling (to my shame) that their appreciation for it feeling safe surprised me. This has made me think about how we plan the most functional of infrastructure. And there isn’t much more functional than car parking, except possibly power stations. The Copenhill waste to energy power station in Copenhagen processes around half a million tonnes of waste each year, powering 150,000 homes. Yet it is also the city’s “epicentre for urban mountain sport” with a ski slope, hiking trails and a major climbing wall incorporated to the building’s design. Copenhill’s designer, Bjarke Ingels, has spoken of Copenhill as being, “A crystal clear example of hedonistic sustainability – that a sustainable city is not only better for the environment – it is also more enjoyable for the lives of its citizens." Could or should the same principle extend to all our public infrastructure? In many ways, this is exactly what TfL’s Healthy Streets initiatives are capturing, and what underpins so much of the Safe Roads for All strategy. If we want to create healthy communities, then should we be asking more of our public infrastructure to achieve that aim – should parts of our transport system also be specifically designed to be hedonistically sustainable? As well as the need for more public toilets, bench seating and street trees, should we be examining our designs to look for ways we can do more for the communities they will be built in? What could have happened if our team had considered the empty car park as a possible location for skaters or at least a third place for the Golden Triangle’s teenagers? Could we have slightly changed materials to dampen it acoustically? Installed simple perch seating as part of the curtain wall screening? Thought how to communicate to people parking there that their cars are safer from having skateboarders carefully practicing nearby thanks to the free security and overlooking (and that there is nothing to fear from a bunch of teens sat discreetly on the ground, listening to Twenty One Pilots)? So often I see consultation remarks that skateboarders are a menace to the public realm, damaging seating and kerbs with their tricks. Could we (should we?) be looking to design in some resilience to those spaces, creating areas which can better withstand the impact of skaters rather than anti-socially looking to delimit their activity in public spaces? How far are we prepared to take the concept of inclusive design? If it means getting more use out of our public infrastructure: encouraging more activity in general, and in urban areas in particular, then is it time to start thinking about infrastructure differently and bringing a little more hedonistic sustainability to our everyday lives? * for what it is worth, the Rose Lane MSCP gets my vote for best car park in the city.

South Sudan has mismanaged an estimated $25 billion in oil revenue since 2011, undermining public services and deepening the humanitarian crisis. From a policy perspective, this reflects sustained governance failures that have translated directly into widespread hunger and instability. With more than 7 million people facing severe food insecurity and the U.S. Department of State signaling potential aid reductions after investing $9.5 billion, accountability and genuine partnership are essential to prevent further deterioration.

Have you ever wondered how registered apprenticeships work? Apprentices have the opportunity to immediately apply what they learn in the classroom to build real-world skills. Work-based learning under the mentorship of an experienced professional ensures that apprentices can build knowledge in context rather than merely trying to understand abstract concepts. 

Often adult learners learn better in alternative settings than the regular classroom environment, and RAs allow students who learn better with visual and hands-on assessments to really shine. Get educated about #Apprenticeships and consider getting your adult education program involved today!

Learn more about the benefits of RAs! https://lnkd.in/emtJiJDR

Have you ever wondered how registered apprenticeships work? Apprentices have the opportunity to immediately apply what they learn in the classroom to build real-world skills. Work-based learning under the mentorship of an experienced professional ensures that apprentices can build knowledge in context rather than merely trying to understand abstract concepts.

Often adult learners learn better in alternative settings than the regular classroom environment, and RAs allow students who learn better with visual and hands-on assessments to really shine. Get educated about #Apprenticeships and consider getting your adult education program involved today!

Learn more about the benefits of RAs! https://lnkd.in/emtJiJDR

post_text:
DO GOOD.

IT WILL COME BACK TO YOU
IN UNEXPECTED WAYS

Agree?? 💯 💯 

Do good even when nobody notices. 

The world has a way of remembering kindness. The help you give, the respect you show, and the good you put into people's lives often return when you least expect it. 

Sometimes not from the same person, not in the same form, but always in a way that reminds you that goodness is never wasted

We've encountered a technical issue following a recent Dentrix update that’s causing a "Database connection issue." This problem is primarily due to new automatic updates, where sometimes the server updates, but the workstations don’t—leading to potential office-wide disruptions.

Here’s what you need to know:
Issue Description: The update causes connection problems if the server updates but the workstations do not.
Possible Fix: Often, a manual reboot of the server is required. After the server restarts, the issue usually resolves.
Recommended Action: If you face this issue, call Real IT Solutions at 616.209.8900 for professional help. Alternatively, you can reboot the server yourself and then manually check each workstation for updates.

Stay proactive to avoid downtime! 💻🔧

Developing EnviroShield has been a journey of learning and growth—combining my expertise in algae with a deep dive into skincare formulation. This serum reflects my commitment to sustainability, science, and creating products that truly make a difference.

With a spa-like luxury and the powerful benefits of algae, EnviroShield is more than skincare—it’s a connection between science and self-care.

post_text: On my trip to Antarctica and the South Georgia Islands we got to learn more about the incredible man, explorer and leader Sir Earnest Shackleton. Shackleton famously was a “failure” in his goal to reach the South Pole. However he is widely regarded as one of the best leaders that has ever lived. It has got me thinking about leadership, what really is “success” and how you lead in times of disaster and difficulties is the true test of leadership and courage. You will see many blue sky photos of Antartica in the brochures but the reality is a wild, cold, beautiful but inhospitable place, the reality of what Shakelton and his men faced. Attached are some of the lessons learnt from Shakelton - “what would Shakelton do?”. How can I measure up to these lessons is what I am thinking about as we visit this beautiful place.

post_text:
O1 vs Sonnet Fight for $50,000!

How does Claude3.5-sonnet Agent compete against o1-preview Agent for $50k Kaggle Challege?

Last week, I shared an experiment where an AI agent participated in an active Kaggle competition with a $50,000 prize pool. 

To evaluate the best coding mode, I decided to try sonnet this week, after o1. 

Below are the results:
1️⃣ o1-preview ranked in the bottom 1% (1447th/1457) with an (Root Mean Square Error)RMSE-loss of 0.594.
2️⃣ Claude3.5-sonnet was also in the bottom 1% but the RMSE-loss increased to 0.851.
3️⃣ Whereas GPT-4o, but it couldn’t even produce a valid submission.

This is not surprising, as o1 has much more horsepower than sonnet

But what about the cost? sonnet was ~40% cheaper than o1 with only ~30% reduction in RMSE Score

this is still super exciting as an AI agent can autonomously generate a functional solution in just a couple of hours in less than $1.

Next up: 
1. Evaluate the performance latest Gemini experimental model
2. Test on other active challenges that require fine-tuning a LLM
3. Make this agent an effective copilot for ML engineers/developers 

If you have suggestions, ideas, or thoughts on tasks I should try with this agent, I’d love to hear from you.

LLMs: The Real Difference Between “Full” and “Parameter-Efficient” Fine-Tuning In the world of Large Language Models, fine-tuning is where the real magic happens — but not all fine-tuning is created equal. Here’s the breakdown 👇 🔹 Full Fine-Tuning You update every single weight in the model. ✅ Maximum performance on your task ❌ Requires enormous GPU memory ❌ Creates a new copy of the model for each task Great for research labs. Not so practical for startups or rapid experimentation. 🔹 Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) You freeze the base model and train only a small set of adapter parameters. Techniques like LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, and Spectrum make this possible. 💡 The SuperAnnotate team notes that LoRA can reduce trainable parameters by up to 10,000× while still delivering near full-tuning performance. That means lower GPU bills, faster iteration, and less catastrophic forgetting. 🔹 Alternative Adaptation Methods Other approaches — like multi-task fine-tuning, sequential fine-tuning, and instruction tuning — teach models to handle multiple tasks or follow human-like prompts. And if you want knowledge without retraining? Use RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — it doesn’t touch model weights at all, just brings in external context when needed. 💭 The takeaway: Fine-tuning isn’t one-size-fits-all. O1 vs Sonnet Fight for $50,000!

How does Claude3.5-sonnet Agent compete against o1-preview Agent for $50k Kaggle Challege?

Last week, I shared an experiment where an AI agent participated in an active Kaggle competition with a $50,000 prize pool.

To evaluate the best coding mode, I decided to try sonnet this week, after o1.

Below are the results:
1️⃣ o1-preview ranked in the bottom 1% (1447th/1457) with an (Root Mean Square Error)RMSE-loss of 0.594.
2️⃣ Claude3.5-sonnet was also in the bottom 1% but the RMSE-loss increased to 0.851.
3️⃣ Whereas GPT-4o, but it couldn’t even produce a valid submission.

This is not surprising, as o1 has much more horsepower than sonnet

But what about the cost? sonnet was ~40% cheaper than o1 with only ~30% reduction in RMSE Score

this is still super exciting as an AI agent can autonomously generate a functional solution in just a couple of hours in less than $1.

Next up:
1. Evaluate the performance latest Gemini experimental model
2. Test on other active challenges that require fine-tuning a LLM
3. Make this agent an effective copilot for ML engineers/developers

If you have suggestions, ideas, or thoughts on tasks I should try with this agent, I’d love to hear from you.

post_text: Many businesses rely on outsourcing. Bringing everything in-house is an unrealistic aim for most companies, so the problem facing many entrepreneur is one of selection - which aspects of the business should be handled in-house and which should be outsourced? Here is an explanation of the advantages and disadvantages associated with outsourcing sales functions to a third-party organisation. One advantage of outsourcing sales is that it can release senior staff members from the administrative hassle associated with sales implementation and management, freeing up valuable human resources for other administrative tasks. Choosing to outsource sales at an early stage can spare your business the recruitment costs associated with sourcing and securing an experienced and competent sales team. Recruitment also requires a considerable investment of time and senior-level human resources, so outsourcing sales can greatly increase speed of response and enable a business to become operational within a shorter time frame. An in-house sales team represents a constant drain on resources through salaries and this can reduce the flexibility of a business. Outsourcing sales work to a reputable agency can spare your business the year-round commitment of paying salaries and replace it with a flexible arrangement that takes into account the possibility of heightened periods of sales activity, e.g. around Christmas time, interspersed with periods of lower activity. Agencies are also able to recruit staff to profile for particular jobs. Outsourcing sales can also be a means of accessing the most developed sales skills and the most experienced sales personnel. Agencies that specialist in sales are often better equipped to provide an effective sales service than an enterprise with many other interests. On the other hand, outsourcing sales does reduce the level of control exerted by a business over its sales practices and personnel. Although there are opportunities to write any level of micromanagement into an outsourcing contract, this defeats part of the object of outsourcing in the first place. Problems can sometimes arise from third-party organizations misrepresenting or mis-selling the products of a business and this can create legal problems. Sales personnel from an agency may not be as familiar with your products as your own staff members and this too can create problems in some situations. Another disadvantage of outsourcing sales is that financial savings are not as apparent here as they are in many other areas. It is difficult to calculate a cost comparison between outsourcing and non-outsourcing scenarios over an extended period of time, leading some businesses to treat sales outsourcing with mistrust. sales outsourcing is not the best option for every business, but it brings several significant advantages over a non-outsourcing scenario - chief among these are improved speed of response, increased flexibility, lower recruitment costs, more specialist personnel, and reduced administrative commitments for senior staff. In many cases, field sales solutions can be carried out more effectively by a third-party organisation and outsourcing sales can enable a business to respond more quickly and efficiently than working with an in-house team.

post_text: How to Build a Trading Routine That Reduces Psychological Errors A strong trading routine automates discipline, eliminating moments where psychology fails. It's your essential pre-game ritual for the mind The Blueprint for a Resilient Routine Pre-Market (15 min): Review your written trading plan. Check the economic calendar. Set your daily rules—and do not change them Trading Session: Follow your plan mechanically. Use alarms to end pre-defined blocks (e.g., 90 mins). When the alarm sounds, take a 10-minute trading break Post-Market (20 min): Journal objectively. Log trades, note any rule deviations, and plan for tomorrow. Then, mentally declare the day over Why It Works A routine reduces decision fatigue and creates predictability. When actions become habitual, you're less likely to deviate due to emotion or trading impulse Common Routine Gaps to Avoid · Trading without a clear session plan · Skipping breaks, increasing fatigue-driven errors · Neglecting the post-market review, missing crucial learning Real Trading Discipline Examples · Anna K.: Used to jump into trades at the open. A strict 15-minute pre-market planning block eliminated her impulsive opening trades · Mark T.: Traded for hours without breaks, leading to revenge trading. His 90-minute session alarms now force a reset, preserving trading focus Conclusion Your routine is your first defense against trading psychology. Structure your time to make disciplined actions automatic. Consistency in routine breeds consistency in results From the trading giant's blog. https://lnkd.in/dtC335hw

How to Build a Trading Routine That Reduces Psychological Errors
 
A strong trading routine automates discipline, eliminating moments where psychology fails. It's your essential pre-game ritual for the mind
 
The Blueprint for a Resilient Routine
 
Pre-Market (15 min): Review your written trading plan. Check the economic calendar. Set your daily rules—and do not change them
Trading Session: Follow your plan mechanically. Use alarms to end pre-defined blocks (e.g., 90 mins). When the alarm sounds, take a 10-minute trading break
Post-Market (20 min): Journal objectively. Log trades, note any rule deviations, and plan for tomorrow. Then, mentally declare the day over
 
Why It Works
A routine reduces decision fatigue and creates predictability. When actions become habitual, you're less likely to deviate due to emotion or trading impulse
 
Common Routine Gaps to Avoid
 
· Trading without a clear session plan
· Skipping breaks, increasing fatigue-driven errors
· Neglecting the post-market review, missing crucial learning
 
Real Trading Discipline Examples
 
· Anna K.: Used to jump into trades at the open. A strict 15-minute pre-market planning block eliminated her impulsive opening trades
· Mark T.: Traded for hours without breaks, leading to revenge trading. His 90-minute session alarms now force a reset, preserving trading focus
 
Conclusion
Your routine is your first defense against trading psychology. Structure your time to make disciplined actions automatic. Consistency in routine breeds consistency in results
