Beyond Coins & Cards: Uncovering Overlooked Investment-Grade Collectibles When most people hear “collectibles,” they picture baseball cards, comic books, or coins. And while those can be solid investments, there’s a world of under-the-radar items quietly climbing in value—with less competition and often greater long-term upside. If you’re looking to diversify your collection and build enduring value, here are some often-overlooked categories of investment-grade collectibles worth considering. Vintage Jewelry and Signed Pieces Pieces from Cartier, Tiffany & Co., and Van Cleef & Arpels aren’t just beautiful—they hold and grow value. Art Deco and Mid-Century styles crafted in high-karat gold or platinum continue to outperform. Bonus: Original boxes, certificates, and provenance can double or triple market value. Vintage Film Memorabilia Original movie props, scripts, film reels, and wardrobe pieces from iconic films—think Star Wars or Indiana Jones—remain high-demand, low-supply assets. Collectors pay significant premiums for authentic Hollywood history, and values continue to climb as these pieces become rarer. Foreign Silver and Historical Bullion Many collectors overlook this category. Examples include 19th-century Latin American pesos, European crowns, and Middle Eastern trade coinage with .720 to .925 silver content. These coins are harder to find, often undervalued, and rich in historical significance. Vintage Toys off the Beaten Path Collectible toys go well beyond Star Wars figures or Barbie dolls. Early wind-ups, obscure European diecast models, and even short-lived toy lines in pristine condition can command strong value. Look for original packaging, limited production runs, and unique mechanical features. Stock Certificates and Historic Ephemera Old stock certificates—particularly from railroads, steel companies, or early technology firms—have become highly collectible. Scarcity, design quality, and historical relevance all influence market value. Framed, these certificates serve as both investment pieces and striking decor. Casino Chips and “Dead” Club Memorabilia Chips and tokens from closed casinos or private clubs can be worth far more than their face value. The rarer the chip—and the more notorious the venue—the higher the premium. This niche market continues to show surprising potential for serious collectors. Why This Matters The best investments are often the ones everyone else overlooks. Items with story, scarcity, and authenticity tend to hold their own—and often outperform—when chosen wisely and preserved well. Whether you’re collecting for passion, protection, or legacy, blind spots in the market are where real opportunity lives. Gold, and the Shifting Balance of Global Value For centuries, gold has been the ultimate measure of wealth and stability. It has been the reserve of nations, the cornerstone of investment portfolios, and the cultural anchor across civilizations. Gold will continue to hold that space—it is too deeply embedded in financial systems and human psychology to lose its throne. But we are entering a fascinating inflection point. The silver-to-gold ratio breaking its long-standing pattern is more than a market anomaly—it’s a signal. Silver is no longer just “the poor man’s gold.” Its dual role as both an industrial metal and a store of value is reshaping how economies, investors, and consumers see it. A few observations: Macroeconomics & Accessibility With gold crossing affordability thresholds, its demand as adornment is slowing. It is increasingly treated as a locked asset, rather than wearable wealth. Silver, on the other hand, still provides accessibility—an entry point for millions of consumers globally who aspire to own meaningful jewelry that balances beauty with value. Consumer Behavior & Democratization of Luxury The modern customer is more discerning, but also more pragmatic. They seek creativity, differentiation, and emotional value at a price point that does not feel exclusionary. Silver jewelry provides this canvas—designers can experiment with form, texture, and gemstone pairings in ways that gold pricing simply restricts. This democratization of luxury will fuel sustained demand. Geopolitical & Industrial Dynamics Silver’s role in clean energy (solar, EVs, batteries) ensures long-term industrial demand. This intertwines jewelry markets with broader economic forces. As silver becomes scarcer through industrial absorption, jewelry pieces made today may carry not only aesthetic but strategic value in the decades ahead. The Future of the Jewelry Industry I do not see silver replacing gold—it will complement it. Gold will remain a financial hedge. Silver will become a cultural hedge. It represents wearable identity, artistic freedom, and the democratization of elegance. For us at Kanaya Silver , this trend is not a surprise. We have long believed that silver is the true artisan’s canvas—rooted in heritage, but alive with potential for innovation. It is the medium through which jewelry can remain accessible, relevant, and emotionally powerful in a world where gold risks becoming confined to vaults. The global jewelry economy is moving towards a dual-metal narrative: Gold: Stability, tradition, financial security. Silver: Creativity, accessibility, cultural expression. Both will co-exist, but I believe silver’s cultural capital will only expand in the years to come. Back in 2011, BlueStone set out to do what many thought was impossible: convince Indians to buy gold and diamonds online.

At its core was a bold belief that India’s jewelry market, dominated for generations by family jewelers, was ready to be reshaped by design, technology, and above all, trust.

What began as a 33-slide idea deck is today a billion-dollar public company, proving that conviction paired with clarity can rewrite an entire category.

On PitchCraft Season 2, Founder Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and early investor Prashanth Prakash, revisit that very first deck, surfacing lessons every founder can carry forward:

𝟭. 𝗣𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗮 𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗺𝗼𝗮𝘁

From his Amazon years, Gaurav saw that horizontal players could swallow many verticals. Jewelry was different: it demanded specialist supply chains, design expertise, and a trust equation outsiders couldn’t easily replicate.

Lesson: When giants loom, pick a space where differentiation is baked into the category itself.

𝟮. 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

Buying jewelry online in 2011 seemed absurd. BlueStone answered with 3D renders more lifelike than photographs, alloy replicas for home try-ons, and a 30-day money-back promise. These weren’t features; they were trust signals.

Lesson: In high-friction markets, innovation lies in reducing anxiety, not just in refining the product.

𝟯. 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗯𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗱, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗳𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁

The first roadmap imagined solitaires, watches, and even men’s accessories. Reality forced discipline. Solitaires were too spec-driven, margins too thin. What clicked was everyday, design-led jewelry.

Lesson: Ambition sets direction, but survival depends on pruning fast and doubling down on where you’re truly distinct.

𝟰. 𝗦𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗱𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁’𝘀 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗲𝗱

Jewelry isn’t built in a funding cycle. Even Tanishq struggled for its first decade. Credibility compounds over years, not months.

Lesson: In brand-heavy categories, patience and persistence are as important as capital.

𝟱. 𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿’𝘀 𝗱𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆

As Prashanth recalls, 'It was the person behind the deck first.' What stood out wasn’t just jewelry, but Gaurav’s conviction that India wouldn’t follow the US diamond-centric path, and gold and design would define this market.

Lesson: First-principles insight often outweighs the TAM slide.

𝟲. 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗲𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲, 𝘀𝗼 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂

BlueStone’s early bet that internet-savvy men would buy gifts didn’t hold. The real customers? Married women, 25-45, building new lives away from their family jeweler.

Lesson: Hypotheses will fail. Winners are those who grow with their customers.

As we wrap up the year, thrilled to share a brand-new episode—perfect for reflecting on all the AI advancements of 2024.

🎯 Practical use cases of Generative AI (allergen detection, customer support systems)
🧠 Building and scaling Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines
🚧 Overcoming common challenges in productionizing AI

💫 Privacy and security considerations in Gen AI
💫 RAG vs. fine-tuning: when to use which
💫 Lessons from scaling and integrating Gen AI solutions

post_text: Summer breaks homework, always brings back memories of fun experiences, travel and plays. Atul, A city boy, was no exception .While doing his summer break homework , remembered his native and Raju, his best friend who he spent a lot of time with during the vacations . They shared a special bond, Atul learned new things from Raju, and Raju was taught new city things from Atul.However, Raju’s life was tough as his father was an alcoholic and forced him to work for long hours. This summer when Atul visited his native, he wasn't accompanied by Raju, as he was busy doing his “secret work”. Later Atul stumbled across Raju working under very harsh conditions forced by the adults around him. After returning to school, Atul saw Raju by a dumpster but thought it’s just his imagination and went home. However, his mom informed him that Raju ran away from home tired of all the work and his father’s behaviour under alcohol. Atul sets on a mission to find his friend, during his search he stumbles upon the harsh reality of this world. Child labor, Illiteracy, and “nameless Raju’s”. As he delved deeper, his heart sank, with the news of discoveries of children working in hazardous conditions, families forcing their kids into labor due to poverty and lack of education, innocent lives being crushed for meeting adult expectations. These instances shocked him and he decided to share it to his classmates , to which his teacher explained how child labor takes place in society , how children are raised by parents only for labor money. She also explains to the students about their rights and also explains how the UN Convention on Rights of the Child acts as the guardian angel for all the children. Atul also learns more about such children through online and news channels. Atul’s eyes opened up to the reality of the world, that childhood is a luxury only few could afford. A devastating reality which we know exists, ruining lives of the young and without access to education, they are like soldiers in a battlefield without any weapons to shield. Education is the foundation on which dreams are built, opportunities are captured and potentials are realized. Locking a child up and forcing labor, is not only a violation of their rights but a theft of their childhood, of their innocence. Ignoring the education of a child is condemning a cycle of poverty and exploitation. Therefore, it is crucial that we prioritize education and abolish the practice of child labor well and thorough , only then can we ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive, learn and reach their utmost potential. Reference:- Raju and I, Short film (ASEEMA)

post_text: As the EACH Cardiovascular Health Summit unfolds, MEP Maria Walsh (EPP, Ireland) reflects on the transformative potential of the upcoming European Cardiovascular Health Plan. 💡 The plan has the real potential to transform how we tackle the leading cause of death in Europe, by keeping people healthy for longer, strengthening prevention, improving early detection and treatment, and ensuring services are accessible and equitable for all. If we are serious about cardiovascular health, nobody and nothing can be left behind, including: 🔹 Rehabilitation, which is the essential bridge from survival to full participation in life. 🔹 Mental health, a critical and still unmet need for many cardiovascular patients. 🔹 Addressing inequalities: women and young people continue to be overlooked. CVD is the number one cause of death for women in Europe, yet women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and face higher mortality after heart attacks. 🔹 Supporting national heart foundations, which keep communities strong and help people stay out of the hospital. 🎥 Tune into the EACH Summit livestream on YouTube: https://lnkd.in/edzct68s #CVHealthForAll #EACHSummit2025

As the EACH Cardiovascular Health Summit unfolds, MEP Maria Walsh (EPP, Ireland) reflects on the transformative potential of the upcoming European Cardiovascular Health Plan.

💡 The plan has the real potential to transform how we tackle the leading cause of death in Europe, by keeping people healthy for longer, strengthening prevention, improving early detection and treatment, and ensuring services are accessible and equitable for all.

If we are serious about cardiovascular health, nobody and nothing can be left behind, including:
🔹 Rehabilitation, which is the essential bridge from survival to full participation in life.
🔹 Mental health, a critical and still unmet need for many cardiovascular patients.
🔹 Addressing inequalities: women and young people continue to be overlooked. CVD is the number one cause of death for women in Europe, yet women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and face higher mortality after heart attacks.
🔹 Supporting national heart foundations, which keep communities strong and help people stay out of the hospital.

🎥 Tune into the EACH Summit livestream on YouTube: https://lnkd.in/edzct68s

#CVHealthForAll #EACHSummit2025

Learning the Basics Made Me a Better Developer I didn’t become a better developer by learning more frameworks. I became better when I went back to the basics. Early in my journey, I thought “progress” meant stacking tools on my CV. New framework. New library. New buzzwords. But during interviews, real projects, and debugging sessions… the cracks showed. What actually changed things for me was rebuilding my foundation. When I focused on: How JavaScript really works (not just syntax) How the browser interprets HTML & CSS How data flows through an application How to read and understand errors instead of avoiding them I noticed a shift. I could explain my code, not just write it. I could debug faster, not panic. I could learn new frameworks quickly — because the concepts made sense. From a hiring perspective, this mattered. Frameworks can be taught. Strong fundamentals, clear thinking, and problem-solving skills are much harder to train. That’s why I now believe this: 👉 The basics don’t make you slower — they make you employable. If you’re preparing for interviews or trying to stand out as a developer, don’t skip the fundamentals. 2025 was the year everyone talked about AI, data, digital transformation…

And while all of that matters, it’s not what FM teams ask me about.

They ask for something simpler:
Less noise.
Less duplication.
Less proving themselves every day.
Less friction between teams and contractors.

For 2026 and beyond, I think FM needs three things:

Tools that lighten workload, not increase oversight.
Data that’s actually usable, not just visual.
Leadership that listens before deciding.

FM doesn’t need more buzzwords.
It needs support.

That’s the direction we’re taking into 2026.

#FacilitiesManagement #FacilitiesServices #FM

En BIP Agencia sabemos que hoy en día disponer de un seguro que garantice la educación de tus hijos tanto en el colegio como en la universidad es una prioridad... Es por eso que en este blog te explicaremos cómo un seguro de vida con un componente de ahorro puede ser la clave para asegurar su futuro y sobre todo cómo puede ayudar a cumplir tus metas personales, sin dejar de brindar estabilidad a tu familia. ¿Cómo asegurar la educación de tus hijos hijos? Uno de los mayores desafíos financieros que enfrentan los padres es costear la educación de sus hijos, incluso en su ausencia. Los gastos escolares, universitarios y extracurriculares tienden a aumentar cada año. Aquí es donde un seguro de vida entra en juego como una solución ideal para garantizar la educación de tus hijos. Con un seguro de vida con componente de ahorro para estudios universitarios , puedes crear un plan a largo plazo que asegure que, pase lo que pase, habrá fondos disponibles para cubrir su educación . Ya sea que estés ahorrando para la universidad o quieras garantizar una educación de calidad en el extranjero desde los primeros años , un seguro de vida te brinda la tranquilidad de que tus hijos estarán protegidos financieramente. Otra alternativa para asegurar la educación de tus hijos es mediante una póliza de seguro de vida con opción de inversión, lo que significa que los montos que inviertas se pueden utilizar en diferentes instrumentos financieros para obtener mejores resultados, además que no está sujeta a factores volátiles y proporciona acumulación de valores a una tasa competitiva y superiores a las de los bancos, por lo que se puede pagar en pocos años la póliza. Tranquilidad de planificar para el mañana Un seguro de vida también te permite tener una visión a largo plazo de tu futuro financiero. Si eliges un seguro de vida con un componente de ahorro o inversión , estás creando una reserva que puede ayudarte en momentos clave. Puedes aprovechar este ahorro para múltiples propósitos, como financiar proyectos familiares, emprender un negocio o incluso para asegurar tu retiro. Esto significa que, un seguro de vida con ahorro puede ser tu mejor aliado en caso de una eventualidad económica. Esta previsión te da la capacidad de reaccionar ante imprevistos sin comprometer tus metas de largo plazo. Invertir en un seguro de vida con componente de ahorro o inversión, no solo garantiza la seguridad de tu familia, sino que también te permite cumplir tus metas personales y garantizar un futuro brillante para tus hijos. post_text:
Sometimes the worst spot you can be is in your own head. 

I’m going to be vulnerable here.

The last few weeks I’ve been in my own head A LOT. 

Despite all my accomplishments, I’ve been feeling pretty low.

Not depressed. 

Just blah. Uninspired. And not important.

In some capacities, I feel I have a lot of content I could create to help others achieve things I have…  but then usually talk myself out of it.

Why??

In my own head.

Likely a bit of imposter syndrome. 

I shared this with my wife tonight and honestly she was baffled at this.

Of all the things I am… inexperienced isn’t really one of them.

Tonight became a reminder that if you’re not careful… the forces of average and FEAR can cripple you if you’re not careful

Fear comes in MANY forms and not just feeling afraid.

- Feeling inadequate.

- Feeling like you shouldn’t even try because it will likely fail. 

- Avoiding creating for fear of what people will think.

- procrastination is also a form of fear… because often we are just crippled by fear.


This design is 10 years old.

I made it for myself and never printed it and I’m thinking of making it

When we started Kick Print I was so scared that I almost didn’t do it.

Then I got mad at myself. 

Similar to how I am right now. 

And I made this design and just kept it as a wallpaper. 

But I think I need to print a few of these and give them out to people as a reminder. 

Give fear a Kick To the face! 

So make the calls you need to make.

Put yourself out there.

Because NOT moving is worse than failing. 

Reminder to both myself as well.

Sometimes the worst spot you can be is in your own head.

I’m going to be vulnerable here.

The last few weeks I’ve been in my own head A LOT.

Despite all my accomplishments, I’ve been feeling pretty low.

Not depressed.

Just blah. Uninspired. And not important.

In some capacities, I feel I have a lot of content I could create to help others achieve things I have… but then usually talk myself out of it.

Why??

In my own head.

Likely a bit of imposter syndrome.

I shared this with my wife tonight and honestly she was baffled at this.

Of all the things I am… inexperienced isn’t really one of them.

Tonight became a reminder that if you’re not careful… the forces of average and FEAR can cripple you if you’re not careful

Fear comes in MANY forms and not just feeling afraid.

- Feeling inadequate.

- Feeling like you shouldn’t even try because it will likely fail.

- Avoiding creating for fear of what people will think.

- procrastination is also a form of fear… because often we are just crippled by fear.


This design is 10 years old.

I made it for myself and never printed it and I’m thinking of making it

When we started Kick Print I was so scared that I almost didn’t do it.

Then I got mad at myself.

Similar to how I am right now.

And I made this design and just kept it as a wallpaper.

But I think I need to print a few of these and give them out to people as a reminder.

Give fear a Kick To the face!

So make the calls you need to make.

Put yourself out there.

Because NOT moving is worse than failing.

Reminder to both myself as well.

post_text: Quantitative research is the process of collecting and analyzing numerical data . It can be used to find patterns and averages, make predictions, test causal relationships , and generalize results to wider populations. Quantitative research is the opposite of qualitative research , which involves collecting and analyzing non-numerical data (e.g., text, video, or audio). Quantitative research is widely used in the natural and social sciences: biology, chemistry, psychology, economics, sociology, marketing, etc. Quantitative research methods You can use quantitative research methods for descriptive, correlational or experimental research . In descriptive research , you simply seek an overall summary of your study variables. In correlational research , you investigate relationships between your study variables. In experimental research , you systematically examine whether there is a cause-and-effect relationship between variables. Correlational and experimental research can both be used to formally test hypotheses , or predictions, using statistics. The results may be generalised to broader populations based on the sampling method used. To collect quantitative data, you will often need to use operational definitions that translate abstract concepts (e.g., mood) into observable and quantifiable measures (e.g., self-ratings of feelings and energy levels). Quantitative data analysis Once data is collected, you may need to process it before it can be analysed. For example, survey and test data may need to be transformed from words to numbers. Then, you can use statistical analysis to answer your research questions . Descriptive statistics will give you a summary of your data and include measures of averages and variability. You can also use graphs, scatter plots and frequency tables to visualise your data and check for any trends or outliers. Using inferential statistics , you can make predictions or generalisations based on your data. You can test your hypothesis or use your sample data to estimate the population parameter . Advantages of quantitative research Quantitative research is often used to standardise data collection and generalise findings . Strengths of this approach include: Replication Repeating the study is possible because of standardised data collection protocols and tangible definitions of abstract concepts. Direct comparisons of results The study can be reproduced in other cultural settings, times or with different groups of participants. Results can be compared statistically. Large samples Data from large samples can be processed and analyzed using reliable and consistent procedures through quantitative data analysis. Hypothesis testing Using formalized and established hypothesis testing procedures means that you have to carefully consider and report your research variables, predictions, data collection and testing methods before coming to a conclusion. Disadvantages of quantitative research Despite the benefits of quantitative research, it is sometimes inadequate in explaining complex research topics. Its limitations include Superficiality Using precise and restrictive operational definitions may inadequately represent complex concepts. For example, the concept of mood may be represented with just a number in quantitative research, but explained with elaboration in qualitative research. Narrow focus Predetermined variables and measurement procedures can mean that you ignore other relevant observations. Structural bias Despite standardised procedures, structural biases can still affect quantitative research. Missing data , imprecise measurements or inappropriate sampling methods are biases that can lead to the wrong conclusions. Lack of context Quantitative research often uses unnatural settings like laboratories or fails to consider historical and cultural contexts that may affect data collection and results.

I almost quit using AI when answers felt shallow. But then I tried this.

I was getting answers.

But they felt…
surface-level.

No depth.
No reasoning.
Just conclusions.

That’s when I learned about Chain-of-Thought Prompting.

Instead of asking for the answer,
I asked the AI to think step by step.

And everything changed.

Chain-of-Thought Prompting means:

You explicitly ask the AI to:

Break the problem into steps
Explain its reasoning
Show how it reached the answer

It’s like asking a student:
“Don’t just give the result show your working.”

The result?
Clear logic.
Fewer mistakes.
Much deeper insights.

The big takeaway:
If you want better answers, ask for better thinking.

👉 Be honest:
Do you usually ask for answers… or for reasoning?
Let’s discuss 👇

It can serve as a powerful storytelling medium, while also holding the potential to enable the creator economy. post_text: Temporary employees play a critical role in many organizations, especially in industries with fluctuating workloads or seasonal demands. Including them in safety initiatives is essential for both legal compliance and fostering a comprehensive safety culture. Here are key reasons to actively engage temporary employees in safety solutions: 1. Exposure to the Same Risks as Permanent Staff Temporary workers often perform the same tasks as permanent employees, exposing them to similar hazards. Even brief periods of inattention or a lack of familiarity with procedures can lead to accidents. Solution: Involve temporary workers in safety discussions, debriefs, and huddles to ensure they are aware of risks and can contribute to safer practices. 2. Fresh Perspectives and Observations New or temporary workers may notice hazards or inefficiencies that long-term employees have overlooked due to familiarity with the environment. They can provide valuable insights on onboarding processes and suggest improvements for future hires. Example: A temporary worker might highlight a gap in the training process or suggest a clearer way to label hazardous areas. 3. Prevent “Us vs. Them” Dynamics Excluding temporary staff from safety programs can create divisions between them and permanent employees, reducing teamwork and trust. This dynamic can lead to unsafe behaviors, as temporary workers might hesitate to speak up if they feel unwelcome or unsupported. Solution: Encourage participation by treating all workers equally in safety programs, rewarding good safety practices regardless of employment status. Tip: Ensure that temporary employees receive the same safety training, personal protective equipment (PPE), and access to reporting systems as permanent staff. 5. Strengthen Organizational Safety Culture Temporary workers may return for future assignments, so engaging them in safety programs ensures continuity and consistency. A strong safety culture that includes everyone—temporary and permanent workers—reduces overall risks, increasing both trust and productivity. Outcome: Workers who feel included are more likely to report hazards, participate in safety initiatives, and follow protocols, reducing the likelihood of accidents. Summary Including temporary employees in safety solutions ensures that all workers, regardless of tenure, are equipped to handle hazards and contribute to a safe working environment. Their unique perspectives, combined with equal access to safety programs, help prevent incidents and foster a unified, proactive safety culture. Today I'm excited to announce that Merit Systems has raised $10M of seed funding from a16z crypto and Blockchain Capital to unleash Open Source Capitalism.

I'm proud to be joined by Ryan Sproule and Mason Hall. We've done our time in the SWE ranks of Big Tech and the investment committees of VC. We share a passion for progress and intimate familiarity with the economy's existing engine for innovation.

What is Open Source Capitalism?

Engineers working on Open Source Software are the most productive workers in human civilization. Yet macro economic measures fail to capture their output, and outdated legal structures fail to reward them appropriately.

Modern firms are cybernetic organisms. Human and machine intelligence united by shared incentives. The Open Source ecosystem is a larger such organism, a fractal of smaller entities woven together. But it lacks the coordination mechanisms to reach its full potential.

The future of innovation looks different: fluid teams, partial attention, contributions flowing from the edges of the network. Traditional management structures would only constrain and suffocate the dynamic nature that makes these networks thrive.

We're building the infrastructure for an Open Source future at Merit Systems. A system where builders truly own what they build. Where attribution and ownership are enshrined by default, rewarding each contributor in proportion to their merit.

We're refining the factory for innovation, creating a system to focus the world's best minds towards humanity's biggest challenges.

The future belongs to those who build it.

Avalanche’s $1 Billion “War Chest”: A Bold Bid to Reclaim the Layer-1 Throne In a move that’s turning heads across crypto and Wall Street alike, Avalanche (AVAX) is reportedly building a $1 billion war chest — not for venture funding or ecosystem grants — but to buy its own token. It’s a strategy that merges tokenomics, finance, and self-belief. ⚙️ What’s Happening According to the Financial Times, the Avalanche Foundation is launching two U.S.-based entities designed to accumulate and hold AVAX on a massive scale. 🔹 $500 M via a SPAC structure, supported by Dragonfly Capital Together, they’ll create a financial engine meant to strengthen AVAX’s market presence, fund development, and send a message of long-term conviction. In parallel, Anthony Scaramucci’s Hivemind and AgriFORCE are backing AVAX One, a crypto-treasury venture planning to accumulate up to $700 million in AVAX. 🧠 The Strategic Logic Avalanche isn’t just buying its own token — it’s reshaping tokenomics as a financial model. Here’s what they’re betting on: Scarcity = Value Reducing the circulating supply can push upward pressure on price, assuming stable or rising demand. Institutional Confidence Using regulated fundraising structures signals maturity and bridges DeFi with traditional capital markets. Liquidity Support A large on-chain treasury can act as a buffer during volatility and provide liquidity to ecosystem projects. Narrative Power “If we buy, others will too.” Market psychology matters — this creates a powerful perception of internal belief. 🧩 But There Are Big Risks This is not a simple win-button. ❗ Regulatory exposure — SPACs and token buybacks can trigger SEC or CFTC review, especially if U.S. investors are involved. ❗ Market timing — If AVAX is overbought, the treasury may end up underwater. ❗ Governance concerns — Selling discounted tokens to entities tied to the Foundation could raise fairness and transparency issues. ❗ Execution risk — Managing multi-entity capital raises, compliance, and large-scale purchases without spooking markets is complex. 🌐 The Bigger Picture Avalanche’s move comes as the Layer-1 competition heats up again. Ethereum dominates institutional adoption. Solana captured the retail and meme energy. If successful, this $1B treasury could anchor AVAX as a hybrid of tech and finance — a blockchain that not only builds decentralized apps but also manages assets like a sovereign fund. 🔮 What It Means for the Industry This could mark the start of a new trend: → Blockchain protocols acting like central banks, using token reserves to stabilize and grow their ecosystems. Open source projects move like academic research. They are slower, more thoughtful, and often maintained by part-timers who contribute when inspiration strikes. Both open source and commercial projects attract completely different types of engineers, and both types are essential. Open source engineers are tinkerers. They obsess over elegant solutions and build things that last decades. They are not worried about quarterly releases because they're solving problems that matter for the long term. Commercial engineers are grinders. They ship features fast and optimize for what customers actually need right now. They are not building monuments - they are building businesses. Most companies try to force one culture onto everyone, which is a mistake. At Blockstream , we deliberately separate these two cultures. Our open source contributions follow academic timelines and perfectionist standards while our commercial products follow market demands and revenue deadlines. Bitcoin Core improvements, Lightning protocol enhancements, cryptographic research - all of this work happens slowly because it has to be bulletproof. The grinders, on the other hand, ship customer-facing products that generate revenue and prove market demand. Wallets, trading platforms, enterprise tools, the work that happens fast because markets don't wait. Neither approach is superior. They're complementary. Companies that only hire grinders ship fast but build on shaky foundations. Companies that only hire tinkerers build beautiful systems that never reach customers. Today I'm excited to announce that Merit Systems has raised $10M of seed funding from a16z crypto and Blockchain Capital to unleash Open Source Capitalism.

I'm proud to be joined by Ryan Sproule and Mason Hall. We've done our time in the SWE ranks of Big Tech and the investment committees of VC. We share a passion for progress and intimate familiarity with the economy's existing engine for innovation.

What is Open Source Capitalism?

Engineers working on Open Source Software are the most productive workers in human civilization. Yet macro economic measures fail to capture their output, and outdated legal structures fail to reward them appropriately.

Modern firms are cybernetic organisms. Human and machine intelligence united by shared incentives. The Open Source ecosystem is a larger such organism, a fractal of smaller entities woven together. But it lacks the coordination mechanisms to reach its full potential.

The future of innovation looks different: fluid teams, partial attention, contributions flowing from the edges of the network. Traditional management structures would only constrain and suffocate the dynamic nature that makes these networks thrive.

We're building the infrastructure for an Open Source future at Merit Systems. A system where builders truly own what they build. Where attribution and ownership are enshrined by default, rewarding each contributor in proportion to their merit.

We're refining the factory for innovation, creating a system to focus the world's best minds towards humanity's biggest challenges.

The future belongs to those who build it.

For more details, check out:

16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence: Raising Boys to Champion Equality and Reject Violence
The 16 Days of Activism reminds us of the urgent need to end gender-based violence (GBV). But true change begins not just in boardrooms or policies but in how we raise the next generation.
As we advocate for equality, let’s focus on nurturing boys into men who are strong—not through dominance, but through empathy, respect, and accountability. Strength is not aggression. It’s the ability to support, protect, and champion others, especially women and girls, regardless of circumstances.
🔑 Here’s how we can make a difference:
Promote Healthy Masculinity: Teach boys that being a man is about respect, not control.
Encourage Emotional Intelligence: Let boys express emotions and process anger constructively.
Lead by Example: Fathers, mentors, and male role models—show what non-violent strength looks like.
Engage in Conversations: Use this period to challenge gender stereotypes at home, in schools, and in the workplace.
Ending GBV is a shared responsibility. By raising boys to embody feminist values of equality and non-violence, we build a society where mutual respect thrives.
Let’s use these 16 Days of Activism to commit to this vision—one where no woman or girl lives in fear, and every boy grows into a man who uplifts, supports, and empowers.
💬 How are you contributing to this cause? Share your thoughts and actions below.
#16DaysOfActivism #EndGBV #GenderEquality #Feminism #Respect

16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence: Raising Boys to Champion Equality and Reject Violence
The 16 Days of Activism reminds us of the urgent need to end gender-based violence (GBV). But true change begins not just in boardrooms or policies but in how we raise the next generation.
As we advocate for equality, let’s focus on nurturing boys into men who are strong—not through dominance, but through empathy, respect, and accountability. Strength is not aggression. It’s the ability to support, protect, and champion others, especially women and girls, regardless of circumstances.
🔑 Here’s how we can make a difference:
Promote Healthy Masculinity: Teach boys that being a man is about respect, not control.
Encourage Emotional Intelligence: Let boys express emotions and process anger constructively.
Lead by Example: Fathers, mentors, and male role models—show what non-violent strength looks like.
Engage in Conversations: Use this period to challenge gender stereotypes at home, in schools, and in the workplace.
Ending GBV is a shared responsibility. By raising boys to embody feminist values of equality and non-violence, we build a society where mutual respect thrives.
Let’s use these 16 Days of Activism to commit to this vision—one where no woman or girl lives in fear, and every boy grows into a man who uplifts, supports, and empowers.
💬 How are you contributing to this cause? Share your thoughts and actions below.

ETH Agentic Systems Lab 💪🏻💪🏻 Bloom (YC X25)
We’re pumped to announce our next partnership in the AI startup ecosystem.

Bloom is a YC-backed startup unlocking the creator economy for software by making cross-platform app development as simple as speaking into your phone.

Founded by two students, David Oort Alonso and Sirian Maathuis, Bloom eliminates the friction of traditional app development—no code, no backend infra, no App Store Developer accounts, no App Store reviews. Instead, Blooms empowers creators, developers and entrepreneurs to turn ideas into real, deployed, shareable apps in seconds.

With investors like Moonfire, Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, and a group of world-class founders and operators from companies like Hugging Face, Weaviate, Convex, Expo, OpenAI, and Meta, Bloom is building the future of how software is created and shared.

Together, we’re aiming to strengthen the AI ecosystem in Zurich:

✨ Supporting students who want to explore AI coding agents through coursework, in collaboration with Bloom (semester projects, bachelor’s & master’s theses).

✨ Creating opportunities for students to engage directly with the Bloom team and learn what it takes to build an AI startup.

Big thanks to David Oort Alonso and Sirian Maathuis for inspiring and supporting the next generation of AI talent in Zurich and beyond. 🙌

Their story—pivoting twice before building Bloom—is a powerful reminder that true strength often lies in persistence.

👉 Students: Applications for our Genesis Batch are now open! Come with your own idea or team up with Bloom and our other startup partners.

👉 Companies: Interested in collaborating with the ETH Agentic Systems Lab? Now’s the perfect time—we’re just at the beginning of our journey.

Deep tech = hardcore hardware stuff like quantum computing, robotics, advanced materials etc. All these things involve a lot of R&D, have high technical risk and require substantial capital. These products are so complex and cutting-edge that there is a big chance of failure. European investors don't like failures, they want safe bets 🙂 So the road of raising a round for a pre-seed deep tech startup is almost certainly closed (esp. if founder has not previously exited few companies). Most accelerators and incubators don't fit the deep tech pace. They invite projects for 3-month programs - and what can you invent in 3 months in hardware?? Getting grants is a true feat (we did it) and getting a big one is almost impossible. It's also long, you often have to wait for 8-12 months only to be rejected. Many startups don't have enough runway to survive for so long. The only 'space' that offers engineers and inventors an opportunity to develop their tech are universities, they are funded by governments (although better to say 'underfunded' - but it's at least something). But then there is a new problem that these projects are not made for commercialization, so there is an issue with tech transfer. As a result, deep tech in EU is chronically underfunded. ikes":28,"post_id":"7374028920842584065","post_text":"Cambridge startup Hiverge has clinched $5 million seed funding to accelerate a pathfinding ‘algorithm factory’. It has been envisioned to solve a hidden yet critical business challenge: discovering and deploying algorithms that help organisations rapidly improve their operations at scale. Big name investors were buzzing around the company's Hive platform. Flying Fish Partners in Seattle led the seed funding round, with Ahren Innovation Capital and Google DeepMind chief scientist Dr Jeff Dean among the other backers. Hiverge, whose registered office is in Station Road, has reimagined algorithmic coding through program synthesis. Hive combines AI creativity with rigorous testing, designed to discover breakthrough algorithms that solve the toughest optimisation headaches. Founders include CEO Alhussein Fawzi , a former Google DeepMind research scientist and MIT Innovators Under 35 award winner, CTO Bernardino Romera Paredes , also a former Google DeepMind research scientist and part of the Nobel prize-winning AlphaFold team, and chief science officer Hamza Fawzi , a professor in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics (DAMTP) at the University of Cambridge and a specialist in mathematical optimisation. Fawzi said: “Algorithms drive the revenue of most businesses today – from finance to AI inference. But algorithms of today are struggling to keep up with challenges of scale and speed, and traditional methods aren’t working anymore. “At Hiverge, we are creating algorithmic superintelligence, giving companies the ability to discover and deploy not just new algorithms, but ones that are tailored to their specific tasks. With Hiverge, companies will be able to unlock algorithms that are beyond the limits of current approaches.” Frank Chang , Managing Partner at Flying Fish, said: “Hiverge is delivering everything we look for in a company: a highly experienced founding team with deep technical expertise in their field; a genuinely innovative solution to a major market issue; and a unique deployment of powerful technology to enable it all. A partnership between King's E-Lab Cambridge and Founders at the University of Cambridge , SPARK 1.0 programme has brought together 24 ventures from 17 departments for four weeks of intensive validation, learning and momentum. What sets it apart is its focus on grassroots ambition - giving students and alumni the space support & permission to take risks, learn fast and validate ideas and research. Backing young talent at this stage is one of the most powerful ways to drive impact. With tech contributing £159 billion to the UK economy & 3 million jobs, supporting founders as they take their first steps is essential for the future. While AI tools are proving invaluable for accelerating routine tasks like coding, drafting marketing materials, and conducting market research, the program's leaders emphasize that AI has not fundamentally altered the core principles of entrepreneurship. Startups like Mendhai Health use AI for efficiency in healthcare, while Cognify is building entirely AI-native solutions for user interaction. This balanced approach highlights AI as a powerful accelerant, not a replacement for human ingenuity. Experts caution against overreliance, stressing that direct customer interaction, identifying specific demographics, and human validation remain paramount for true market fit and understanding customer needs. The message is clear: AI is a phenomenal co-pilot, but the entrepreneur must still steer the ship, leveraging human connection to solve complex business challenges. ETH Agentic Systems Lab 💪🏻💪🏻 Bloom (YC X25)
We’re pumped to announce our next partnership in the AI startup ecosystem.

Bloom is a YC-backed startup unlocking the creator economy for software by making cross-platform app development as simple as speaking into your phone.

Founded by two students, David Oort Alonso and Sirian Maathuis, Bloom eliminates the friction of traditional app development—no code, no backend infra, no App Store Developer accounts, no App Store reviews. Instead, Blooms empowers creators, developers and entrepreneurs to turn ideas into real, deployed, shareable apps in seconds.

With investors like Moonfire, Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, and a group of world-class founders and operators from companies like Hugging Face, Weaviate, Convex, Expo, OpenAI, and Meta, Bloom is building the future of how software is created and shared.

Together, we’re aiming to strengthen the AI ecosystem in Zurich:

✨ Supporting students who want to explore AI coding agents through coursework, in collaboration with Bloom (semester projects, bachelor’s & master’s theses).

✨ Creating opportunities for students to engage directly with the Bloom team and learn what it takes to build an AI startup.

Big thanks to David Oort Alonso and Sirian Maathuis for inspiring and supporting the next generation of AI talent in Zurich and beyond. 🙌

Their story—pivoting twice before building Bloom—is a powerful reminder that true strength often lies in persistence.

👉 Students: Applications for our Genesis Batch are now open! Come with your own idea or team up with Bloom and our other startup partners.

👉 Companies: Interested in collaborating with the ETH Agentic Systems Lab? Now’s the perfect time—we’re just at the beginning of our journey.

When Morgan came to me for coaching he felt lost—lacking discipline, clarity, and motivation.

Can you relate?

This is exactly what I help my clients achieve—clarity, confidence, and momentum to move forward powerfully.

If you’re ready to get unstuck and create real, lasting change, I invite you to apply for 1:1 coaching today.

10 things i've learned about public sector sales in 10 years of public sector sales

1) you ain't convincing anybody to do anything. stop trying to sell to agencies that aren't already planning to do something in your category.

2) don't pitch extra revenue, or reduced costs. These are not for profit folks and they don't get performance bonuses. lean into less work / making their life easier.

3) tell them why this is low risk. you can't win in gov, but you can definitely lose. these folks don't want to look bad in front of their community.

4) city clerks are your best friend.

5) never respond to an RFP if you didn't help write it.

6). understand budget cycles. But not just when the cities new budget year starts. ask your champion when they need to submit their budget requests for the next fiscal year. ( If you are not in their budget requests, you're not in the budget.)

7). take care of your customers. this is a referral business. but don't name drop a big city customer thinking that it helps you with a small city customer, or vica versa. it actually hurts you, different customer base entirely.

8). don't be afraid to call the mayor on their cell. they are just regular people and often have a second job.

9). the "will help you source funding / apply for grants" thing sounds nice but never works.

10). lead with research, do your homework on their plans and initiatives. show them you know them. easy way to stand out against your competitors.

Many sellers make big mistakes here, which are often hard to recover from. Here’s how to avoid the biggest mistakes sellers make: 👇 1. Sold comps > active listings: Active listings show what sellers hope to get, but not what’s actually getting sold. Recent sold comps show what buyers were actually willing to pay. Those are the numbers you want to focus on when setting a smart price. 2. Don’t let emotions take the wheel: It’s easy to overprice when your home is full of your favourite memories and years of nostalgia. But, respectfully, buyers don’t care. They pay for value, location, and condition, which is what your price SHOULD be based on 3. First impressions are everything: The right price creates urgency. The wrong price often results in a whole lotta nothing. *cue the tumbleweed* 🏜️ That can lead to price drops… which leads to lowball offers… which costs you time and money… You get the idea. post_text: Meditate A few minutes of practice per day can help ease anxiety. “Research suggests that daily meditation may alter the brain’s neural pathways, making you more resilient to stress,” says psychologist Robbie Maller Hartman, Ph.D., a Chicago health and wellness coach. It's simple. Sit up straight with both feet on the floor. Close your eyes. Focus your attention on reciting -- out loud or silently -- a positive mantra such as “I feel at peace” or “I love myself.” Place one hand on your belly to sync the mantra with your breaths. Let any distracting thoughts float by like clouds. Breathe Deeply Take a 5-minute break and focus on your breathing. Sit up straight, eyes closed, with a hand on your belly. Slowly inhale through your nose, feeling the breath start in your abdomen and work its way to the top of your head. Reverse the process as you exhale through your mouth. “Deep breathing counters the effects of stress by slowing the heart rate and lowering blood pressure,” psychologist Judith Tutin, Ph.D., says. She's a certified life coach in Rome, GA. Be Present “Take 5 minutes and focus on only one behavior with awareness,” Tutin says. Notice how the air feels on your face when you’re walking and how your feet feel hitting the ground. Enjoy the texture and taste of each bite of food. When you spend time in the moment and focus on your senses, you should feel less tense. Reach Out Your social network is one of your best tools for handling stress. Talk to others -- preferably face to face, or at least on the phone. Share what's going on. You can get a fresh perspective while keeping your connection strong. Tune In to Your Body Mentally scan your body to get a sense of how stress affects it each day. Lie on your back, or sit with your feet on the floor. Start at your toes and work your way up to your scalp, noticing how your body feels. “Simply be aware of places you feel tight or loose without trying to change anything,” Tutin says. For 1 to 2 minutes, imagine each deep breath flowing to that body part. Repeat this process as you move your focus up your body, paying close attention to sensations you feel in each body part. Decompress Place a warm heat wrap around your neck and shoulders for 10 minutes. Close your eyes and relax your face, neck, upper chest, and back muscles. Remove the wrap, and use a tennis ball or foam roller to massage away tension. “Place the ball between your back and the wall. Lean into the ball, and hold gentle pressure for up to 15 seconds. Then move the ball to another spot, and apply pressure,” says Cathy Benninger, a nurse practitioner and assistant professor at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center in Columbus. Laugh Out Loud A good belly laugh doesn’t just lighten the load mentally. It lowers cortisol, your body’s stress hormone, and boosts brain chemicals called endorphins, which help your mood. Lighten up by tuning in to your favorite sitcom or video, reading the comics, or chatting with someone who makes you smile. Crank Up the Tunes Research shows that listening to soothing music can lower blood pressure, heart rate, and anxiety. “Create a playlist of songs or nature sounds (the ocean, a bubbling brook, birds chirping), and allow your mind to focus on the different melodies, instruments, or singers in the piece,” Benninger says. You also can blow off steam by rocking out to more upbeat tunes -- or singing at the top of your lungs! Get Moving You don’t have to run in order to get a runner’s high. All forms of exercise, including yoga and walking, can ease depression and anxiety by helping the brain release feel-good chemicals and by giving your body a chance to practice dealing with stress. You can go for a quick walk around the block, take the stairs up and down a few flights, or do some stretching exercises like head rolls and shoulder shrugs. Be Grateful Keep a gratitude journal or several (one by your bed, one in your purse, and one at work) to help you remember all the things that are good in your life. “Being grateful for your blessings cancels out negative thoughts and worries,” says Joni Emmerling, a wellness coach in Greenville, NC. Use these journals to savor good experiences like a child’s smile, a sunshine-filled day, and good health. Don’t forget to celebrate accomplishments like mastering a new task at work or a new hobby. When you start feeling stressed, spend a few minutes looking through your notes to remind yourself what really matters.

post_text: In the past years, I have done dozens of user interviews. Before then I used to do other UX research methods. but since I embraced conducting user interviews in my UX work, I have seen a tremendous change in my outcomes. User interviews are the best (and perhaps the only) way to understand your users, empathize with them and understand their needs. Not only that but also if you manage to ask the right questions, you will discover new business ideas and potential opportunities for your product that none of your competitors have. This article is a summary of tens of articles and books I have read, and of my personal experience with conducting user interviews. In this article, I will try to be as practical as possible. You will get clear and detailed tips about every stage of conducting user interviews so you can start doing user interviews from tomorrow. I will assume that you already know what user interviews are and I will jump right away into the important questions. Why to conduct user interviews? I have seen that a lot. A group of cool guys gathered to build the next big thing, so they hired a UI/UX/graphic designer to build fancy UI screens and a bunch of developers to turn those screens into a real app and they end up building something nobody wants. User interviews bridge the gap between you and your user needs. it gets you and your team arguing over real data instead of what they think users want. User interviews are the best way to gain actionable and testable insights not only by asking but also by observing user’s behaviors, words, facial expressions, and the environment around him or her. According to a study undertaken by Forrester , on average, every dollar invested in UX brings 100 dollars in return, that’s an ROI of an impressive 9,900 percent and the study clearly mentioned that observing customers Interactions with your product is the first step towards good UX design “A field visit tells you if you’re designing the right thing. A usability test tells you if you’ve designed the thing right — Think like a UX researcher book” When to conduct user interviews? The simple and short answer to this question is whenever you feel you need it, and a more specific answer, if we are going to divide the product life cycle into 3 phases then the answer would be the following: Ideation and research phase: To gather data, understand your users, build persona or validate business assumptions. Product design and development phase: To test your prototype and ensure that you have a truly relevant solution. To gather more data about your customers or know more about a particular insight from round 1 research. To test your user flows and journey maps. Release phase: To conduct usability testing or seeking for enhancing to your product. To know the ROI of investing in your research (Besides UX analytics ) How to conduct user interviews? 1.Before the Interview Defining Research objective Why would you conduct user interviews? If you don’t have a clear and precise answer to this question then none of the upcoming makes sense. The research objective is usually 3 to 4 lines outlining what you expect to get by the end of the research. Collecting qualitative data to build a persona, validating design assumptions, or maybe you want to know more about a specific feature or product to know how to build it or improve it. Here is an example: “ To explore why 30% of our users are dropping off from the checkout page. What are the problems they are facing on the page? What are the incentives needed for encouraging them to complete the purchase ” Recruiting participants select your participants based on the research objectives. You may need to recruit participants that match your persona or you may need participants to help you uncover new potential ideas. It all depends on the interview goal. I like to conduct interviews in rounds. 5 participants each round. If I notice by participant 5 that I am no longer getting insights, I don’t start round 2. This is Nielsen Norman’s principle for usability testing. You can use IDEO’s Extremes and Mainstreams method to select the sample. Survey a patch of product users (usually from 100 to 1000 depending on your users' response rate). In the survey, ask them if they would like to come to the company office for interviews and share some thoughts. And then let them select their available days. If you don’t have users yet. You can contact your competitors’ users or users who use similar products. You can find them on advertising channels like Facebook. Call the respondents and explain to them the process and what are we going to do in the interview. Don’t forget to mention the incentive and send them the office location after the call. Incentives are usually financial or maybe a discount code. It varies based on the customer segment and your product. Call more than you need. Try to avoid participant no-shows at all costs. emphasize how important he or she is to the research and how his or her input will serve the product. Call the participant on the morning of the interview day to make sure all is fine. Prepare the Interview questions What to ask about? Demographic questions are critical in every user interview. You need to know who you are asking before jumping to the real questions. Demographics include age, marital status and kids, carer occupation and aspiration …etc The use of technology in general The use of your product user’s main objectives and motivations user’s pain points Their life habits, purchasing habits, and daily routine How to ask? Try to keep leading questions to the minimum (Do you use product X rather than how many times did you use product X) Use follow up questions (what do you like and don’t like about product X ) Ask open-ended questions to encourage the user to talk (what are the products you use to transfer money) Ask about behaviors and habits more than feelings and expectations (did you face any problems with product x? What are they?) Don’t make assumptions. Ask stupid questions Don’t ask about solutions. Ask about problems. Solutions require thinking about the unknown, unlike problems that come from the present, from what people are actually experiencing Ask about the past experiences, not the expected (Tell me about the experience of the last time you transferred money rather than how would you like to transfer money) Ask them to show you if possible and if needed Start with the easier and more general questions Hint: The goal of asking questions is not getting answers, the goal is opening discussions. The Insights you will get from the words between the lines are far more important than the direct answers The “Why” questions are the most important questions.” Why” questions tells you why people want what they want rather than just what they want 2. During the Interview Before starting the interview make sure to prepare all the tools you will need for the interview. Usually, you may need a mobile phone to record the interview, White paper, and pen, maybe some sticky notes and designs if you are going to show your user any. During the interview try to observe user’s Behavior : what they do Words : what they say and how do say it Facial expressions : How do they react Context : where they are (also known as Contextual Inquiry ) Also, make sure to do the following: Start the interview by explaining to the user why you do what you do. I like to say something like “We are doing this interview to validate some assumptions and answer some questions we have, in order to give our customers including you a better service and experience. There is no right or wrong answer. The answer you are going to say is the right one. Imagine we’re sitting in a cafe and having some casual chat ” Make sure that your interviewee is comfortable and offer him or her something to drink Ask the question, then pause. Listen more than speak Try to keep the interview on time and heading in the right direction Avoid taking notes unless they are critical and look unique (you are already recording) Don’t correct, teach, or educate your interviewees. Invite other team members. If the interviewee mentioned something about operations for example. Bring the operation guy and involve him in the interview Use problem-solving techniques during the interview. Techniques like fishbone diagrams and 5 whys are very helpful to uncover user deep thoughts. For example, the 5 whys technique helps you dig deep into the user’s answer. Make it engaging and interactive. Don’t just ask and wait for the answer, use pen and paper, draw on whiteboards and ask your interviewee to express his or her ideas visually Never compare the interviewee with others (the last user said so, do you agree with him?) Thank the interviewee at the end of the interview and ask him or her if he or she has any questions Ask the interviewee to send you any suggestions or questions that might come to his or her mind after the interview. I like to take selfies with the interviewee after the interview :) 3. After the Interview After the interview, you now have an audio or video recording. I usually transcribe the recording into a google sheet consisting of 3 columns and one big row. In the row, I put the name of the user and all his demographics. The 3 columns are Insight, min/sec, and notes like the screenshot below. The importance of the min column is you might need to get back to the recording later to listen or see how the user said a specific sentence. After listing all the insights of all the users I create another tab to categorize the insights into groups (ex: observations, pain points, opportunities, needs, purchasing habits …etc) groups names vary depending on the goal of the study. Also, you can use the Thematic analysis technique to analyze the data. Feel free to reach out to me if you need any support building up your product management team, hiring one, or even a direct consultation for your product. Thanks for reading If you are looking for a digital product designer to help you build your next big thing. Reach me out on Linkedin

The goal is to create a seamless financial ecosystem that benefits businesses and consumers alike, fostering deeper economic ties between the nations. PPC strategy and optimization – Managed ad campaigns with a focus on lowering ACoS while scaling profitable keywords across multiple product lines.

Every breath you take, depending on where you take it, is poisonous in varying degrees.
 
Five years after the country launched its National Clean Air Programme, it is distressing to note that even in cities that have seen the greatest improvement in Air Quality Index (AQI), the air still falls in the ‘moderately polluted’ category. The National AQI describes this bracket as one that “may cause breathing discomfort to people with lung disease such as asthma, and discomfort to people with heart disease, children and older adults”.

The power of partnership!

We had a fantastic event at Northumbria Lodge in Cowgate, Newcastle, bringing residents and our teams together to talk about safety, improvements and building a stronger community in one of the city's tallest buildings.
 
A huge thank you to all the Northumbria Lodge residents who came along and shared their views!
 
What we talked about?

✅ We launched a new engagement leaflet to make it easier for residents to get involved and stay updated on building safety.
✅ Our Building Safety Team gave updates on fire door inspections and fire safety.
✅ We introduced support for residents who might need help getting out of the building in an emergency. For those customers who need extra support, we are creating a personal plan for them.
✅ We showed our updated Northumbria Lodge webpage and got great feedback on how to make it even better.
✅ We also talked about improving recycling and waste systems.

Events like this show what we can achieve when we work together. The residents at Northumbria Lodge showed us the power of partnership. 
 
Thank you again to everyone who attended - the feedback from the meeting is shaping our next steps and helping us build a safer, stronger community.

#partnership #firesafety #communities

post_text: 🌸 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐞𝐬𝐬—𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐲: 𝐋𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐉𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐧 —𝐢𝐭’𝐬 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐚 𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐥. Two weeks in Japan reminded me that in a world constantly demanding our attention, the real wisdom lies in the space between. Here are the seven principles that helped me reset: ✅ 𝘐𝘬𝘪𝘨𝘢𝘪 (生き甲斐 – 𝘙𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘉𝘦𝘪𝘯𝘨) Minimalism isn’t just less—it’s living aligned with what truly matters. Find the intersection of what you love, what you’re good at, and what the world needs. Minimalism starts with clarity—when you know your “why,” you stop chasing what doesn’t matter. ✅ 𝘖𝘮𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘢𝘴𝘩𝘪 (おもてなし – 𝘞𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘦𝘩𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘏𝘰𝘴𝘱𝘪𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘺) Create space not just for yourself, but to serve others with care and thoughtfulness. In life and leadership, create space for others—listen deeply, serve generously, and lead with empathy. ✅𝘔𝘢 (間 – 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘉𝘦𝘢𝘶𝘵𝘺 𝘰𝘧 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘤𝘦) Ma teaches us that emptiness isn’t absence—it’s potential. Leave white space in your calendar and your mind. Creativity and clarity often emerge in the pauses, not the hustle. ✅ 𝘚𝘦𝘬𝘬𝘪 (節氣 – 𝘍𝘭𝘰𝘸 𝘞𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘚𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘴) Life is temporary, reminding us that life moves in cycles. Instead of resisting change, embrace it. Celebrate transitions—whether in nature, business, or personal growth. ✅𝘞𝘢𝘣𝘪-𝘚𝘢𝘣𝘪 (侘寂 – 𝘐𝘮𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘧𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘭𝘺 𝘗𝘦𝘳𝘧𝘦𝘤𝘵) Perfection is sterile; imperfection is authentic. Like Kintsugi repairs cracks with gold, your flaws and failures can become your most beautiful strengths. Own your story. ✅ 𝘋𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘪 (斷捨離 – 𝘋𝘦𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘵𝘵𝘦𝘳) Decluttering isn’t just physical—it’s mental and emotional. Say no to commitments that drain you, habits that no longer serve you, and noise that clouds your focus. 🌸 𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐞𝐬𝐬—𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐲: 𝐋𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐉𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐧 —𝐢𝐭’𝐬 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐚 𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐥.

Two weeks in Japan reminded me that in a world constantly demanding our attention, the real wisdom lies in the space between.

Here are the seven principles that helped me reset:

✅ 𝘐𝘬𝘪𝘨𝘢𝘪 (生き甲斐 – 𝘙𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘉𝘦𝘪𝘯𝘨)
Minimalism isn’t just less—it’s living aligned with what truly matters. Find the intersection of what you love, what you’re good at, and what the world needs. Minimalism starts with clarity—when you know your “why,” you stop chasing what doesn’t matter.

✅ 𝘖𝘮𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘢𝘴𝘩𝘪 (おもてなし – 𝘞𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘦𝘩𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘏𝘰𝘴𝘱𝘪𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘺)
Create space not just for yourself, but to serve others with care and thoughtfulness. In life and leadership, create space for others—listen deeply, serve generously, and lead with empathy.

✅𝘔𝘢 (間 – 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘉𝘦𝘢𝘶𝘵𝘺 𝘰𝘧 𝘚𝘱𝘢𝘤𝘦)
Ma teaches us that emptiness isn’t absence—it’s potential. Leave white space in your calendar and your mind. Creativity and clarity often emerge in the pauses, not the hustle.

✅ 𝘚𝘦𝘬𝘬𝘪 (節氣 – 𝘍𝘭𝘰𝘸 𝘞𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘚𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘴)
Life is temporary, reminding us that life moves in cycles. Instead of resisting change, embrace it. Celebrate transitions—whether in nature, business, or personal growth.

✅𝘞𝘢𝘣𝘪-𝘚𝘢𝘣𝘪 (侘寂 – 𝘐𝘮𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘧𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘭𝘺 𝘗𝘦𝘳𝘧𝘦𝘤𝘵)
Perfection is sterile; imperfection is authentic. Like Kintsugi repairs cracks with gold, your flaws and failures can become your most beautiful strengths. Own your story.

✅ 𝘋𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘪 (斷捨離 – 𝘋𝘦𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘵𝘵𝘦𝘳)
Decluttering isn’t just physical—it’s mental and emotional. Say no to commitments that drain you, habits that no longer serve you, and noise that clouds your focus. Freedom begins with letting go.

✅ 𝘔𝘰𝘵𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘪 (勿体無い – 𝘙𝘦𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘤𝘵 𝘞𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘠𝘰𝘶 𝘏𝘢𝘷𝘦)
This principle teaches gratitude and sustainability. Treat what you own with care—whether it’s time, relationships, or resources. When you value what you have, you live with intention.

🌿 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐦, 𝐈 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝, 𝐢𝐬 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠—𝐢𝐭’𝐬 𝐚 𝐰𝐚𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐞, 𝐩𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐭.

Wishing everyone a meaningful wrap-up to 2025 and an inspiring start to 2026. 🌟

post_text: What an amazing celebration we had today at our Columbus, Mississippi facility for our 20th anniversary! With speeches from our esteemed guests, a ribbon-cutting ceremony for our brand new display helicopter, and an outstanding static display, featuring the U.S. Coast Guard MH-65 helicopter, Army National Guard Lakota helicopter, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety H125 and PHI Aviation 's H160 and H135, this event was one for the books! As we reflect on this milestone, I want to extend my gratitude to all those who contributed to the success of this event - our former Airbus leaders, partners, supporters, and the dedicated community members who have stood by us throughout this journey. But my most heartfelt thanks go to our incredible employees. Your dedication, passion, and tireless efforts have been the driving force behind our achievements. It's your hard work and commitment that make me proud to be part of this success story. Our 20th anniversary celebration was a day that will be cherished for years to come. It was a testament to our past achievements, a celebration of our present capabilities, and a promise of an even brighter future. We look forward to many more years of innovation, growth, and shared success. #AirbusHeliColumbus20years Scott Tumpak Marc Paganini Sam Adcock Johannes Dienemann Cindy Hyde-Smith Roger Wicker Trent Kelly

With speeches from our esteemed guests, a ribbon-cutting ceremony for our brand new display helicopter, and an outstanding static display, featuring the U.S. Coast Guard MH-65 helicopter, Army National Guard Lakota helicopter, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety H125 and PHI Aviation's H160 and H135, this event was one for the books!

As we reflect on this milestone, I want to extend my gratitude to all those who contributed to the success of this event - our former Airbus leaders, partners, supporters, and the dedicated community members who have stood by us throughout this journey.

But my most heartfelt thanks go to our incredible employees. Your dedication, passion, and tireless efforts have been the driving force behind our achievements. It's your hard work and commitment that make me proud to be part of this success story.

Our 20th anniversary celebration was a day that will be cherished for years to come. It was a testament to our past achievements, a celebration of our present capabilities, and a promise of an even brighter future. We look forward to many more years of innovation, growth, and shared success.

post_text: Good morning/afternoon/evening/night—except for folks who start #marketing from the bottom of this map. That's right... Marketing doesn't start with paid ads; it starts with: → ⅓ Diagnosis: What the f*ck is going on? → ⅓ Strategy: Where the f*ck are we going? → ⅓ Execution: How the f*ck are we going there? But then!, inside Execution, you have the 4 Ps: → ¼ Product: What the f*ck are you selling? → ¼ Price: How much are you f*cking charging for it? → ¼ Place: Where the f*ck are you going to sell it? → ¼ Promotion: How the f*ck are you going to tell people about it? If we start at the bottom—with Promotion—we fly blind by only covering 8% of what marketing should be about (¼ x ⅓ = 1/12 = 8%). Here's a quick-n-dirty plan to explore Marketing Land *without* working 16 hours a day for 6 months, or hiring an outside consultant, or identifying as a marketer. --- 1/ Diagnosis Forget about your business and think like a customer. Understand how you fit into their lives. Look at the data you already have (think sales call recordings, customer service feedback, old surveys...), talk to your customer-facing staff, read online reviews... Be *very* curious. --- 2/ Strategy Pick a group of people 1) you can reach, 2) you like working with, 3) who can pay, and 4) in a growing segment. Position what you do so that you're their *least risky* option in the category where there are differences you can take advantage of. --- 3/ Execution Lead with a no-brainer offer that's difficult for your segment to refuse. Resist discounting. Figure out what this segment is willing to pay—using the Van Westendorp model, for example—or just wing it and see what happens. Choose where/when you want to appear in front of your segment based on what you've learned during 1/ Diagnosis. And then, and only then, focus on Promotion, which I'm sure you're familiar with. --- 4/ Discomfort Learn from your mistakes. It's never your customers' fault; it's always yours. Embrace chaos. Adjust. Move on. Stand the f*ck out. --- Now go explore that map, my little ruby-throated hummingbird. 🐤 Fly and be free. Good morning/afternoon/evening/night—except for folks who start #marketing from the bottom of this map.

That's right...

Marketing doesn't start with paid ads; it starts with:

→ ⅓ Diagnosis: What the f*ck is going on?
→ ⅓ Strategy: Where the f*ck are we going?
→ ⅓ Execution: How the f*ck are we going there?

But then!, inside Execution, you have the 4 Ps:

→ ¼ Product: What the f*ck are you selling?
→ ¼ Price: How much are you f*cking charging for it?
→ ¼ Place: Where the f*ck are you going to sell it?
→ ¼ Promotion: How the f*ck are you going to tell people about it?

If we start at the bottom—with Promotion—we fly blind by only covering 8% of what marketing should be about (¼ x ⅓ = 1/12 = 8%).

Here's a quick-n-dirty plan to explore Marketing Land *without* working 16 hours a day for 6 months, or hiring an outside consultant, or identifying as a marketer.

---

1/ Diagnosis

Forget about your business and think like a customer. Understand how you fit into their lives. Look at the data you already have (think sales call recordings, customer service feedback, old surveys...), talk to your customer-facing staff, read online reviews... Be *very* curious.

---

2/ Strategy

Pick a group of people 1) you can reach, 2) you like working with, 3) who can pay, and 4) in a growing segment. Position what you do so that you're their *least risky* option in the category where there are differences you can take advantage of.

---

3/ Execution

Lead with a no-brainer offer that's difficult for your segment to refuse. Resist discounting. Figure out what this segment is willing to pay—using the Van Westendorp model, for example—or just wing it and see what happens. Choose where/when you want to appear in front of your segment based on what you've learned during 1/ Diagnosis.

And then, and only then, focus on Promotion, which I'm sure you're familiar with.

---

4/ Discomfort

Learn from your mistakes. It's never your customers' fault; it's always yours. Embrace chaos. Adjust. Move on. Stand the f*ck out.

---

Now go explore that map, my little ruby-throated hummingbird. 🐤

Fly and be free.

post_text: So, you’ve finally decided to tackle the JLPT, and here you are, wondering: Exactly how many hours do I need to throw at this beast to finally level up in Japanese? Let’s just say it’s...complicated. Will N1 demand months of monk-like study? Is N5 just glorified Duolingo practice? Buckle up, because we’re about to dive into the messy truth. “Official” Study Hours: JEES Must Be Joking, Right? Back in the day, JEES (Japan Educational Exchanges and Services) gave us some so-called “official” study hours. And they look reasonable… if you’re a language-learning prodigy or a time-traveling wizard. According to them: N1 : 900 hours (sure, if you’re a language god 👀) N2 : 600 hours N4 : 300 hours N5 : 150 hours Uh-huh. So just a few hundred hours, and bam—fluent Japanese? They’ve got jokes. I’d love to meet the person who passed N1 after 900 hours and shake their hand because that’s superhuman. Spoiler alert: in reality, 900 hours might get you to…N3? Maybe? The Real-World JLPT Hours: More Like A Lifetime Commitment Let’s break it down with a bit more realism (and a whole lot more hours): N1 : 2,700–4,500 hours (yes, you read that right; this is like an epic saga with no end in sight) N2 : 1,800–3,000 hours (hello kanji-induced headaches) N4 : 900–1,500 hours (you’re now qualified to read some manga titles) N5 : 450–750 hours (great, you can order ramen and sort of ask for directions) To put that in perspective, if you dedicated 3 hours a day every single day , N1 could take you... forever. But hey, by that point, you might even start dreaming in kanji, so silver linings? Self-Study Warriors, Assemble: What Does This Mean for You? Here’s the thing: if you’re like most of us, studying Japanese solo with the occasional YouTube binge and random grammar notes in your phone, these hours might as well be rough estimates. Some folks pass N2 with half these hours, while others clock in double and still feel lost in Tokyo Station. It’s really a matter of figuring out what works for you and leaning into it hard. Reality Check: “How Many Study Hours Do You Actually Need?” Truth is, JLPT hours are like cooking times in recipes—just a suggestion, and honestly, you’ll probably need a lot more salt and double the effort. So go ahead, prepare yourself for endless kanji flashcards, late-night grammar meltdowns, and a slow descent into JLPT madness. So Tell Me, How Long Have You Been at This? Sound off in the comments! Are you grinding toward N5 or chasing the elusive N1? How many hours have you poured into this wild ride?
