post_text: Ask yourself this question, if you were given a cash bonus on April 27th, what would you do with the money? For most people it would not be to go buy additional shares in their employer’s company. So if your answer was anything other than buy shares, there’s a good chance the right answer for you is to sell in you open window after the vesting date of the shares. Why sell RSUs? The employee’s main source of future income (salary) is already tied to the company and thus the employee is taking equity risk in this avenue. Said another way, if the company fails, your income goes away with the company. If the stock loses value after the vest, you could create a capital loss that could not be fully deductible when you sell the shares unless you have adequate capital gains. The company likely also provides the family medical benefits and while there are safeguards in place (COBRA) losing a job can be a significant disruption in medical care. The employee, unless it is their first year of RSUs, likely has a large pool of unvested RSUs that give them a level of exposure to the stock of the company that could be outsized relative to their tolerance for risk. For reference, the Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act would dictate that a fiduciary does not have more than 10% of the institution’s capital in one position. Which lots to sell: As mentioned above, there are significant advantages to selling the shares as they vest. However, if you do hold shares after they vest, we recommend that you are mindful of the shares that you sell. It is possible that you could have vests with different fair market values at vest and different holding periods. It is to your advantage to specifically identify what lots you are selling the shares from. Our general recommendation of priority is as follows: First, sell lots held less than 365 days that are held at a loss. (Short term Capital Loss) Second, sell lots held longer than 365 days that are held at a loss. (Long term capital loss) Third, sell lots held longer than 365 days that are held at a gain. (Long term capital gain) Fourth, sell lots held less than 365 days that are held at a gain. (Short term Capital Gain) Remember, individual facts and circumstances will vary. You should consult your tax advisor on your personal situation. Interesting facts to remember about RSU’s: At vesting the income is considered taxable wages as a supplemental income payment Companies generally are required to withhold minimum federal income tax withholding of 22% on the first $1,000,000 of supplemental income (state income tax withholding requirements vary by state, but if applicable would be additional withholding). After you exceed the $1,000,000 of supplemental income, the company is required to withhold federal income taxes at 37% (similar to above, state taxes may be applicable) These withholding rules generally result in you owing additional federal taxes in April when you file your taxes if you have significant income withheld at 22%. A good rule of thumb is to assume you will owe an additional 15% of that income. If during the period between the grant and vest of your RSU’s you worked/lived in a state with an individual income tax, your employer should withhold state income taxes based upon the percentage of days you lived/worked in that state. For example, if you lived in CA for 80% of the vesting period and then moved to Washington, it is likely your employer would withhold California income taxes on 80% of the income realized on the vesting of the RSU’s (that would result in you needing to file a California nonresident income tax return for that year). Look, this is gonna sound basic as hell to some of you, but I need to say it out loud anyway:

The hardest part of anything worth doing is literally just starting.
That’s it. The mountain isn’t climbing itself—it’s the first stupid step you keep postponing.

We’re all masters at “I’ll do it when…” ESPECIALLY ME!!!
When I feel ready. When life calms down. When the stars align. When Monday hits different.

Spoiler: those perfect conditions don’t exist.
So yeah—Nike was onto something stupidly simple and stupidly true:
Just do it.
Not tomorrow. Not next week.
Today. Right now. This exact messy, imperfect moment.

I’m not telling you to sprint until you puke or ignore real life obstacles.
Some people genuinely can’t move yet—and that’s valid.
But be brutally honest with yourself: is your “I can’t right now” actually true…
or is it just fear wearing a very convincing excuse?

There’s something alive and electric in the present that later never quite captures.
The first awkward line, the ugly first draft, the shaky first rep, the terrifying send button—

But it's not your fault… some people have all this fancy equipment, which makes you think you need that as well… ...but you don’t. A simple smartphone is all you need! HITTERS · H - Hook or Pattern Interrupt · I - Ideology or Break Beliefs Pattern · T - Throw rocks at who’s to blame · T - Tell a story or personal experience · E - Entice them with a promise (pre-frame the funnel page or next step) · R - Reveal the Offer · S - Strike while the iron’s hot (Call to Action) This formula is used repeatedly. post_text: Ivrea, the Industrial Utopia of Adriano Olivetti The inscription, in July of 2018, of the site of "Ivrea, a 20th century industrial city" (Photo 1) in the World Heritage list, celebrates the great industrial, social, urban and architectural programs promoted by Adriano Olivetti (1901-1960). Ivrea is perhaps the most significant of all the industrial "utopias" of the 20th century, and as such is should be compared with the different advanced and socially-conscious models of industrial development experimented in America and Europe over the last two centuries. It is in America that originates the great saga of the Olivettis: Camillo Olivetti (1868-1943) (Photo 2), Adriano's father, went there in 1893 - together with his Master, the famous engineer and scientist Galileo Ferraris - to visit the World Colombian Exhibition of Chicago, which presented to the world the technological innovations that were bolstering the rapid American industrial progress. Upon his return, he founded an industrial company for the production of electrical measuring instruments. After a second trip to America in 1910, Camillo Olivetti began producing in Ivrea the typewriters that will give the company international recognition and turn it into one of the pillars of industrial innovation in Italy. Adriano Olivetti (Photo 3) grows up in the climate of innovation and social reformism promoted by his father, who advocated progressive ideas and had already launched a social and economic assistance policy for company workers. He also visited America for a long time in 1925-26, to study the new production processes, in particular those promoted by Henry Ford in Detroit. When Adriano took over the management of the company in 1933, he started a season of industrial innovation and of experimentations in architecture, based on the ideas promoted in those years by the Modern Movement. In 1934, Adriano entrusted the task of drafting a new Urban Plan for the industrial city of Ivrea to two young Milanese architects, Luigi Figini (1903-1984) and Gino Pollini (1903-1991). Figini and Pollini adhered to the rationalist principles of the "functional city" promoted by the Modern Movement and by CIAM (Congrès International d’Architecture Moderne), and from the very beginning they adopted a modern architectural language in their projects. The need to extend the original Laboratory, the Mattoni Rossi building, built by Camillo Olivetti at the beginning of the 20th century (Photo 4), motivated the building of new of structures which became known as the expression of the most advanced Italian architectural culture. The first extension (1934-36) consisted of an L-shaped reinforced concrete structure, the Industrial Building Office, with 4-meter high floors with a free plan to allow mass production to be introduced (Photo 5 ). Between 1936 and 1941 the second and third extensions were built, in continuity with the first but with numerous innovative elements, which enhanced the modernity of the whole (Photo 6-7). A fourth extension of the complex will follow in 1955-58. The work of Figini and Pollini was not limited to industrial architecture, but also embraced the company's social policy, and in particular the workers' residences. Between 1939 and 1941 they built the seven buildings for large families (Photo 8), the workers' houses of Borgo Olivetti, and the beautiful nursery school, remarkable for the construction of the relationship between the interiors and the landscape (Photo 9). The Master Plan of Ivrea, realized in 1938 by a group formed by Luigi Figini, the urban planner Luigi Piccinato (1899-1983) and the engineer Egisippo Devoti, sealed this season with innovative choices that looked at the needs of industrial development but at the same time ensured the preservation of the historical fabric. The post-war period saw a huge international expansion of Olivetti, with initiatives in different countries of the world, from Scotland, Argentina, Brazil, to the United States. The growth of production and the development of new areas of operation, including information technology, was paralleled by the development of the social vision of Adriano Olivetti. In 1947 he founded the Community Movement (Photo 10), with a cultural and political program oriented towards the person and the citizen. This later became a political movement, with good local results (Adriano Olivetti was Mayor of Ivrea from 1956 to 1958) but a very modest national response. Olivetti's commitment to urban planning, which brought him to take the Presidency of the Italian Urban Planning Institute (INU) from 1950 to 1960, is also reflected in the numerous editorial initiatives, technical magazines (Photo 11), and cultural promotion. Following a sustained industrial growth, in the post-war period the company promoted the construction of a large number of new architectures, for the working needs of the company but also aimed to improve the living conditions of the employees, based on an overall program that will be completed only after the premature death of Adriano Olivetti, in 1960. Between 1948 and 1955, Marcello Nizzoli (1887-1969) and Gian Mario Oliveri (1921-2007) designed a series of residential buildings inspired by the principles of Modernism: the single-family houses for executives (Photo 12), the houses with 4 apartments (Photo 13), the building with 18 apartments (Photo 14), in addition to the elegant Villa Capellaro (Photo 15). In those years several projects were promoted by the Employees Housing Office (UCCD) of Olivetti. In line with the principles expressed by the Community Movement, the company offered loans to employees to facilitate their access to home ownership, in order to promote an harmonious and integrated social fabric. Among the main achievements are the condominium Fiò Bellot of 1951 (Photo 16), and some single-family buildings (Casa Stratta, Casa Morucci, Casa Perotti), designed by Emilio Aventino Tarpino. In 1953 Ignazio Gardella (1905-1999) was commissioned to build the company canteen and recreational club (Photo 17), planned for over 1600 employees. Gardella created a building of great typological complexity, which looks at Wright's lesson in the general layout, in the treatment of surfaces and in the architectural details. A result that, when it was presented to the last CIAM Congress in Otterlo in 1959, aroused a heated controversy. By Edoardo Vittoria (1923-2009) are the Olivetti Study and Research Center (Photo 18) of 1951-54, defined by an open plan and a blue clinker cladding, and the building for the Thermal Plant of 1956-59 ( Photo 19). The Palazzo for the Olivetti Offices (Photo 20), designed by Annibale Fiocchi (1915-2011), Gian Antonio Bernasconi and Marcello Nizzoli, form one of the most representative buildings of the city. In 1968 a highly innovative architecture was designed by Roberto Gabetti (1925-2000) and Aimaro Oreglia d'Isola (b. 1928): a building for temporary residences, the west residential unit, called by the inhabitants “Talponia”, a semicircular shape and length over 300 meters (Photo 21). The construction of important architectures did not end with the progressive decline of the enterprise: in 1985-88, Gino Valle (1923-2003) built a new Office Building, a structure six floors high, which completes the modern image of Ivrea and symbolizes its transformation from an industrial city to a tertiary city (Photo 22). Today the Industrial City imagined by Adriano Olivetti no longer exists and many of the buildings originally used for production have been altered by companies that have inherited the Company's properties, not always in ways that respect their architectural value. However, the inscription of Ivrea in the World Heritage List will allow to maintain the memory of an important chapter of modern social thinking, as in other iconic sites that have marked the history of modern industry: New Lanarck, Saltaire, La Chaux De Fond, Crespi d'Adda, the Van Nelle Factory. The inscription in the World Heritage List of this great social, industrial and urban planning project came after many years of careful preparation, supported by local and regional institutions, but promoted primarily by Laura Olivetti (1950-2015), Adriano's daughter (Photo 23), who unfortunately could not see the outcome of his work but who certainly was the main architect of this international recognition. 1 Ivrea , area listed in the World Heritage List of UNESCO 2. Ivrea, the Industrial Utopia of Adriano Olivetti




The inscription, in July of 2018, of the site of "Ivrea, a 20th century industrial city" (Photo 1) in the World Heritage list, celebrates the great industrial, social, urban and architectural programs promoted by Adriano Olivetti (1901-1960).


Ivrea is perhaps the most significant of all the industrial "utopias" of the 20th century, and as such is should be compared with the different advanced and socially-conscious models of industrial development experimented in America and Europe over the last two centuries.


It is in America that originates the great saga of the Olivettis: Camillo Olivetti (1868-1943) (Photo 2), Adriano's father, went there in 1893 - together with his Master, the famous engineer and scientist Galileo Ferraris - to visit the World Colombian Exhibition of Chicago, which presented to the world the technological innovations that were bolstering the rapid American industrial progress.


Upon his return, he founded an industrial company for the production of electrical measuring instruments. After a second trip to America in 1910, Camillo Olivetti began producing in Ivrea the typewriters that will give the company international recognition and turn it into one of the pillars of industrial innovation in Italy.


Adriano Olivetti (Photo 3) grows up in the climate of innovation and social reformism promoted by his father, who advocated progressive ideas and had already launched a social and economic assistance policy for company workers.


He also visited America for a long time in 1925-26, to study the new production processes, in particular those promoted by Henry Ford in Detroit.


When Adriano took over the management of the company in 1933, he started a season of industrial innovation and of experimentations in architecture, based on the ideas promoted in those years by the Modern Movement.


In 1934, Adriano entrusted the task of drafting a new Urban Plan for the industrial city of Ivrea to two young Milanese architects, Luigi Figini (1903-1984) and Gino Pollini (1903-1991).


Figini and Pollini adhered to the rationalist principles of the "functional city" promoted by the Modern Movement and by CIAM (Congrès International d’Architecture Moderne), and from the very beginning they adopted a modern architectural language in their projects.


The need to extend the original Laboratory, the Mattoni Rossi building, built by Camillo Olivetti at the beginning of the 20th century (Photo 4), motivated the building of new of structures which became known as the expression of the most advanced Italian architectural culture.


The first extension (1934-36) consisted of an L-shaped reinforced concrete structure, the Industrial Building Office, with 4-meter high floors with a free plan to allow mass production to be introduced (Photo 5 ).


Between 1936 and 1941 the second and third extensions were built, in continuity with the first but with numerous innovative elements, which enhanced the modernity of the whole (Photo 6-7). A fourth extension of the complex will follow in 1955-58.


The work of Figini and Pollini was not limited to industrial architecture, but also embraced the company's social policy, and in particular the workers' residences. Between 1939 and 1941 they built the seven buildings for large families (Photo 8), the workers' houses of Borgo Olivetti, and the beautiful nursery school, remarkable for the construction of the relationship between the interiors and the landscape (Photo 9).


The Master Plan of Ivrea, realized in 1938 by a group formed by Luigi Figini, the urban planner Luigi Piccinato (1899-1983) and the engineer Egisippo Devoti, sealed this season with innovative choices that looked at the needs of industrial development but at the same time ensured the preservation of the historical fabric.


The post-war period saw a huge international expansion of Olivetti, with initiatives in different countries of the world, from Scotland, Argentina, Brazil, to the United States.


The growth of production and the development of new areas of operation, including information technology, was paralleled by the development of the social vision of Adriano Olivetti.


In 1947 he founded the Community Movement (Photo 10), with a cultural and political program oriented towards the person and the citizen. This later became a political movement, with good local results (Adriano Olivetti was Mayor of Ivrea from 1956 to 1958) but a very modest national response.


Olivetti's commitment to urban planning, which brought him to take the Presidency of the Italian Urban Planning Institute (INU) from 1950 to 1960, is also reflected in the numerous editorial initiatives, technical magazines (Photo 11), and cultural promotion.


Following a sustained industrial growth, in the post-war period the company promoted the construction of a large number of new architectures, for the working needs of the company but also aimed to improve the living conditions of the employees, based on an overall program that will be completed only after the premature death of Adriano Olivetti, in 1960.


Between 1948 and 1955, Marcello Nizzoli (1887-1969) and Gian Mario Oliveri (1921-2007) designed a series of residential buildings inspired by the principles of Modernism: the single-family houses for executives (Photo 12), the houses with 4 apartments (Photo 13), the building with 18 apartments (Photo 14), in addition to the elegant Villa Capellaro (Photo 15).


In those years several projects were promoted by the Employees Housing Office (UCCD) of Olivetti. In line with the principles expressed by the Community Movement, the company offered loans to employees to facilitate their access to home ownership, in order to promote an harmonious and integrated social fabric.


Among the main achievements are the condominium Fiò Bellot of 1951 (Photo 16), and some single-family buildings (Casa Stratta, Casa Morucci, Casa Perotti), designed by Emilio Aventino Tarpino.


In 1953 Ignazio Gardella (1905-1999) was commissioned to build the company canteen and recreational club (Photo 17), planned for over 1600 employees. Gardella created a building of great typological complexity, which looks at Wright's lesson in the general layout, in the treatment of surfaces and in the architectural details. A result that, when it was presented to the last CIAM Congress in Otterlo in 1959, aroused a heated controversy.


By Edoardo Vittoria (1923-2009) are the Olivetti Study and Research Center (Photo 18) of 1951-54, defined by an open plan and a blue clinker cladding, and the building for the Thermal Plant of 1956-59 ( Photo 19). The Palazzo for the Olivetti Offices (Photo 20), designed by Annibale Fiocchi (1915-2011), Gian Antonio Bernasconi and Marcello Nizzoli, form one of the most representative buildings of the city.


In 1968 a highly innovative architecture was designed by Roberto Gabetti (1925-2000) and Aimaro Oreglia d'Isola (b. 1928): a building for temporary residences, the west residential unit, called by the inhabitants “Talponia”, a semicircular shape and length over 300 meters (Photo 21).


The construction of important architectures did not end with the progressive decline of the enterprise: in 1985-88, Gino Valle (1923-2003) built a new Office Building, a structure six floors high, which completes the modern image of Ivrea and symbolizes its transformation from an industrial city to a tertiary city (Photo 22).


Today the Industrial City imagined by Adriano Olivetti no longer exists and many of the buildings originally used for production have been altered by companies that have inherited the Company's properties, not always in ways that respect their architectural value.


However, the inscription of Ivrea in the World Heritage List will allow to maintain the memory of an important chapter of modern social thinking, as in other iconic sites that have marked the history of modern industry: New Lanarck, Saltaire, La Chaux De Fond, Crespi d'Adda, the Van Nelle Factory.


The inscription in the World Heritage List of this great social, industrial and urban planning project came after many years of careful preparation, supported by local and regional institutions, but promoted primarily by Laura Olivetti (1950-2015), Adriano's daughter (Photo 23), who unfortunately could not see the outcome of his work but who certainly was the main architect of this international recognition.

Diwali felt different. Not just because of the lights or the festivals but because of the real estate conversations I kept hearing everywhere. Friends, clients, even people on flights… everyone was talking about property deals. So I dug deeper. Turns out, Diwali 2025 pushed India’s real estate market to record highs ₹6.05 lakh crore in sales, a 25% jump from last year. That’s not a festive spike. That’s a market shift. Developers across metros were moving serious inventory. Flexible payment plans, genuine 8 to 12% discounts, and tie-ups with banks offering low-interest loans it all came together perfectly. For the first time, buyers weren’t just window-shopping during the festive season… they were signing deals. And the big game-changer? GST 2.0. When the tax on under-construction homes dropped from 5% to 3.5%, it actually lowered costs. Buyers saved ₹3 to 6 lakh per property, and EMIs came down by ₹5,000 to ₹8,000 a month. That’s the kind of reform that translates directly to confidence. Even the luxury segment was on fire. Sales of ₹2 crore+ homes jumped 40%, and I noticed more HNIs moving from stocks and gold into real estate not for show, but for yield and stability. In places like Gurgaon, Mumbai, and Noida, luxury launches were selling out in weeks. Then came the cultural layer. Registrations spiked across Maharashtra, NCR, and Karnataka. Searches for “buy property” shot up 4x on Google. Families planned Griha Pravesh ceremonies as part of their Diwali rituals proof that tradition and investment timing aligned perfectly this year. Of course, not everything stays on sale forever. Steel, cement, and labor costs are already up 8 to 15%, which means prices for new projects in 2026 could rise 5 to 8%. But the sentiment has shifted. The market feels more confident, more mature. To me, Diwali 2025 wasn’t just a good quarter it was a reset moment for Indian real estate. Buyers got real value. Developers cleared stock. And the industry found fresh momentum heading into 2026. Sometimes, one festive season can change the story for an entire market. 🚨 India’s ₹6.05 Lakh Crore Diwali Boom: What It Signals for Real Estate in 2025–26 🚨

As a Real Estate Strategist, we don’t just track numbers—we decode patterns. And this Diwali, India didn’t just celebrate—it invested. ₹6.05 lakh crore in festive turnover (₹5.4L Cr in goods + ₹65K Cr in services) isn’t just a record—it’s a referendum on rising consumer confidence, Swadeshi sentiment, and economic resilience.

📊 #ArhamEstate Deep Analysis :

What does this mean for Real Estate?
Let’s break it down 🔍:

✅ Consumer Confidence = Property Confidence :
When 87% of buyers choose Indian goods and luxury sale spikes, it signals a readiness for big-ticket investments—like homes. Expect a surge in premium and branded residences, especially from NRIs and HNIs riding the festive momentum.

✅ GST 2.0 = Construction Cost Relief :
With rationalized GST on cement, bricks, and raw materials, developers can now pass on 3–5% cost savings to buyers. Affordable and mid-segment housing just got more attractive.

✅ Tier 2 & 3 Cities = New Growth Corridors :
The Swadeshi wave isn’t just emotional—it’s geographical. Semi-urban India is spending, aspiring, and upgrading. Infrastructure-led real estate in these zones will see a sharp uptick.

✅ Wedding Season Tailwind :
Post-Diwali weddings traditionally drive demand for furnishings, gold, and… new homes. This seasonal liquidity will spill into Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 sales.

✅ Industrial & Warehousing = Silent Winners
With domestic manufacturing rising, demand for logistics hubs, warehousing, and industrial parks will follow. Real estate isn’t just residential—it’s the backbone of Bharat’s production engine.

🎯 Our Strategic Advise :
For Investors : Focus on affordable housing, warehousing, and Tier 2/3 cities.
For Developers : Prioritize transparency, amenities, and Swadeshi-aligned branding.
For Policymakers : Fast-track infra and reduce transaction costs.

💡From Diwali discounts to down payments—India just gave us a ₹6.05 lakh crore signal. If you’re still waiting for the ‘right time’ to invest in real estate, this might be it. Share if you feel the shift too.

🔖 Save this post if you’re serious about understanding where India’s real estate is headed in 2025–26. This isn’t just a festive spike—it’s a structural shift.

En dan zit je ineens niet meer op je werk ...

Sinds de start van dit nieuwe jaar is mijn rol binnen ProBär drastisch veranderd. Ik heb mijn dagelijkse werkzaamheden neergelegd en terwijl mijn omgeving dagelijks aan of naar het werk gaat, zit ik thuis. Het voelt onwennig, en eerlijk gezegd vind ik het best lastig. Niets voor mij dat stilzitten, maar toch is het een bewuste keuze.

Een stap naar het onbekende
Tijdens de kerstdagen van 2023 sprak ik voor het eerst hardop uit dat 2024 mijn laatste jaar zou worden bij ProBär. Niet omdat ik mijn werk niet meer leuk vond, maar omdat ik voelde dat het tijd was voor iets nieuws. Toch was het besluit nemen makkelijker dan het daadwerkelijk uitvoeren, er was altijd wel een excuus om door te gaan. Nu ben ik zeker niet risicomijdend, maar je hebt toch ook een bepaald verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel richting je familie, je team en de klanten. En laten we eerlijk zijn: het verlaten van je comfortzone blijft een grote uitdaging.

Plannen en omwegen
Mijn oorspronkelijke plan was om ProBär te verkopen. Het is een prachtig nichebedrijf in materialen voor teddyberen, en ik vond dat het een nieuwe enthousiaste eigenaar verdient. Maar hoewel er geïnteresseerden waren, vond ik geen koper die juiste passie en visie deelde.

Plan B was drastischer: alles verkopen en de deuren sluiten. Dat zou veel impact hebben op het team, niet alleen ik, maar iedereen zou door mijn besluit gedwongen worden een nieuwe toekomst te zoeken. Het zorgde daarnaast ook voor onrust bij onze klanten, die grotendeels afhankelijk zijn van onze materialen. De gedachte iedereen in de steek te laten voelde niet goed.

De onverwachte oplossing
De oplossing kwam van dichterbij dan ik had durven dromen: mijn fantastische medewerkers. Met hun jarenlange ervaring en liefde voor ProBär stelden zij voor om het bedrijf samen voort te zetten. Ik had nooit gedacht dat zij deze verantwoordelijkheid wilden én konden dragen, maar inmiddels weet ik zeker dat ProBär in de goede handen is.

ProBär blijft mijn bedrijf, maar mijn rol is veranderd. Ik blijf op de achtergrond betrokken, als klankbord en sparringpartner. Dat is wennen, maar tegelijkertijd overheerst het gevoel van trots.

Vooruitkijken
Voor mij is dit een moment van loslaten en vooruitkijken. De toekomst ligt open, en dat voelt zowel inspirerend als spannend. Stilzitten voelt onnatuurlijk, maar misschien geeft juist dat de ruimte die ik nodig heb om mijn volgende stap te ontdekken.

Als ondernemer geloof ik in bewust keuzes maken, ook als die keuzes onzekerheid met zich meebrengen. Soms moet je springen, risico’s nemen en vertrouwen hebben dat je vleugels onderweg vanzelf groeien.

Herken je dit gevoel? Sta jij ook op een kruispunt in je carrière of leven? Ik ben benieuwd naar jouw verhaal en hoe jij keuzes maakt in tijden van verandering. Laten we elkaar inspireren.

En dan zit je ineens niet meer op je werk ...

Sinds de start van dit nieuwe jaar is mijn rol binnen ProBär drastisch veranderd. Ik heb mijn dagelijkse werkzaamheden neergelegd en terwijl mijn omgeving dagelijks aan of naar het werk gaat, zit ik thuis. Het voelt onwennig, en eerlijk gezegd vind ik het best lastig. Niets voor mij dat stilzitten, maar toch is het een bewuste keuze.

Een stap naar het onbekende
Tijdens de kerstdagen van 2023 sprak ik voor het eerst hardop uit dat 2024 mijn laatste jaar zou worden bij ProBär. Niet omdat ik mijn werk niet meer leuk vond, maar omdat ik voelde dat het tijd was voor iets nieuws. Toch was het besluit nemen makkelijker dan het daadwerkelijk uitvoeren, er was altijd wel een excuus om door te gaan. Nu ben ik zeker niet risicomijdend, maar je hebt toch ook een bepaald verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel richting je familie, je team en de klanten. En laten we eerlijk zijn: het verlaten van je comfortzone blijft een grote uitdaging.

Plannen en omwegen
Mijn oorspronkelijke plan was om ProBär te verkopen. Het is een prachtig nichebedrijf in materialen voor teddyberen, en ik vond dat het een nieuwe enthousiaste eigenaar verdient. Maar hoewel er geïnteresseerden waren, vond ik geen koper die juiste passie en visie deelde.

Plan B was drastischer: alles verkopen en de deuren sluiten. Dat zou veel impact hebben op het team, niet alleen ik, maar iedereen zou door mijn besluit gedwongen worden een nieuwe toekomst te zoeken. Het zorgde daarnaast ook voor onrust bij onze klanten, die grotendeels afhankelijk zijn van onze materialen. De gedachte iedereen in de steek te laten voelde niet goed.

De onverwachte oplossing
De oplossing kwam van dichterbij dan ik had durven dromen: mijn fantastische medewerkers. Met hun jarenlange ervaring en liefde voor ProBär stelden zij voor om het bedrijf samen voort te zetten. Ik had nooit gedacht dat zij deze verantwoordelijkheid wilden én konden dragen, maar inmiddels weet ik zeker dat ProBär in de goede handen is.

ProBär blijft mijn bedrijf, maar mijn rol is veranderd. Ik blijf op de achtergrond betrokken, als klankbord en sparringpartner. Dat is wennen, maar tegelijkertijd overheerst het gevoel van trots.

Vooruitkijken
Voor mij is dit een moment van loslaten en vooruitkijken. De toekomst ligt open, en dat voelt zowel inspirerend als spannend. Stilzitten voelt onnatuurlijk, maar misschien geeft juist dat de ruimte die ik nodig heb om mijn volgende stap te ontdekken.

Als ondernemer geloof ik in bewust keuzes maken, ook als die keuzes onzekerheid met zich meebrengen. Soms moet je springen, risico’s nemen en vertrouwen hebben dat je vleugels onderweg vanzelf groeien.

Herken je dit gevoel? Sta jij ook op een kruispunt in je carrière of leven? Ik ben benieuwd naar jouw verhaal en hoe jij keuzes maakt in tijden van verandering. Laten we elkaar inspireren.

#goals #levenlangleren #verandering #ondernemen #continuverbeteren #nieuweuitdaging #loslaten

Nobody tells you that after you 'make it,' the real work begins: figuring out what the hell you were making it for.
It took me years to understand that financial success ≠ Peace of mind.

We spend our entire lives living in the future:
▪"After 10th boards, I'll relax"
▪"After college, life will be easier"
▪"After this promotion, I'll take a break"

The goalpost keeps moving. And we keep chasing, and treating life like a destination. Work hard for a year, then vacation. Grind for 5 years, then enjoy. But that "then" never really comes.

There's a book, 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗼𝗽 𝗙𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗯𝘆 𝗕𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗶𝗲 𝗪𝗮𝗿𝗲, in which a nurse interviewed patients in their final days. Not ONE person said "I wish I'd made more money”.

Instead, the regrets were:

Wishing they’d lived a life true to themselves
Wishing they hadn’t worked so hard
Wishing they’d stayed in touch with friends
Wishing they’d let themselves be happier

And that changed my perspective so much.

Now I'm learning to set goals that actually matter - and enjoy the journey while getting there. Not postponing life for some future milestone.

Because this IS life happening. Right now, while you’re reading this.

So take this post as a reminder to do that one thing you’ve been sitting on for long!

#success #work #life #goals

post_text: Day 3 of our NSS Annual Camp was definitely one of the most satisfying days for us, as it gave us a chance to serve the community directly and learn the actual meaning of empathy. We began the day by conducting a medical camp for the villagers. Interacting with the villagers and assisting them in the process made us understand the actual significance of such camps, especially in villages where people do not have regular access to healthcare. Next, we conducted a cloth donation campaign, where we distributed clothes to those who needed them. This activity was a humbling experience, as it made us realize that even the smallest acts of kindness can bring smiles to many faces. Later in the day, the mood changed to one of happiness and excitement as we played games. Such events did not just rejuvenate us but also helped us bond as a team. On the whole, the experiences of the day sharpened our perspective on service, empathy and teamwork.

New Year, New Possibilities! ✨

Stepping into 2025, I’m filled with excitement for the growth, connections, and creativity this new year will bring. There’s something magical about a fresh start—it’s a chance to reevaluate goals, refresh our brand, and capture the moments that define us.

If you’re thinking about elevating your brand (personal or business) this year, here are a few quick tips to ensure your image reflects the best version of you:

Pose with Purpose – Consider what message you want to convey. Strong and wide stances project confidence, while relaxed postures that lean in look more approachable.
Align with Your Brand Colors – Choose outfits or backdrops that complement your brand’s color palette for a cohesive look across your website and social media.
Update Regularly – If your current photos are over three years old, it’s time for a refresh. Your photos should grow with you and reflect the direction your brand is headed.
Let 2025 be the year your brand shines brighter than ever—bold, authentic, and ready to make an impact.

I can’t wait to see what we all create this year. Here’s to fresh starts and bold moves! 🚀

post_text_html:
New Year, New Possibilities! ✨

Stepping into 2025, I’m filled with excitement for the growth, connections, and creativity this new year will bring. There’s something magical about a fresh start—it’s a chance to reevaluate goals, refresh our brand, and capture the moments that define us.

If you’re thinking about elevating your brand (personal or business) this year, here are a few quick tips to ensure your image reflects the best version of you:

Pose with Purpose – Consider what message you want to convey. Strong and wide stances project confidence, while relaxed postures that lean in look more approachable.
Align with Your Brand Colors – Choose outfits or backdrops that complement your brand’s color palette for a cohesive look across your website and social media.
Update Regularly – If your current photos are over three years old, it’s time for a refresh. Your photos should grow with you and reflect the direction your brand is headed.
Let 2025 be the year your brand shines brighter than ever—bold, authentic, and ready to make an impact.

I can’t wait to see what we all create this year. Here’s to fresh starts and bold moves! 🚀

#ConfidenceInYourBrand

3. Qualität bleibt unser wichtigstes Versprechen – an unsere Kunden und an uns selbst.

Delegates at the IMO in London postponed the decision following intense U.S. diplomatic pressure and threatened retaliatory measures. Earlier in the year, many expected this to pass. What happens when your real estate strategy suddenly stops working?

In this episode of The Real Wealth Show, Kate Lynch shares how she left her Wall Street career to build a high cash-flow Airbnb portfolio in Cleveland, only to see regulations change almost overnight.

With income dropping fast, Kate was forced to make tough decisions and quickly adapt her approach.

In this conversation, Kate and Kathy Fettke discuss:

How Kate built a profitable short-term rental business and what made it work
What happened when local regulations shifted, and how it impacted her cash flow
The tough decisions she had to make and how she pivoted her investment strategy
How she transitioned into opportunity zone investing and glamping developments
Key lessons on flexibility, resilience, and adapting to changing market conditions

If you're navigating changing markets, uncertain cash flow, or shifting regulations, this episode offers real-world insight on how to adjust your strategy and keep moving forward.

What happens when your real estate strategy suddenly stops working?

In this episode of The Real Wealth Show, Kate Lynch shares how she left her Wall Street career to build a high cash-flow Airbnb portfolio in Cleveland, only to see regulations change almost overnight.

With income dropping fast, Kate was forced to make tough decisions and quickly adapt her approach.

In this conversation, Kate and Kathy Fettke discuss:

How Kate built a profitable short-term rental business and what made it work
What happened when local regulations shifted, and how it impacted her cash flow
The tough decisions she had to make and how she pivoted her investment strategy
How she transitioned into opportunity zone investing and glamping developments
Key lessons on flexibility, resilience, and adapting to changing market conditions

If you're navigating changing markets, uncertain cash flow, or shifting regulations, this episode offers real-world insight on how to adjust your strategy and keep moving forward.

post_text_html:
Brasileiros podem se filiar ou renovar sua condição de membro agora e aproveitar as condições de membro de países emergentes com a taxa reduzida (USD 100).

BENEFÍCIOS PARA MEMBROS

No coração da ASIS, há uma rede global de 34.000 membros apaixonados que, juntos, estão impulsionando os padrões e diretrizes do setor, treinamento especializado e certificações para aprimorar a segurança em todo o mundo.

Junte-se a nós e tome o seu lugar na liderança do futuro do gerenciamento de segurança.

Engajamento com impacto

Conecte-se de maneiras significativas e construa uma poderosa rede de suporte:

  • Comunidade on-line robusta somente para membros, o ASIS Connects
  • Rede mundial de mais de 240 capítulos regionais
  • Programa de mentoria e HQ de carreira projetados para profissionais de segurança global

Conheça o seu setor

Mantenha-se informado sobre as tendências de segurança e o cenário global para mitigar riscos

  • Assinatura gratuita da premiada revista Security Management da ASIS e dos boletins eletrônicos diários e semanais da Security Management
  • Acesso somente on-line gratuito à versão eletrônica de todas as normas e diretrizes (Standards e Guidelines).
  • Acesso gratuito aos relatórios de pesquisa da ASIS Foundation

Avance na sua carreira

Expanda seus conhecimentos e aumente seu perfil com valiosas ofertas de desenvolvimento profissional - desfrute de economias substanciais para os membros

  • Quatro programas distintos de certificação ASIS reconhecidos mundialmente como uma marca de excelência em gerenciamento de segurança
  • Conferências globais durante todo o ano, cúpulas de executivos e o principal evento do setor - Global Security Exchange (GSX)
  • Webinars, programas presenciais e aprendizado on-line

Compartilhe sua experiência

Molde o futuro do gerenciamento de segurança, devolvendo a profissão:

  • Voluntarie-se através de capítulos, conselhos e comitês da ASIS
  • Contribua com artigos do setor, white papers e relatórios de pesquisa
  • Compartilhe práticas recomendadas, tendências de segurança e insights de liderança em reuniões locais de capítulos, eventos regionais e GSX

Amplie suas habilidades, expanda sua rede profissional e ajude a moldar o futuro da profissão de segurança para um amanhã mais seguro - torne-se um membro da comunidade ASIS hoje.

Entre em 2020 com o pé direito. Filie-se agora!

Abraço,

Gustavo Dietz

Chairman – ASIS Chapter Rio

The competitiveness of the Basketball Africa League is increasing, but why was this an issue in the first place? Especially because most African NBA talent comes from sub-saharan countries.
#playbookafrica 

Past BAL Champions include:

2021: Zamalek (Egypt)
2022: US Monastir (TUnisia)
2023: Al AHLY (Egypt)

And this wasn’t particularly surprising because North African teams tend to have a couple of advantages:

1. North African countries historically have more established domestic basketball leagues and programs compared to sub-Saharan Africa. 
→ The more time you’ve been around, the more developed you are(generally).

Zamalek was founded in 1911 and This could translate to better infrastructure, facilities, and financial resources for professional teams.

2. North African countries like Morocco, Egypt, and Tunisia likely have a larger middle class consumer and sponsor base to support professional basketball teams financially compared to many sub-Saharan nations. 
→ The more money you have, the better talent you can buy.

*Any other reasons you can think of?*

The longevity of any league relies on competitiveness because simply put, a game isn’t interesting when you already know who is going to win.

We'll see how the league evolves but surely more investors and corporates participating in the sports industry in Sub-Saharan basketball will translate to even higher competition and an even better product on the court.

About 'Reading'

Ever crossed your mind what "reading" really means? If you are reading this, you are involuntarily doing it currently. The Oxford English Dictionary defines "read" as "to look at and comprehend the meaning of (written or printed matter) by interpreting the characters or symbols of which it is composed." Merriam-Webster suggests that "reading is to understand the meaning of written or printed words, characters, or symbols." Philosophical discussions on literacy often implicitly center on the visual decoding of symbols. 

The common thread, it seems, almost always involves the act of ‘looking at’ or ‘perusing visually’ fundamentally involving vision by the eye. For most of my life, as someone who used to effortlessly devour books and screens, this definition made perfect sense.

But then, macular degeneration began to dim that window. What was once a simple joy became a struggle, and traditional reading felt like a precious loss. Magnifiers offered brief help, but long articles or novels became impossible. I started to lose hope.

And then, a new path opened up. I discovered screen readers. At first, it was a steep learning curve, navigating interfaces purely by sound. But slowly, painstakingly, I learned. And as I did, a whole new world of information, previously inaccessible, unfurled before me. I could go through long texts again, process complex information, and engage with the written word in a way I hadn't thought possible.

In fact, this newfound access led to an incredible opportunity. I trained at v-shesh, joined them as an intern before finding my current role assistant researcher at Anyssa Venture Capital. My job now involves diving into lengthy reports, extensively surfing the internet for diverse information, and poring over countless articles. All of this is done through the incredible power of a screen reader.

So here's where my initial question about the definition of reading comes back with renewed force. By the common definitions from Oxford, Merriam-Webster, and even broader philosophical interpretations, which often emphasize "looking at" or "perusing visually," am I truly reading? Or is the prevailing definition of "read" too narrow, failing to encompass the diverse ways we now access and comprehend information?

For me, the information is processed, understood, and utilized. The meaning is comprehended. The knowledge is gained. The only difference is the sensory input - my eyes aren't doing the work- my ears and mind are. If the goal is understanding, then how we achieve it should be less important than the outcome.

#VisualImpairment #Accessibility #ScreenReader #Inclusion

You have one hour this Friday to sit across from the CEO who built a $15 billion business across 17 countries and ask him anything.

His name is Alain Bejjani, former CEO of Majid Al Futtaim. 

He took a single Dubai shopping mall and turned it into one of the largest privately held businesses in the Middle East. 

No master plan. 
Principles, applied with discipline.

He's lived the things most CEOs are navigating right now:

- Scaling beyond your own capacity
- Letting go of control
- Building something that doesn't depend on you being in every room.

On Friday, Alain is in the room inside my WCL21 CEO community. 

Not to lecture. 

To hear your challenges and share what he learned the hard way.

This session is normally closed to members. 

I'm opening two or three seats for CEOs outside the community.

Friday 5 June. 2pm UK. 
One hour. Online.

If you're a CEO and want to be in that room, comment or DM "ALAIN". 

(Picture taken during the recording of our episode of The World Class Leaders Show, which will be released in July).

post_text: Today the default is remember, but should we learn to forget? 🤔 The paradox of our age! I just analysed a must-see episode of "Delete: The Virtue of Forgetting in the Digital Age with Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger" part of Bridging the Gaps a show hosted by Dr Waseem Akhtar ( https://shorturl.at/vAprh ) and this is what I found, as part of my Research Methods assignment: ➡️ The guest and expert is Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger, a renowned academic at Oxford University and one of the most influential voices globally on issues of Information Governance with an emphasis on AI and big data. His work focuses on how technologies redefine decision-making and power in the digital age. ( https://lnkd.in/gtazWKN4 ) This expert argues that we have reversed the balance from a natural "default of forgetting" to a permanent "default of remembering" due to: - Digitization made possible to use the same storage and processing devices for all kinds of different types of information. - The storage prices have come down dramatically. (It’s 50 million times cheaper than a few decades ago.) -The global network called the Internet, through which we can access vast amounts of digital storage. ➡️ As part of my assignment in Research Methods, I chose this chapter because personally, the approach of forgetting as a virtue awakens in me an interest in analysing our behaviour as Internet users and rethinking why today we have put our lifes in the hands of technology and entrusted our memories to large companies. This may raise a fundamental question for any user of the digital world: Who has real control over our digital footprint? I think it is also important to publicise cases such as that of Stacy Snyder, a student teacher who wanted to become a teacher but thanks to a particular photo on her MySpace page labeled "drunken pirate." it was impossible. ( https://lnkd.in/gp-DYkQn ). This demonstrates a big problem in the world today, where everything can be saved and remembered, as Viktor says: As mush as you want something to be forgotten, the internet will not let it go. ➡️ My 3 Key Learnings: - The Power of Digital Traces: The persistence of data (e.g. the Stacey Snyder case) creates a risk of permanent surveillance and requires researchers to verify the temporality and context of information, not just its existence. - Risk of Self-Censorship: If we are aware that you can't delete, just mark for deletion, self-censorship is induced, limiting the quality and diversity of information shared, a crucial bias to consider in data collection. - The Methodological Solution: Expiration Tags: The strategy going forward is not cognitive adaptation, but technological innovation. We must demand tools, such as the Drop ( https://lnkd.in/gWUJg-VE ), that allowed information to have an expiry date or expiration tags, re-establishing user control over their own data.

That’s what the UK’s new FRIDGE project is proving possible. FRIDGE, led by The Alan Turing Institute with the AI Research Resource (including the Dawn and Isambard-AI supercomputers), is building a way to do sensitive data research safely at massive scale. It’s a simple but powerful idea: bring privacy and high-performance computing together instead of treating them as opposites. Here’s what makes it different: ➥ It combines the speed of supercomputers with the strict controls of secure data labs (Trusted Research Environments). ➥ It builds “private zones” inside the supercomputer so sensitive work stays locked down, but results can still be shared safely. ➥ It shares the policies, designs, and lessons openly, so others can reuse what works instead of reinventing it. This changes the old story. Privacy is no longer a barrier to research, it’s what makes large-scale, ethical AI research possible in the first place. Today the default is remember, but should we learn to forget? 🤔 The paradox of our age!

I just analysed a must-see episode of "Delete: The Virtue of Forgetting in the Digital Age with Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger" part of Bridging the Gaps a show hosted by Dr Waseem Akhtar (https://shorturl.at/vAprh) and this is what I found, as part of my Research Methods assignment:

➡️ The guest and expert is Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger, a renowned academic at Oxford University and one of the most influential voices globally on issues of Information Governance with an emphasis on AI and big data. His work focuses on how technologies redefine decision-making and power in the digital age. (https://lnkd.in/gtazWKN4)

This expert argues that we have reversed the balance from a natural "default of forgetting" to a permanent "default of remembering" due to:
- Digitization made possible to use the same storage and processing devices for all kinds of different types of information.
- The storage prices have come down dramatically. (It’s 50 million times cheaper than a few decades ago.)
-The global network called the Internet, through which we can access vast amounts of digital storage.

➡️ As part of my assignment in Research Methods, I chose this chapter because personally, the approach of forgetting as a virtue awakens in me an interest in analysing our behaviour as Internet users and rethinking why today we have put our lifes in the hands of technology and entrusted our memories to large companies. This may raise a fundamental question for any user of the digital world: Who has real control over our digital footprint?

I think it is also important to publicise cases such as that of Stacy Snyder, a student teacher who wanted to become a teacher but thanks to a particular photo on her MySpace page labeled "drunken pirate." it was impossible. (https://lnkd.in/gp-DYkQn).

This demonstrates a big problem in the world today, where everything can be saved and remembered, as Viktor says: As mush as you want something to be forgotten, the internet will not let it go.

➡️ My 3 Key Learnings:
- The Power of Digital Traces: The persistence of data (e.g. the Stacey Snyder case) creates a risk of permanent surveillance and requires researchers to verify the temporality and context of information, not just its existence.

- Risk of Self-Censorship: If we are aware that you can't delete, just mark for deletion, self-censorship is induced, limiting the quality and diversity of information shared, a crucial bias to consider in data collection.

- The Methodological Solution: Expiration Tags: The strategy going forward is not cognitive adaptation, but technological innovation. We must demand tools, such as the Drop (https://lnkd.in/gWUJg-VE), that allowed information to have an expiry date or expiration tags, re-establishing user control over their own data.

I just analysed a must-see episode of "Delete: The Virtue of Forgetting in the Digital Age with Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger" part of Bridging the Gaps a show hosted by Dr Waseem Akhtar (https://shorturl.at/vAprh) and this is what I found, as part of my Research Methods assignment: ➡️ The guest and expert is Professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger, a renowned academic at Oxford University and one of the most influential voices globally on issues of Information Governance with an emphasis on AI and big data. His work focuses on how technologies redefine decision-making and power in the digital age. (https://lnkd.in/gtazWKN4) This expert argues that we have reversed the balance from a natural "default of forgetting" to a permanent "default of remembering" due to: - Digitization made possible to use the same storage and processing devices for all kinds of different types of information. - The storage prices have come down dramatically. (It’s 50 million times cheaper than a few decades ago.) -The global network called the Internet, through which we can access vast amounts of digital storage. ➡️ As part of my assignment in Research Methods, I chose this chapter because personally, the approach of forgetting as a virtue awakens in me an interest in analysing our behaviour as Internet users and rethinking why today we have put our lifes in the hands of technology and entrusted our memories to large companies. This may raise a fundamental question for any user of the digital world: Who has real control over our digital footprint? I think it is also important to publicise cases such as that of Stacy Snyder, a student teacher who wanted to become a teacher but thanks to a particular photo on her MySpace page labeled "drunken pirate." it was impossible. (https://lnkd.in/gp-DYkQn). This demonstrates a big problem in the world today, where everything can be saved and remembered, as Viktor says: As mush as you want something to be forgotten, the internet will not let it go. ➡️ My 3 Key Learnings: - The Power of Digital Traces: The persistence of data (e.g. the Stacey Snyder case) creates a risk of permanent surveillance and requires researchers to verify the temporality and context of information, not just its existence. - Risk of Self-Censorship: If we are aware that you can't delete, just mark for deletion, self-censorship is induced, limiting the quality and diversity of information shared, a crucial bias to consider in data collection. - The Methodological Solution: Expiration Tags: The strategy going forward is not cognitive adaptation, but technological innovation. We must demand tools, such as the Drop (https://lnkd.in/gWUJg-VE), that allowed information to have an expiry date or expiration tags, re-establishing user control over their own data.

Loyalty rewards that deliver measurable impact, audited on blockchain.

Context is the real power behind every DAX formula. 7. A simple function can unlock complex business logic. 8. DAX rewards clarity more than complexity. 9. Filters are not limits; they are perspectives. 10. Time intelligence in DAX brings trends to life. 11. Good DAX makes reports faster and smarter. 12. Measures adapt, visuals react, insights grow. 13. DAX connects business questions with mathematical answers. 14. It transforms dashboards into decision-making tools. 15. Learning DAX is learning how data behaves. 16. It respects: Start date End date Granularity Period length If your report filters Jan 1–15, it returns Jan 1–15 last year. If your report filters Q2, it returns Q2 last year. Ex: Sales LY = CALCULATE( [Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]) ) Use it when your analysis requires true year-over-year comparisons with identical period shapes. 🔸 PARALLELPERIOD() — Shifts Time, Not Shape This function shifts the entire period by a fixed interval (month, quarter, year), regardless of the current filter’s shape. If your filter is Jan 1–15, shifting by -1 YEAR returns full January last year, not Jan 1–15. Ex: Sales PY = CALCULATE( [Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD('Date'[Date], -1, YEAR) ) Use it when you need structural time shifts — rolling periods, offset analysis, or custom comparisons. 🎯 When to Use Which Use SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR when the shape of the selected period matters. Use PARALLELPERIOD when the shift matters more than the shape. Two functions that look similar on the surface — SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR() and PARALLELPERIOD() — behave very differently once you understand how the engine evaluates dates. 🔹 SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR() — Preserves the Shape of the Filter Context This function returns the exact same date range, shifted one year back. It respects: Start date End date Granularity Period length If your report filters Jan 1–15, it returns Jan 1–15 last year. If your report filters Q2, it returns Q2 last year. Ex: Sales LY = CALCULATE( [Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]) ) Use it when your analysis requires true year-over-year comparisons with identical period shapes. 🔸 PARALLELPERIOD() — Shifts Time, Not Shape This function shifts the entire period by a fixed interval (month, quarter, year), regardless of the current filter’s shape. If your filter is Jan 1–15, shifting by -1 YEAR returns full January last year, not Jan 1–15. Ex: Sales PY = CALCULATE( [Total Sales], PARALLELPERIOD('Date'[Date], -1, YEAR) ) Use it when you need structural time shifts — rolling periods, offset analysis, or custom comparisons. 🎯 When to Use Which Use SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR when the shape of the selected period matters. Use PARALLELPERIOD when the shift matters more than the shape. Thoughts on DAX in Power BI

1. DAX is the language that turns raw data into real insight.

2. It teaches us how numbers think, not just how they look.

3. With DAX, calculations become dynamic, not static.

4. Every measure tells a story hidden inside the data.

5. DAX helps compare past, present, and future in one view.

6. Context is the real power behind every DAX formula.

7. A simple function can unlock complex business logic.

8. DAX rewards clarity more than complexity.

9. Filters are not limits; they are perspectives.

10. Time intelligence in DAX brings trends to life.

11. Good DAX makes reports faster and smarter.

12. Measures adapt, visuals react, insights grow.

13. DAX connects business questions with mathematical answers.

14. It transforms dashboards into decision-making tools.

15. Learning DAX is learning how data behaves.

16. One well-written measure can replace many manual steps.

17. DAX turns data models into powerful engines.

18. Precision in DAX leads to confidence in results.

19. Strong DAX skills mean stronger analytics thinking.

20. Mastering DAX is mastering the language of data.

Most media platforms are optimized for reaction.

People's Voice is being built for direction.

That difference is small on the surface and huge underneath. Reactions tell you what someone noticed after the fact. Direction tells you what an audience wants answered, investigated, explained, or created next.

For creators and reporters, that matters because attention alone is a noisy assignment desk. The loudest post is not always the most valuable signal. The most viral topic is not always where trust gets built. And the best question is often buried in a comment thread that disappears before anyone can act on it.

People's Voice turns that scattered demand into a structured market.

Audiences can vote on the questions and requests they want delivered. Free daily votes keep participation open. Paid votes add a stronger signal. When work is completed, creators or reporters, voters, the original asker, and the platform all share in the value created.

The goal is not to make media more reactive. It is to make audience demand visible enough that better editorial and creative decisions can happen earlier.

We think the next durable media companies will be built around trust, participation, and economic alignment. Not just more content. Not just faster feeds. Better signal.

People's Voice exists to help make that shift real.

If audience demand was easier to see before production began, what would your team make differently?

post_text_html:
Most media platforms are optimized for reaction.

People's Voice is being built for direction.

That difference is small on the surface and huge underneath. Reactions tell you what someone noticed after the fact. Direction tells you what an audience wants answered, investigated, explained, or created next.

For creators and reporters, that matters because attention alone is a noisy assignment desk. The loudest post is not always the most valuable signal. The most viral topic is not always where trust gets built. And the best question is often buried in a comment thread that disappears before anyone can act on it.

People's Voice turns that scattered demand into a structured market.

Audiences can vote on the questions and requests they want delivered. Free daily votes keep participation open. Paid votes add a stronger signal. When work is completed, creators or reporters, voters, the original asker, and the platform all share in the value created.

The goal is not to make media more reactive. It is to make audience demand visible enough that better editorial and creative decisions can happen earlier.

We think the next durable media companies will be built around trust, participation, and economic alignment. Not just more content. Not just faster feeds. Better signal.

People's Voice exists to help make that shift real.

If audience demand was easier to see before production began, what would your team make differently?

post_text: Stress verstehen – bevor er uns ausbremst Stress ist allgegenwärtig – und doch wissen viele nicht genau, was dabei eigentlich in Körper und Geist passiert. Dabei ist das Verständnis der Stressreaktion eine wichtige Grundlage, um ihn besser zu regulieren und langfristig gesund zu bleiben. Zunächst einmal: Stress ist keine Emotion wie Angst oder Trauer. Er ist vielmehr ein Zustand des inneren Ungleichgewichts – ein Warnsignal unseres Körpers. Wenn wir das Gefühl haben, einer Situation nicht gewachsen zu sein, aktiviert sich das Alarmsystem unseres Körpers: Der Sympathikus übernimmt. Puls und Blutdruck steigen, die Muskeln spannen sich an, der Blutzuckerspiegel erhöht sich – wir sind in Alarmbereitschaft. Diese Reaktion kann extrem hilfreich sein: Sie mobilisiert Kraftreserven und hilft uns, Höchstleistungen zu vollbringen. In der Psychologie spricht man in solchen Fällen von „Eustress“, also positivem Stress. Etwa wenn wir in einem wichtigen Meeting brillieren wollen oder uns auf eine sportliche Herausforderung vorbereiten. Die Stressreaktion unterstützt uns dabei, unser Potenzial voll auszuschöpfen. Problematisch wird es jedoch, wenn der Stress nicht nachlässt. Wenn die Erholung ausbleibt, obwohl der Körper sie dringend braucht. Dann spricht man von „Disstress“ – negativem Stress, der nicht antreibt, sondern auslaugt. In solchen Situationen wird das Hormon Cortisol ausgeschüttet. Und dieses kann langfristig schwerwiegende Auswirkungen haben: Konzentrationsprobleme, Gedächtnislücken, Schlafstörungen, ein erhöhtes Risiko für Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen oder Burnout. Stress verliert dann seine ursprüngliche Funktion als kurzfristiger Helfer – und wird zur chronischen Belastung. Achtsamkeit, bewusste Erholungsphasen und alltagstaugliche Strategien zur Stressbewältigung können dabei helfen, das Gleichgewicht wiederherzustellen – bevor Stress zur gesundheitlichen Gefahr wird. post_text: Facebook ads can be important for article posts for several reasons, helping to enhance visibility, engagement, and reach a targeted audience. Here are some key benefits: 1. Targeted Reach: Facebook allows you to define a specific target audience based on demographics, interests, behavior, and more. This targeting capability ensures that your article reaches the right people who are likely to be interested in your content. 2. Increased Visibility: With the sheer number of users on Facebook, advertising allows you to increase the visibility of your article beyond your organic reach. This is particularly important if you want to promote your content to a wider audience. 3. Engagement Opportunities: Facebook ads can encourage users to engage with your content through likes, comments, and shares. This engagement not only increases the visibility of your article but also helps to build a community around your content. 4. Analytics and Insights: Facebook provides detailed analytics and insights into the performance of your ads. This data can help you understand how well your article is resonating with the audience, allowing you to make informed decisions and optimize future campaigns. 5. Customizable Ad Formats: Facebook offers various ad formats, including carousel ads, video ads, and slideshow ads. You can choose the format that best suits your article content, making it more visually appealing and engaging. 6. Call-to-Action (CTA): You can include a call-to-action button in your Facebook ads, directing users to take a specific action such as visiting your website, signing up for a newsletter, or downloading additional content related to your article. 7. Remarketing Opportunities: Facebook allows you to retarget users who have previously engaged with your content. This is valuable for re-engaging users who may have shown interest in your articles but did not take a specific action. 8. Budget Control: You have control over your ad budget, allowing you to set a daily or lifetime budget based on your marketing goals. This flexibility is useful for businesses and individuals with varying budget constraints. In summary, Facebook ads can play a crucial role in promoting article posts by providing targeted reach, increasing visibility, encouraging engagement, and offering valuable insights into audience behavior. They are a powerful tool for content promotion in a platform where a large and diverse audience spends a significant amount of time.
